trials.name: E1900
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed AML, age 17-60, fit for intensive induction
trials.descriptor: Anthracycline dose intensification - daunorubicin 90 vs 45 mg/m2 in 7+3
trials.population: 657 patients aged 17-60 with previously untreated AML
trials.arms: Daunorubicin 90 mg/m2 vs 45 mg/m2 IV daily x 3, each with cytarabine 100 mg/m2/day CIV x 7 days; responders offered allogeneic HCT or HiDAC +/- gemtuzumab then autologous transplant
trials.results: Intention-to-treat: CR 70.6% with high-dose vs 57.3% with standard-dose daunorubicin (P<0.001); median OS 23.7 vs 15.7 months (P=0.003) at median follow-up 25.2 months.
trials.toxicity: Rates of serious adverse events were similar in the two groups.
trials.reference: Fernandez HF et al. N Engl J Med 2009;361:1249-1259
highlights: Made daunorubicin 90 mg/m2 (or at minimum 60) the standard anthracycline dose in 7+3 for younger adults, displacing 45 mg/m2.
The higher dose bought a better remission rate and longer survival without more serious toxicity - dose intensification is essentially free in a fit patient.
trials.takeaway: Use daunorubicin 90 mg/m2, not 45, with cytarabine in fit adults under 60 - higher CR rate and 8 months longer median survival.

trials.name: ALFA-0701
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed de novo CD33-positive AML, age 50-70, fit for intensive induction
trials.descriptor: Adding fractionated low-dose gemtuzumab ozogamicin to induction and consolidation
trials.population: 280 previously untreated patients aged 50-70 with de novo AML at 26 French centres
trials.arms: Standard induction and consolidation chemotherapy alone vs the same plus fractionated gemtuzumab ozogamicin 3 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 4 and 7 of induction and day 1 of each of two consolidation courses (five doses total)
trials.toxicity: Persistent thrombocytopenia more common with GO (16% vs 3%; P<0.0001), without an increase in death from toxicity.
trials.reference: Castaigne S et al. Lancet 2012;379:1508-1516
highlights: Rehabilitated gemtuzumab after its 2010 market withdrawal by showing that fractionated low doses deliver a higher cumulative dose safely - and drove the 2017 FDA re-approval.
The survival gain concentrates in favourable- and intermediate-risk cytogenetics, which is why GO is routinely added to 7+3 for core-binding-factor AML.
trials.takeaway: Fractionated GO 3 mg/m2 on days 1, 4 and 7 added to 7+3 improves EFS, RFS and OS in CD33-positive AML, at the cost of persistent thrombocytopenia.

trials.name: APL0406
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed low- to intermediate-risk acute promyelocytic leukemia (WBC <=10 x 10^9/L)
trials.descriptor: Chemotherapy-free ATRA + arsenic trioxide versus ATRA + chemotherapy
trials.population: 162 adults with newly diagnosed low-to-intermediate-risk APL; 156 evaluable for response (77 ATRA-ATO, 79 ATRA-chemotherapy)
trials.arms: ATRA + arsenic trioxide for induction and consolidation (chemotherapy-free) vs ATRA-idarubicin induction, three cycles of ATRA + chemotherapy consolidation, and low-dose chemotherapy + ATRA maintenance. Non-inferiority design, 5-point margin for 2-year EFS
trials.results: CR 77/77 (100%) with ATRA-ATO vs 75/79 (95%) with ATRA-chemotherapy (P=0.12). At median follow-up 34.4 months, 2-year EFS 97% vs 86% (95% CI for difference 2-22 points; P<0.001 for non-inferiority, P=0.02 for superiority). Overall survival also better with ATRA-ATO (P=0.02).
trials.toxicity: Less hematologic toxicity and fewer infections with ATRA-ATO, but more hepatic toxicity. QT prolongation and differentiation syndrome are recognized ATO effects, not quantified in the primary report.
trials.reference: Lo-Coco F et al. N Engl J Med 2013;369:111-121
highlights: Established a completely chemotherapy-free regimen as standard of care for non-high-risk APL, with cure rates above 95% and no anthracycline exposure.
Trades myelosuppression and infection for hepatotoxicity, QT prolongation and differentiation syndrome - a monitorable rather than life-threatening profile in most patients.
trials.takeaway: For low/intermediate-risk APL, ATRA + arsenic trioxide is non-inferior and probably superior to ATRA + chemotherapy, and spares cytotoxics entirely.

trials.name: MRC/NCRI AML15
trials.setting: Younger adults with newly diagnosed AML, consolidation phase
trials.descriptor: Multi-randomization trial; the consolidation question was cytarabine 1.5 vs 3 g/m2
trials.population: Younger AML patients, median age 49 (range 0-73); the cytarabine consolidation dose comparison included 657 patients
trials.arms: Cytarabine consolidation 3 g/m2 vs 1.5 g/m2 (n=657). Other randomizations in the same trial: DA +/- etoposide; ADE vs FLAG-Ida; MACE-MidAc vs high-dose cytarabine; a fifth course or not
trials.primary_endpoint: Not designated in the primary report; outcomes reported are remission rate, relapse, relapse-free survival and overall survival
trials.results: Cytarabine 1.5 g/m2 was equivalent to 3 g/m2 - no benefit from dose escalation (no HR or p-value published for this comparison). Outcomes were similar between MACE/MidAc and high-dose cytarabine, but cytarabine required less supportive care; MACE/MidAc was superior for high-risk patients; a fifth course provided no benefit. For FLAG-Ida x2 plus cytarabine x2, 8-year survival was 63% (intermediate risk) and 95% (favourable risk).
trials.toxicity: No toxicity difference reported between the 1.5 and 3 g/m2 cytarabine doses.
trials.reference: Burnett AK et al. J Clin Oncol 2013;31:3360-3368
highlights: The randomized evidence that intermediate-dose cytarabine (1.5 g/m2) consolidation is equivalent to high-dose (3 g/m2), underpinning the widespread use of lower-dose schedules - particularly relevant over age 60.
A factorial multi-randomization trial that also showed no benefit from a fifth chemotherapy course and defined FLAG-Ida as effective induction for younger adults.
trials.takeaway: Escalating consolidation cytarabine from 1.5 to 3 g/m2 adds nothing - the lower dose is equivalent.

trials.name: AML17 (daunorubicin dose)
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed AML or high-risk MDS, first induction, mostly age <60
trials.descriptor: daunorubicin 90 vs 60 mg/m2 in induction - the comparison E1900 never made
trials.population: 1,206 adults with untreated AML or high-risk MDS, most younger than 60, randomized within the UK NCRI AML17 trial
trials.arms: First induction course with daunorubicin 90 mg/m2 vs 60 mg/m2 on days 1, 3 and 5, each combined with cytarabine. All patients then received a second course containing daunorubicin 50 mg/m2 on days 1, 3 and 5
trials.primary_endpoint: Complete remission rate (with overall survival and 60-day mortality)
trials.results: No difference in CR: 73% (90 mg/m2) vs 75% (60 mg/m2); OR 1.07 (0.83-1.39), P=0.6 - and no subgroup showed benefit. 60-day mortality was HIGHER with 90 mg/m2: 10% vs 5%, HR 1.98 (1.30-3.02), P=0.001. No difference in 2-year OS: 59% vs 60%, HR 1.16 (0.95-1.43), P=0.15
trials.toxicity: The excess early death at 90 mg/m2 is the headline safety finding. An exploratory analysis showed a significant interaction by FLT3-ITD status, but no subgroup reached significant benefit
trials.reference: Burnett AK et al. Blood 2015;125:3878-3885
highlights: E1900 established daunorubicin 90 > 45 mg/m2, and 90 was widely adopted as standard - but 60 mg/m2 was what most centers actually used and had never been compared head to head
AML17 made that comparison and found no efficacy gain from 90 over 60, with double the 60-day mortality
Read the two trials together: the lesson is that 45 mg/m2 is too low, not that 90 is best. 60 mg/m2 is the modern standard dose in 7+3
trials.takeaway: Daunorubicin 90 mg/m2 offers no remission or survival advantage over 60 mg/m2 and doubles 60-day mortality - 60 mg/m2 is the standard anthracycline dose in 7+3.

trials.name: RATIFY (CALGB 10603)
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed FLT3-mutated AML, age 18-59, fit for intensive induction
trials.descriptor: Adding midostaurin to 7+3 induction, consolidation and maintenance
trials.population: 717 FLT3-mutated patients aged 18-59 with newly diagnosed non-APL AML (ITD-high 214, ITD-low 341, TKD 162), screened from 3277; 68.6% normal karyotype
trials.arms: Midostaurin 50 mg PO BID days 8-21 vs placebo, each added to daunorubicin 60 mg/m2 days 1-3 + cytarabine 200 mg/m2 CIV days 1-7; then 4 cycles HiDAC 3000 mg/m2 q12h days 1, 3, 5; then 12 cycles maintenance
trials.results: Median OS 74.7 months (95% CI 31.5-NR) vs 25.6 months (95% CI 18.6-42.9); HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.63-0.96), one-sided P=0.009. 4-year OS 51.4% vs 44.3%. Median EFS 8.2 vs 3.0 months, HR 0.78 (0.66-0.93), P=0.002. CR 58.9% vs 53.5% (P=0.15). Benefit consistent across ITD-high, ITD-low and TKD and in the transplant-censored analysis; 57.0% underwent transplant.
trials.toxicity: Similar overall severe adverse events; grade 3-5 rash higher with midostaurin (14.1% vs 7.6%, P=0.008) and anemia (92.7% vs 87.8%, P=0.03).
trials.reference: Stone RM et al. N Engl J Med 2017;377:454-464
highlights: The first targeted agent to improve survival when added to 7+3, and the trial that made rapid FLT3 testing at diagnosis mandatory - the inhibitor starts on day 8.
Benefit held across ITD-high, ITD-low and TKD, so midostaurin is given for any activating FLT3 mutation, not ITD alone.
trials.takeaway: Add midostaurin to 7+3 and consolidation for any FLT3-mutated AML in a fit younger adult - 22% lower risk of death.

trials.name: CPX-351 (Study 301)
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed high-risk or secondary AML, age 60-75, fit for intensive induction
trials.descriptor: Liposomal cytarabine-daunorubicin (5:1 fixed ratio) versus conventional 7+3
trials.population: 309 patients age 60-75 with newly diagnosed high-risk or secondary AML
trials.arms: CPX-351 (dual-drug liposomal cytarabine + daunorubicin, 5:1 molar ratio) vs conventional 7+3; one to two induction cycles followed by similar consolidation
trials.results: Median OS 9.56 vs 5.95 months; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.52-0.90), one-sided P=.003. Overall remission rate 47.7% vs 33.3% (two-sided P=.016). Improvements seen across age groups and AML subtypes. Early mortality: day 30 5.9% vs 10.6% (P=.149); day 60 13.7% vs 21.2% (P=.097).
trials.toxicity: Non-hematologic adverse event rates comparable between arms, but prolonged time to neutrophil and platelet recovery with CPX-351 and a longer treatment phase.
trials.reference: Lancet JE et al. J Clin Oncol 2018;36:2684-2692
highlights: The trial that established CPX-351 for secondary and therapy-related AML in older adults, and the basis for its FDA approval.

Important caveat: the comparator was 7+3, not venetoclax + azacitidine. Real-world survival is comparable to ven/aza, so the niche has narrowed to the fitter older adult (~60-75) with secondary or therapy-related AML who is a transplant candidate.
trials.takeaway: CPX-351 beat 7+3 on survival in older adults with secondary or high-risk AML (9.56 vs 5.95 months), but it was never compared with venetoclax + azacitidine.

trials.name: ADMIRAL
trials.descriptor: Single-agent gilteritinib versus investigator-choice salvage chemotherapy
trials.population: 371 eligible adults with relapsed or refractory FLT3-mutated AML
trials.arms: Gilteritinib 120 mg PO daily (n=247) vs salvage chemotherapy (n=124), randomized 2:1
trials.primary_endpoint: Dual: overall survival, and complete remission with full or partial hematologic recovery (CR/CRh)
trials.results: Median OS 9.3 vs 5.6 months; HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.49-0.83), P<0.001. CR/CRh 34.0% vs 15.3% (difference 18.6 points, 95% CI 9.8-27.4); CR 21.1% vs 10.5%. Median EFS 2.8 vs 0.7 months; HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.58-1.09).
trials.toxicity: Adjusted for therapy duration, grade >=3 and serious adverse events were less frequent with gilteritinib. Most common grade >=3 with gilteritinib: febrile neutropenia 45.9%, anemia 40.7%, thrombocytopenia 22.8%. Differentiation syndrome and QT prolongation are class effects.
trials.reference: Perl AE et al. N Engl J Med 2019;381:1728-1740
highlights: Made single-agent gilteritinib the standard salvage for relapsed/refractory FLT3-mutated AML, beating intensive chemotherapy on survival with less toxicity.
An oral, better-tolerated bridge to allogeneic transplant - the higher CR/CRh rate translates into more patients actually reaching transplant.
trials.takeaway: In relapsed/refractory FLT3-mutated AML, oral gilteritinib beats salvage chemotherapy on survival (9.3 vs 5.6 months) with fewer severe toxicities.

trials.name: QUAZAR AML-001
trials.setting: AML in first complete remission after intensive induction, age 55+, not a transplant candidate
trials.descriptor: Oral azacitidine (CC-486) maintenance versus placebo in CR1
trials.population: 472 patients aged >=55 in complete remission with or without count recovery after intensive chemotherapy, not candidates for stem-cell transplantation; median age 68
trials.arms: CC-486 (oral azacitidine, NOT bioequivalent to injectable azacitidine) 300 mg PO daily for 14 days of each 28-day cycle (n=238) vs placebo (n=234)
trials.results: Median OS from randomization 24.7 vs 14.8 months (P<0.001; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.55-0.86). Median relapse-free survival 10.2 vs 4.8 months (P<0.001). Benefit across most baseline subgroups; health-related quality of life preserved.
trials.toxicity: Most common events grade 1-2 gastrointestinal (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea). Grade 3-4 neutropenia 41% vs 24%; thrombocytopenia 22% vs 21%.
trials.reference: Wei AH et al. N Engl J Med 2020;383:2526-2537
highlights: Created a maintenance standard for older AML patients in CR1 who cannot proceed to transplant - the first maintenance strategy to prolong overall survival in this setting.
CC-486 is a distinct oral formulation and is NOT interchangeable with injectable azacitidine; 300 mg for 14 days per cycle is the tested schedule.
trials.takeaway: Oral azacitidine 300 mg for 14 days per cycle as CR1 maintenance adds about 10 months of median overall survival in older AML patients who are not transplant candidates.

trials.name: VIALE-A
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed AML ineligible for intensive induction (age 75+ or significant comorbidity)
trials.descriptor: Adding venetoclax to azacitidine in unfit newly diagnosed AML
trials.population: 431 previously untreated patients ineligible for standard induction because of coexisting conditions, age >=75, or both; median age 76
trials.arms: Azacitidine 75 mg/m2 SC or IV days 1-7 of each 28-day cycle plus venetoclax (target 400 mg) PO daily (n=286) or placebo (n=145)
trials.results: At median follow-up 20.5 months, median OS 14.7 vs 9.6 months; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.52-0.85), P<0.001. CR 36.7% vs 17.9% (P<0.001); composite CR 66.4% vs 28.3% (P<0.001).
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 febrile neutropenia 42% vs 19%; thrombocytopenia 45% vs 38%; neutropenia 42% vs 28%; any-grade infection 85% vs 67%; serious adverse events 83% vs 73%.
trials.reference: DiNardo CD et al. N Engl J Med 2020;383:617-629
highlights: Redefined frontline therapy for AML unfit for induction, roughly doubling the CR rate and adding 5 months of median survival over a hypomethylating agent alone.
The cost is real myelosuppression - febrile neutropenia more than doubled - so cycle-1 marrow assessment, venetoclax duration truncation and azole dose adjustment are part of delivering it safely.
trials.takeaway: Azacitidine + venetoclax is standard for newly diagnosed AML unfit for intensive chemotherapy: median OS 14.7 vs 9.6 months.

trials.name: AGILE
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed IDH1-mutated AML, ineligible for intensive induction
trials.descriptor: Adding the IDH1 inhibitor ivosidenib to azacitidine
trials.population: 146 patients with newly diagnosed IDH1-mutated AML ineligible for intensive induction (72 ivosidenib-azacitidine, 74 placebo-azacitidine)
trials.arms: Ivosidenib 500 mg PO daily + azacitidine 75 mg/m2 for 7 days of each 28-day cycle vs placebo + the same azacitidine
trials.primary_endpoint: Event-free survival (treatment failure, relapse or death)
trials.results: At median follow-up 12.4 months, HR for treatment failure, relapse or death 0.33 (95% CI 0.16-0.69), P=0.002; event-free at 12 months 37% vs 12%. Median OS 24.0 vs 7.9 months; HR 0.44 (95% CI 0.27-0.73), P=0.001.
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 febrile neutropenia 28% vs 34%, neutropenia 27% vs 16%; any-grade bleeding 41% vs 29%; infection 28% vs 49%. Differentiation syndrome any grade 14% vs 8%.
trials.reference: Montesinos P et al. N Engl J Med 2022;386:1519-1531
highlights: Established ivosidenib + azacitidine as a frontline option for IDH1-mutated AML unfit for induction, with a median OS of 24 months - the longest reported in this population.
Interpret the EFS with care: failure to achieve CR by week 24 counted as an event dated back to randomization, which inflates early curve separation. The OS result is the more robust finding.
trials.takeaway: In IDH1-mutant AML unfit for induction, ivosidenib + azacitidine triples median overall survival (24.0 vs 7.9 months); watch for differentiation syndrome.

trials.name: QuANTUM-First
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD-positive AML, age 18-75, fit for intensive induction
trials.descriptor: Adding the type II FLT3 inhibitor quizartinib to 7+3, consolidation and up to 3 years of continuation
trials.population: 539 adults aged 18-75 with newly diagnosed FLT3-ITD-positive AML at 193 sites in 26 countries; median age 56
trials.arms: Quizartinib 40 mg PO daily from day 8 for 14 days vs placebo, added to standard 7+3; responders received HiDAC consolidation with quizartinib or placebo, allogeneic HCT, or both, then single-agent continuation up to 3 years
trials.results: At median follow-up 39.2 months, median OS 31.9 months (95% CI 21.0-NE) vs 15.1 months (95% CI 13.2-26.2); HR 0.78 (95% CI 0.62-0.98), P=0.032.
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 adverse events 92% vs 90%; most common febrile neutropenia, hypokalaemia and pneumonia in both arms, plus neutropenia with quizartinib. Known QT-prolongation risk drives the REMS requirement.
trials.reference: Erba HP et al. Lancet 2023;401:1571-1583
highlights: A second FLT3 inhibitor option for newly diagnosed disease, doubling median overall survival versus chemotherapy alone in FLT3-ITD AML.
Unlike RATIFY it enrolled up to age 75 and included up to 3 years of continuation - but it applies only to ITD-positive disease, since quizartinib has no activity against TKD mutations.
trials.takeaway: Quizartinib added to 7+3 prolongs survival in FLT3-ITD AML up to age 75, with QT monitoring as the practical cost.

trials.name: SWOG S1203
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed AML in younger adults, fit for intensive induction
trials.descriptor: Standard 7+3 versus idarubicin/high-dose cytarabine, with or without vorinostat
trials.population: 738 eligible younger adults with newly diagnosed AML registered 2013-2015; APL and CML blast phase excluded
trials.arms: DA (7+3): daunorubicin 90 mg/m2 + cytarabine 100 mg/m2/day CIV (n=261). IA: idarubicin 12 mg/m2 x3 + cytarabine 1500 mg/m2/day CIV x4 days (n=261). IA+V: vorinostat 500 mg PO TID days 1-3 then IA (n=216; stopped early for futility)
trials.primary_endpoint: Event-free survival (DA vs IA or IA+V); overall survival was secondary
trials.results: No arm beat 7+3. Overall response 77.5% (CR 62.5%, CRi 15.0%) with no difference between arms. At median follow-up 33 months, no significant EFS difference (all P>0.38): 2-year EFS 36% / 41% / 37%. No significant OS difference (all P>0.29): 2-year OS 57% / 59% / 57%. In favourable cytogenetics DA was significantly BETTER than IA (P=0.008) and IA+V (P=0.006). IA+V closed for futility at the second interim analysis; IA later crossed a futility boundary.
trials.toxicity: More toxicity in the experimental arms, driven by IA+V: grade 3 diarrhea 6%/8%/18% (P<0.001); grade 3 typhlitis 3%/5%/10% (P=0.002); grade 4 sepsis 6%/7%/13% (P=0.002); grade 5 sepsis 0%/3%/3% (P=0.03).
trials.reference: Garcia-Manero G et al. Leukemia 2024;38:58-66
highlights: A negative trial that settled the question: high-dose cytarabine induction, with or without vorinostat, does not improve remission, EFS or OS over standard 7+3, and adds gastrointestinal and infectious toxicity.
In favourable-risk cytogenetics the experimental regimens were actually worse than 7+3, reinforcing DA plus gemtuzumab as the right backbone for core-binding-factor AML.
trials.takeaway: 7+3 remains the standard induction for fit younger adults - idarubicin/high-dose cytarabine, with or without vorinostat, offered no benefit and more toxicity.

trials.name: PARADIGM
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed AML, fit for and eligible for intensive induction
trials.descriptor: azacitidine + venetoclax vs intensive induction chemotherapy in induction-ELIGIBLE (fit) AML
trials.population: 172 previously untreated adults with AML who were eligible for intensive induction chemotherapy. Excluded: core binding factor fusions, FLT3 mutations, NPM1 mutations (unless age >=60), t(15;17)/APL, BCR::ABL1, mixed-phenotype acute leukemia. Median age 64; 72% adverse risk by ELN 2022. Median follow-up 21.9 months
trials.arms: Azacitidine + venetoclax (n=86) vs intensive induction chemotherapy (7+3 or CPX-351) (n=86), randomized 1:1
trials.results: Median EFS 14.5 months (95% CI 10.4-24.4) with azacitidine-venetoclax vs 6.2 months (4.1-10.1) with induction chemotherapy; HR for event or death 0.57 (95% CI 0.39-0.84), P=0.002 by stratified log-rank. Overall survival was NOT significantly different (21.5 vs 18.6 months, P=0.19 as presented at ASH 2025); more patients on azacitidine-venetoclax proceeded to allogeneic transplant (P=0.009)
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 infection 28% (95% CI 19-39) with azacitidine-venetoclax vs 41% (30-52) with induction chemotherapy. Grade >=3 hemorrhage 2% (0.3-8) vs 12% (6-20). Patient-reported outcomes favored azacitidine-venetoclax: better quality of life, lower symptom burden and depression scores, less time in hospital and ICU
trials.reference: Fathi AT et al. N Engl J Med 2026;395:845-858
highlights: The first randomized comparison of HMA/venetoclax against intensive induction in patients who were FIT for 7+3 - inverting the usual framing of ven/aza as the therapy for the unfit

Population is induction-eligible but biologically unfavorable: favorable-risk genetics, FLT3 and younger NPM1-mutant patients were excluded, and 72% were ELN 2022 adverse risk. Do NOT extrapolate to a FLT3-mutated or favorable-risk patient
Phase 2 with an EFS primary endpoint. Overall survival was not significantly different, so this is a tolerability, transplant-bridging and EFS argument rather than a demonstrated survival win
Less grade >=3 infection (28% vs 41%) and hemorrhage (2% vs 12%), better quality of life, and more patients reached allogeneic transplant
trials.takeaway: In fit, induction-eligible AML that is not favorable-risk and not FLT3-mutated, azacitidine + venetoclax more than doubled event-free survival versus intensive induction with less infection and bleeding - though overall survival was not significantly different in this phase 2 trial.

trials.name: ABC-02
trials.setting: Locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer, first line
trials.descriptor: gemcitabine plus cisplatin vs gemcitabine alone - the backbone regimen
trials.population: 410 patients with locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer or ampullary cancer
trials.arms: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 + cisplatin 25 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 every 21 days, vs gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 alone
trials.results: Median OS 11.7 vs 8.1 months; HR 0.64 (95% CI 0.52-0.80), P<0.001. Median PFS 8.0 vs 5.0 months
trials.toxicity: More neutropenia with the doublet but no excess infection or treatment-related death; liver-function abnormalities were more frequent with gemcitabine alone
trials.reference: Valle J et al. N Engl J Med 2010;362:1273-1281
highlights: Established the frontline backbone that every subsequent biliary trial has been built on top of
Fifteen years on, gem/cis is still the chemotherapy spine - the only advance has been adding a checkpoint inhibitor to it
Note the trial pooled cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder and ampullary cancer, which is why the evidence base treats them together despite different biology
trials.takeaway: Gemcitabine plus cisplatin remains the chemotherapy backbone for advanced biliary tract cancer.

trials.name: SWOG S0809
trials.setting: Resected extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma or gallbladder cancer, adjuvant
trials.descriptor: adjuvant gemcitabine-capecitabine followed by capecitabine chemoradiation
trials.population: 79 patients with resected extrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (68%) or gallbladder cancer (32%), stage pT2-4, node-positive, or margin-positive
trials.arms: Single-arm: gemcitabine + capecitabine for 4 cycles, then capecitabine concurrent with radiation (45 Gy to regional nodes, 54-59.4 Gy to the tumor bed)
trials.results: Two-year OS 65% overall (95% CI 53-74); 67% for R0 and 60% for R1 resections. Median OS 35 months. Local, distant and combined relapse in 14, 24 and 9 patients respectively
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 toxicity was mostly hematologic; the regimen was deliverable in this population
trials.reference: Ben-Josef E et al. J Clin Oncol 2015;33:2617-2622
highlights: Single-arm, so it provides a benchmark rather than proof of benefit - there is no randomized comparator
The R0 and R1 outcomes were nearly identical, which is the most interesting finding and the reason chemoradiation is considered for margin-positive disease
Applies to extrahepatic and gallbladder disease only - intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma was not studied
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant gemcitabine-capecitabine followed by capecitabine chemoradiation is a reasonable option for node-positive or margin-positive extrahepatic and gallbladder cancer, on single-arm benchmark data.

trials.name: BILCAP
trials.descriptor: adjuvant capecitabine after curative-intent resection
trials.population: 447 patients with completely resected cholangiocarcinoma or gallbladder cancer, ECOG 0-2
trials.arms: Capecitabine 1250 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 of a 21-day cycle for 8 cycles, vs observation
trials.primary_endpoint: Overall survival in the intention-to-treat population
trials.results: ITT median OS 51.1 vs 36.4 months; adjusted HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.63-1.04), P=0.097 - the primary endpoint was NOT met. Per-protocol: 53 vs 36 months, HR 0.75 (0.58-0.97), P=0.028. A prespecified sensitivity analysis adjusting for nodal status, grade and sex gave HR 0.71 (0.55-0.92), P=0.010. ITT relapse-free survival 24.4 vs 17.5 months
trials.toxicity: Grade 3 hand-foot syndrome in about 20%; diarrhea and fatigue were the other common toxicities
trials.reference: Primrose JN et al. Lancet Oncol 2019;20:663-673
highlights: The standard of care in adjuvant biliary cancer rests on a trial that did not meet its primary endpoint - worth knowing before defending it on rounds
Practice changed on the per-protocol and prespecified sensitivity analyses, both of which were positive and internally consistent
ACTICCA-1 (gem/cis vs capecitabine) has completed accrual and may finally settle the question
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant capecitabine for 6 months is the default after resection of biliary tract cancer, on the strength of secondary analyses of a formally negative trial.

trials.name: ClarIDHy
trials.setting: Previously treated advanced cholangiocarcinoma with IDH1 mutation
trials.descriptor: ivosidenib vs placebo in IDH1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma
trials.population: 185 patients with unresectable or metastatic IDH1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma who had progressed on 1-2 prior regimens, randomized 2:1, crossover permitted at progression
trials.arms: Ivosidenib 500 mg orally daily vs placebo
trials.results: Median PFS 2.7 vs 1.4 months; HR 0.37 (95% CI 0.25-0.54), P<0.0001. Final OS 10.3 vs 7.5 months, HR 0.79, one-sided P=0.09 - not significant, but 70.5% of placebo patients crossed over. Adjusting for crossover gave placebo OS 5.1 months and HR 0.49 (0.34-0.70), P<0.0001
trials.toxicity: Generally well tolerated: fatigue, nausea, ascites, diarrhea. No differentiation syndrome of the kind seen with ivosidenib in AML
trials.reference: Abou-Alfa GK et al. Lancet Oncol 2020;21:796-807; final OS Zhu AX et al. JAMA Oncol 2021;7:1669-1677
highlights: A rare randomized targeted-therapy trial in biliary cancer, and the basis for regular FDA approval in August 2021
The PFS separation is statistically emphatic but clinically modest - 2.7 versus 1.4 months; the value is in the tail and in disease control, not in the median
The OS analysis is the teaching point: 70% crossover made the unadjusted comparison uninterpretable, and crossover adjustment is what reveals the effect
trials.takeaway: Ivosidenib improves progression-free survival in IDH1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma after prior therapy, with an overall survival signal obscured by crossover.

trials.name: FIGHT-202
trials.setting: Previously treated advanced cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement
trials.descriptor: pemigatinib in FGFR2-altered cholangiocarcinoma
trials.population: 107 patients with previously treated, locally advanced or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring an FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement
trials.arms: Single-arm: pemigatinib 13.5 mg orally once daily, 2 weeks on / 1 week off, in 21-day cycles
trials.results: ORR 35.5% at primary analysis. Final analysis at 45.4 months of follow-up: ORR 37.0%, median duration of response 9.1 months, median PFS 7.0 months, median OS 17.5 months
trials.toxicity: Hyperphosphatemia in about 60% - on-target and expected. Alopecia ~50%, diarrhea, stomatitis, dry eye, nail toxicity. Serous retinopathy requires baseline and serial ophthalmologic monitoring
trials.reference: Abou-Alfa GK et al. Lancet Oncol 2020;21:671-684; final analysis Vogel A et al. ESMO Open 2024;9:103488
highlights: The first targeted therapy approved in cholangiocarcinoma, on accelerated approval in April 2020 - opened the molecular era in this disease
Only fusions and rearrangements respond; FGFR2 point mutations do not qualify for the label
FIGHT-302 later moved pemigatinib into the first line on PFS but showed no overall survival gain, and the 1L indication is not approved
trials.takeaway: Pemigatinib produces responses in about a third of patients with FGFR2 fusion-positive cholangiocarcinoma after prior therapy.

trials.name: ROAR (biliary cohort)
trials.setting: Previously treated BRAF V600E-mutant biliary tract cancer
trials.descriptor: dabrafenib plus trametinib in BRAF V600E-mutant biliary cancer
trials.population: 43 patients with BRAF V600E-mutant biliary tract cancer who had received prior systemic therapy, within a basket trial of rare BRAF V600E-mutant cancers
trials.arms: Single-arm: dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily + trametinib 2 mg once daily
trials.results: ORR 51% by investigator and 47% by independent review at interim. Final analysis: ORR 53% investigator / 47% independent, median duration of response 8.9 months, median PFS 9.0 months, median OS 13.5 months
trials.toxicity: Pyrexia is the characteristic combination toxicity and the usual reason for dose interruption; also rash, fatigue, nausea
trials.reference: Subbiah V et al. Lancet Oncol 2020;21:1234-1243; final Subbiah V et al. Nat Med 2023
highlights: Supported the tumor-agnostic FDA accelerated approval of dabrafenib plus trametinib for BRAF V600E solid tumors in June 2022 - biliary cancer qualifies, colorectal is excluded
BRAF V600E is found in about 3% of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma and is essentially absent from extrahepatic and gallbladder disease
Response rates near 50% in a chemotherapy-refractory population are among the best seen in biliary cancer - worth testing for despite the low frequency
trials.takeaway: Dabrafenib plus trametinib produces responses in roughly half of BRAF V600E-mutant biliary cancers, via a tumor-agnostic approval.

trials.name: ABC-06
trials.setting: Advanced biliary tract cancer progressing on gemcitabine-cisplatin
trials.descriptor: FOLFOX as second-line therapy after platinum failure
trials.population: 162 patients with locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer that had progressed on first-line gemcitabine plus cisplatin
trials.arms: Modified FOLFOX (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2 day 1 + 5-FU 1200 mg/m2/day over 46-48 hours) every 14 days plus active symptom control, vs active symptom control alone
trials.results: Median OS 6.2 vs 5.3 months; adjusted HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.50-0.97), P=0.031. The median gain is under a month - the honest figures are the survival rates: 6-month OS 50.6% vs 35.5% and 12-month OS 25.9% vs 11.4%
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-5 adverse events 69% vs 52%, chiefly neutropenia, fatigue and infection
trials.reference: Lamarca A et al. Lancet Oncol 2021;22:690-701
highlights: The only randomized evidence for second-line chemotherapy in biliary cancer, and it is a small, open-label trial against best supportive care
A median gain of 0.9 months is easy to dismiss; the doubling of 12-month survival is the number worth quoting to a patient
Molecular profiling should have happened before this point - a targetable alteration beats FOLFOX in almost every case
trials.takeaway: FOLFOX is the default second-line chemotherapy after gem/cis, but the benefit is modest and targeted therapy should be excluded first.

trials.name: TOPAZ-1
trials.setting: Previously untreated advanced biliary tract cancer
trials.descriptor: adding durvalumab to gemcitabine-cisplatin in the first line
trials.population: 685 patients with unresectable, locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic biliary tract cancer and no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease
trials.arms: Durvalumab 1500 mg or placebo on day 1 with gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 + cisplatin 25 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8, every 21 days for up to 8 cycles, then durvalumab or placebo every 4 weeks
trials.results: Median OS 12.8 vs 11.5 months; HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.66-0.97), P=0.021. The more striking number is the tail: 24-month OS 24.9% vs 10.4%. PFS HR 0.75; ORR 26.7% vs 18.7%
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 adverse events were similar between arms. Immune-mediated events occurred in 12.7% vs 4.7%
trials.reference: Oh DY et al. NEJM Evid 2022;1:EVIDoa2200015
highlights: First trial to improve survival over gem/cis alone, and the basis for regular FDA approval in September 2022
The median gain is only about 1.3 months, but the doubling of 24-month survival suggests a subset with durable benefit
No validated predictive biomarker - PD-L1 did not select for benefit, so everyone gets it
trials.takeaway: Adding durvalumab to gemcitabine-cisplatin improves survival in advanced biliary tract cancer, with the benefit concentrated in a long-surviving minority.

trials.name: ASCOT (JCOG1202)
trials.setting: Resected biliary tract cancer, adjuvant, Japan
trials.descriptor: adjuvant S-1 after curative resection
trials.population: 440 Japanese patients with resected biliary tract cancer
trials.arms: Adjuvant S-1 vs observation
trials.results: 3-year OS 77.1% vs 67.6%; HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.51-0.94), one-sided P=0.008. But 3-year relapse-free survival 62.4% vs 50.9%, HR 0.80, P=0.088 - not significant
trials.toxicity: Consistent with the known S-1 profile: myelosuppression, diarrhea, mucositis, biliary infection
trials.reference: Nakachi K et al. Lancet 2023;401:195-203
highlights: Positive for overall survival where BILCAP formally was not - but the RFS result did not reach significance, an unusual and somewhat puzzling pattern
S-1 is not available in the United States, so this changes practice in Asia only
Pharmacogenomic differences in S-1 tolerance between Japanese and Western populations limit extrapolation regardless of availability
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant S-1 improves overall survival after resection of biliary tract cancer in Japan, but the drug is unavailable in the US.

trials.name: FOENIX-CCA2
trials.setting: Previously treated intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement
trials.descriptor: futibatinib, an irreversible covalent FGFR inhibitor, in FGFR2-altered intrahepatic disease
trials.population: 103 patients with unresectable or metastatic intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring an FGFR2 fusion or other rearrangement, with disease progression after one or more prior lines
trials.arms: Single-arm: futibatinib 20 mg orally once daily, continuous
trials.primary_endpoint: Objective response rate by independent central review
trials.results: ORR 42%, median duration of response 9.7 months, median PFS 9.0 months, median OS 21.7 months
trials.toxicity: Hyperphosphatemia in roughly 85% - higher than with the reversible inhibitors. Nail toxicity and onycholysis ~47%, alopecia 33%, dry mouth, diarrhea. Retinal pigment epithelial detachment in 7.8%
trials.reference: Goyal L et al. N Engl J Med 2023;388:228-239
highlights: Covalent irreversible binding gives activity against some acquired FGFR2 kinase-domain resistance mutations that defeat the reversible inhibitors
Accelerated approval September 2022, and note the label is narrower than pemigatinib's - intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma only
Hyperphosphatemia is near-universal and is a pharmacodynamic marker of target engagement rather than a reason to stop
trials.takeaway: Futibatinib produces responses in about 42% of FGFR2-altered intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, with near-universal hyperphosphatemia.

trials.name: HERIZON-BTC-01
trials.setting: Previously treated HER2-amplified biliary tract cancer
trials.descriptor: zanidatamab, a HER2-targeted bispecific antibody, in HER2-amplified biliary cancer
trials.population: 87 patients with unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic HER2-amplified biliary tract cancer who had progressed after gemcitabine-containing therapy. Cohort 1 was HER2 IHC 2+/3+ (n=80); cohort 2 was IHC 0/1+ (n=7)
trials.arms: Single-arm: zanidatamab 20 mg/kg intravenously every 2 weeks
trials.primary_endpoint: Confirmed objective response rate by independent central review
trials.results: Cohort 1 ORR 41.3%. In the HER2 IHC 3+ subgroup (n=62) - the population in the FDA label - ORR was 52% with median duration of response 14.9 months. Final analysis: cohort 1 median PFS 5.5 months, median OS 15.5 months; IHC 3+ median OS 18.1 months
trials.toxicity: Mostly infusion-related reactions and diarrhea; a small number of patients had reduced ejection fraction, so cardiac monitoring applies as with other HER2 agents
trials.reference: Harding JJ et al. Lancet Oncol 2023;24:772-782; final analysis Pant S et al. JAMA Oncol 2026;12:106-109
highlights: The only biliary-specific HER2 approval - accelerated approval November 2024, restricted to IHC 3+, second line and beyond
HER2 is a gallbladder and extrahepatic disease: roughly 11-14% of gallbladder cancers versus about 4% of intrahepatic, so the anatomic site predicts whether this is worth chasing
Trastuzumab deruxtecan can also be used here through the tumor-agnostic IHC 3+ approval, but interstitial lung disease reached 17% in the biliary cohort
trials.takeaway: Zanidatamab produces responses in about half of HER2 IHC 3+ biliary cancers and is the only biliary-specific HER2 approval.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-966
trials.setting: Previously untreated advanced biliary tract cancer
trials.descriptor: adding pembrolizumab to gemcitabine-cisplatin in the first line
trials.population: 1,069 patients with previously untreated, unresectable, locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer
trials.arms: Pembrolizumab 200 mg or placebo on day 1 with gemcitabine + cisplatin, every 21 days. Cisplatin was capped at 8 cycles; gemcitabine could continue
trials.results: Median OS 12.7 vs 10.9 months; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.72-0.95), one-sided P=0.0034
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events 70% vs 69% - essentially identical, with the difference confined to immune-mediated events
trials.reference: Kelley RK et al. Lancet 2023;401:1853-1865
highlights: Confirms the TOPAZ-1 result with a different checkpoint inhibitor in more than twice the patients - regular FDA approval October 2023
HR 0.83 versus TOPAZ-1's 0.80, with nearly identical median gains: the two regimens are effectively interchangeable
As with TOPAZ-1, PD-L1 did not identify who benefits, so the choice between durvalumab and pembrolizumab comes down to logistics and access
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab added to gemcitabine-cisplatin improves survival by a margin indistinguishable from durvalumab - either is a reasonable frontline standard.

trials.name: SWOG S1815
trials.setting: Newly diagnosed advanced biliary tract cancer
trials.descriptor: adding nab-paclitaxel to gemcitabine-cisplatin - a negative trial
trials.population: 441 analyzable patients with newly diagnosed advanced biliary tract cancer, randomized 2:1
trials.arms: Gemcitabine + cisplatin + nab-paclitaxel (GAP) vs gemcitabine + cisplatin
trials.results: Median OS 14.0 vs 13.6 months; HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.72-1.14), P=0.41 - the primary endpoint was NOT met. PFS 7.5 vs 6.3 months, HR 0.89, P=0.32. ORR was higher with the triplet (31% vs 21%, P=0.04)
trials.toxicity: More toxicity with the triplet: dose modification required in 88% vs 78%
trials.reference: Shroff RT et al. J Clin Oncol 2025;43:536-544
highlights: A clean demonstration that a higher response rate does not translate into longer survival - responses rose by 10 points while OS moved not at all
Kills the triplet as a standard regimen, which a promising single-arm phase 2 had made attractive
Exploratory subgroups hinted at a PFS effect in gallbladder cancer, but there was no OS interaction - do not practice off unplanned subsets of a negative trial
trials.takeaway: Adding nab-paclitaxel to gemcitabine-cisplatin improves response rate but not survival, and is not a standard regimen.

trials.name: ReFocus
trials.setting: Previously treated cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement, FGFR-inhibitor-naive
trials.descriptor: lirafugratinib, an FGFR2-selective covalent inhibitor designed to spare FGFR1
trials.population: 116 patients with unresectable or metastatic cholangiocarcinoma harboring a confirmed FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement, naive to prior FGFR inhibitors, progressing after at least one prior systemic regimen
trials.arms: Single-arm: lirafugratinib 70 mg orally once daily
trials.results: ORR 46%, median duration of response 11.8 months. Reported median PFS ~11.3 months and median OS ~22.8 months
trials.toxicity: The point of the molecule: because it spares FGFR1, hyperphosphatemia occurred in only about 21%, against roughly 60% with pemigatinib and 85% with futibatinib
trials.reference: FDA approval 23 September 2026 (Lyrfigtu); ReFocus trial, presented data - no peer-reviewed primary publication yet
highlights: FDA-approved 23 September 2026 for previously treated FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement cholangiocarcinoma
Highest reported response rate among the FGFR inhibitors in this setting, with markedly less hyperphosphatemia - selectivity for FGFR2 over FGFR1 was the design goal and it appears to have worked

Caveat worth carrying: the pivotal data are presented in abstract form; there is no peer-reviewed primary publication yet, and the molecule paper (Cancer Discov 2023, cited here) is preclinical and early-phase
trials.takeaway: Lirafugratinib is the newest and most selective FGFR2 inhibitor for cholangiocarcinoma, with a higher response rate and far less hyperphosphatemia than its predecessors.

trials.name: NSABP B-24
trials.descriptor: tamoxifen after lumpectomy and radiation for DCIS
trials.population: DCIS treated with lumpectomy + whole-breast radiation (positive margins allowed)
trials.arms: Tamoxifen 20 mg/day × 5 years vs placebo
trials.results: Breast-cancer events at 5 yr 8.2% vs 13.4% (p=0.0009); cumulative invasive events 4.1% at 5 yr with tamoxifen (2.1% ipsilateral, 1.8% contralateral); benefit seen even with involved margins; later analysis showed the benefit is confined to ER-positive DCIS (Allred, JCO 2012)
trials.toxicity: Endometrial cancer, VTE, hot flashes
trials.reference: Fisher B et al. Lancet 1999;353:1993; Allred DC et al. JCO 2012;30:1268 (ER subset)
highlights: Tamoxifen after BCS + RT for ER-positive DCIS reduces both ipsilateral and contralateral events; no survival benefit, so it is a shared decision.
Test ER on DCIS — ER-negative DCIS gains nothing.
trials.takeaway: Tamoxifen reduces ipsilateral and contralateral breast events after lumpectomy + RT for ER+ DCIS

trials.name: ACOSOG Z0011
trials.descriptor: sentinel node biopsy alone vs completion axillary dissection
trials.population: cT1–2 N0 breast cancer with 1–2 positive sentinel nodes, treated with lumpectomy + whole-breast RT
trials.arms: Sentinel lymph node dissection alone vs completion axillary lymph node dissection
trials.results: 5-yr OS 92.5% vs 91.8% (SLND alone vs ALND; HR 0.79) and 5-yr DFS 83.9% vs 82.2% — non-inferior; 10-yr update: OS 86.3% vs 83.6%, DFS 80.2% vs 78.2%, regional recurrence 1.5% vs 0.5%
trials.toxicity: Lymphedema, wound infection, paresthesia markedly lower without ALND
trials.reference: Giuliano AE et al. JAMA 2011;305:569; JAMA 2017;318:918 (10-yr)
highlights: Completion ALND is unnecessary for 1–2 positive sentinel nodes after lumpectomy with whole-breast RT — tangent fields cover the low axilla.
Does not apply to mastectomy without RT, ≥3 positive nodes, matted nodes, or node-positive after neoadjuvant therapy.
trials.takeaway: SLNB alone is non-inferior to ALND for 1–2 positive sentinel nodes with lumpectomy + RT

trials.name: BOLERO-2
trials.setting: HR+/HER2- metastatic after NSAI progression, postmenopausal
trials.descriptor: everolimus + exemestane after NSAI
trials.population: 724 postmenopausal women with HR+ ABC recurring or progressing on letrozole or anastrozole
trials.arms: Everolimus 10 mg daily + exemestane 25 mg vs placebo + exemestane (2:1)
trials.results: Interim PFS (local): 6.9 vs 2.8 mo, HR 0.43 (95% CI 0.35-0.54), P<0.001; central 10.6 vs 4.1 mo, HR 0.36. OS (Ann Oncol 2014): 31.0 vs 26.6 mo, HR 0.89 (0.73-1.10), P=0.14 - NOT significant.
trials.toxicity: Stomatitis (most common), anemia, dyspnea, hyperglycemia, fatigue, pneumonitis (3% grade 3-4).
trials.reference: Baselga J et al. N Engl J Med 2012;366:520-9 (PMID 22149876); Piccart M et al. Ann Oncol 2014;25:2357-62 (OS, PMID 25231953)
highlights: mTOR inhibition reverses endocrine resistance
PFS 6.9 vs 2.8 mo (local), HR 0.43
OS 31.0 vs 26.6 mo, HR 0.89 - NOT significant
trials.takeaway: Everolimus + exemestane improves PFS after NSAI failure but not OS, at the cost of stomatitis and pneumonitis.

trials.name: CLEOPATRA
trials.descriptor: docetaxel + trastuzumab + pertuzumab vs placebo
trials.population: HER2+ mBC, no prior chemo or biologic therapy for metastatic disease; ECOG 0-1
trials.arms: Pertuzumab + trastuzumab + docetaxel vs placebo + trastuzumab + docetaxel (double-blind, 1:1)
trials.results: Primary: median PFS 18.5 vs 12.4 mo, HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.51-0.75), P<0.001. End-of-study (median f/u ~99 mo): median OS 57.1 vs 40.8 mo, HR 0.69 (0.58-0.82); 8-yr OS 37% vs 23% (descriptive, 50 crossover patients analyzed in placebo arm).
trials.toxicity: No increase in LV systolic dysfunction; more grade >=3 febrile neutropenia and diarrhea with pertuzumab. Grade 3-4 neutropenia 49% vs 46% (end-of-study).
trials.reference: Baselga J et al. NEJM 2012;366:109; Swain SM et al. NEJM 2015;372:724; Swain SM et al. Lancet Oncol 2020;21:519 (end-of-study OS)
highlights: Established THP as 1L standard for HER2+ mBC
Median OS 57.1 vs 40.8 mo (HR 0.69)
8-yr OS 37% vs 23%; no added cardiotoxicity
trials.takeaway: Adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab + docetaxel improved PFS and gave a ~16-month OS gain, making THP the first-line standard until DESTINY-Breast09.

trials.name: NeoSphere
trials.setting: Neoadjuvant HER2+ operable, locally advanced or inflammatory
trials.descriptor: neoadjuvant pertuzumab + trastuzumab + docetaxel
trials.population: 417 treatment-naive women with operable, locally advanced or inflammatory HER2+ breast cancer
trials.arms: 4 neoadjuvant cycles: A) trastuzumab + docetaxel; B) pertuzumab + trastuzumab + docetaxel; C) pertuzumab + trastuzumab (no chemo); D) pertuzumab + docetaxel (1:1:1:1)
trials.primary_endpoint: Pathological complete response in the breast (ypT0/is)
trials.results: pCR: B 45.8% (95% CI 36.1-55.7) vs A 29.0% (20.6-38.5), P=0.0141; D 24.0%; C 16.8% (chemo-free). 5-yr (Lancet Oncol 2016, descriptive, not powered): PFS 86% B vs 81% A (HR 0.69, 0.34-1.40, NS); DFS 84% vs 81%; total pCR associated with longer PFS (85% vs 76%, HR 0.54).
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 neutropenia most common (similar in docetaxel arms); febrile neutropenia ~8-9 per docetaxel arm; adding pertuzumab did not substantially worsen tolerability; chemo-free arm C had few serious AEs.
trials.reference: Gianni L et al. Lancet Oncol 2012;13:25-32 (PMID 22153890); Gianni L et al. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:791-800 (5-yr, PMID 27179402)
highlights: pCR 45.8% vs 29.0% with dual HER2 blockade + docetaxel
Chemo-free pertuzumab + trastuzumab pCR 16.8%
5-yr PFS 86% vs 81% (HR 0.69, NS - descriptive)
trials.takeaway: Adding pertuzumab to neoadjuvant trastuzumab + docetaxel raised breast pCR from 29% to 46%, supporting accelerated approval of neoadjuvant pertuzumab.

trials.name: AMAROS (EORTC 10981-22023)
trials.setting: Axillary management, cT1-2 cN0 with positive sentinel node
trials.descriptor: axillary RT vs ALND after positive SLN
trials.population: 4806 patients with T1-2 breast cancer, no palpable nodes, randomized pre-SLNB; 1425 with positive SLN form ITT population
trials.arms: Axillary lymph node dissection (n=744) vs axillary radiotherapy (n=681)
trials.results: Median 6.1 y: 5-yr axillary recurrence 0.43% ALND vs 1.19% ART (noninferiority test underpowered, low events); 33% of ALND patients had additional positive nodes. 10-yr (JCO 2023): axillary recurrence 0.93% vs 1.82%, HR 1.71 (0.67-4.39); no difference in OS (HR 1.17, 0.89-1.52) or DFS (HR 1.19, 0.97-1.46).
trials.toxicity: Lymphedema significantly more with ALND at 1, 3 and 5 y; updated 5-yr lymphedema 24.5% ALND vs 11.9% ART (P<0.001); QoL no different; exploratory 10-yr second primary cancers 12.1% ART vs 8.3% ALND.
trials.reference: Donker M et al. Lancet Oncol 2014;15:1303-1310 (PMID 25439688); Bartels SAL et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:2159-2165 (10-yr, PMID 36383926)
highlights: 5-yr axillary recurrence 0.43% vs 1.19%; 10-yr 0.93% vs 1.82%
No OS or DFS difference at 10 y
Lymphedema ~halved: 24.5% ALND vs 11.9% ART at 5 y
trials.takeaway: For cT1-2 cN0 patients with a positive sentinel node, axillary RT gives comparable axillary control and survival to ALND with half the lymphedema.

trials.name: TEXT (+ SOFT combined analysis)
trials.setting: Adjuvant premenopausal HR+ early breast cancer
trials.descriptor: exemestane + OFS vs tamoxifen + OFS
trials.population: 4690 premenopausal women with HR+ early breast cancer (combined TEXT + SOFT exemestane-OFS vs tamoxifen-OFS comparison)
trials.arms: Exemestane + OFS vs tamoxifen + OFS for 5 y (OFS by triptorelin, oophorectomy or ovarian irradiation)
trials.results: Primary (median 68 mo): 5-yr DFS 91.1% vs 87.3%, HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.60-0.85), P<0.001; freedom from breast cancer 92.8% vs 88.8% (HR 0.66); OS NS (HR 1.14, 0.86-1.51). 12-yr update (Pagani JCO 2023, median 13 y): DFS HR 0.79 (0.70-0.90), +4.6% absolute; DRFI HR 0.83 (0.70-0.98), +1.8%; OS 90.1% vs 89.1%, HR 0.93 (0.78-1.11) - NS overall; HER2-negative OS +2.0% (HR 0.85, NS), larger in high-risk (age <35, >2 cm, grade 3). Final 15-yr (Francis Ann Oncol 2026): HER2-negative combined distant recurrence HR 0.75 (0.63-0.90), deaths HR 0.89 (0.74-1.06, NS); OS gain limited to high-risk subgroups.
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 selected AEs 30.6% vs 29.4%; exemestane-OFS more musculoskeletal symptoms, bone loss/osteoporosis, vaginal dryness; tamoxifen-OFS more thromboembolism, hot flashes.
trials.reference: Pagani O et al. N Engl J Med 2014;371:107-118 (PMID 24881463); Pagani O et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:1376-1382 (12-yr, PMID 36521078); Francis PA et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:1367-1385 (final 15-yr SOFT + TEXT, PMID 42229584)
highlights: 5-yr DFS 91.1% vs 87.3% (HR 0.72) with exemestane + OFS
12-yr DRFI HR 0.83; OS HR 0.93 - not significant overall
OS benefit limited to high-risk (young, grade 3, >2 cm, chemo-treated) patients
trials.takeaway: In premenopausal HR+ disease, exemestane + OFS durably reduces recurrence vs tamoxifen + OFS, but OS benefit is confined to high-risk subgroups.

trials.name: APT
trials.descriptor: de-escalated weekly paclitaxel + trastuzumab
trials.population: 406 treated patients with HER2+, node-negative breast cancer <=3 cm (single-arm; 67% HR+)
trials.arms: Paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 + trastuzumab weekly x12, then trastuzumab to complete 1 y (single arm)
trials.results: Primary (median 4.0 y): 3-yr IDFS 98.7% (95% CI 97.6-99.8); 12 relapses, 2 distant. Final 10-yr analysis (Lancet Oncol 2023, median 10.8 y): 10-yr IDFS 91.3% (88.3-94.4), 10-yr RFI 96.3%, 10-yr OS 94.3% (91.8-96.8), 10-yr BCSS 98.8%; only 6 distant recurrences; HER2DX risk score associated with IDFS.
trials.toxicity: Grade 3 neuropathy 3.2%; symptomatic CHF 0.5% (2 patients, LVEF normalized); significant asymptomatic LVEF decline 3.2%; 6% withdrew for protocol-specified AEs.
trials.reference: Tolaney SM et al. N Engl J Med 2015;372:134-141 (PMID 25564897); Tolaney SM et al. Lancet Oncol 2023;24:273-285 (10-yr, PMID 36858723)
highlights: 3-yr IDFS 98.7%
Only 6 distant recurrences in 406 patients at 10 y
trials.takeaway: Weekly paclitaxel x12 + 1 y trastuzumab is the standard for small (<=3 cm) node-negative HER2+ breast cancer, with 10-yr BCSS ~99%.

trials.name: PALOMA-3
trials.setting: HR+/HER2- metastatic after progression on ET, any menopausal status
trials.descriptor: palbociclib + fulvestrant after ET
trials.population: 521 women with HR+/HER2- MBC that progressed on prior ET (pre/perimenopausal received goserelin)
trials.arms: Palbociclib 125 mg d1-21 q28d + fulvestrant 500 mg vs placebo + fulvestrant (2:1; 347 vs 174)
trials.results: Interim PFS (NEJM 2015): 9.2 vs 3.8 mo, HR 0.42. Final PFS (Lancet Oncol 2016): 9.5 vs 4.6 mo, HR 0.46 (95% CI 0.36-0.59), P<0.0001. OS (NEJM 2018): 34.9 vs 28.0 mo, HR 0.81 (0.64-1.03), P=0.09 - NOT significant; endocrine-sensitive subgroup 39.7 vs 29.7 mo, HR 0.72 (0.55-0.94). Time to chemotherapy 17.6 vs 8.8 mo, HR 0.58.
trials.toxicity: Neutropenia (mostly uncomplicated), leukopenia, fatigue.
trials.reference: Turner NC et al. N Engl J Med 2015;373:209-19 (PMID 26030518); Cristofanilli M et al. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:425-39 (PMID 26947331); Turner NC et al. N Engl J Med 2018;379:1926-36 (OS, PMID 30345905)
highlights: Final PFS 9.5 vs 4.6 mo, HR 0.46
OS 34.9 vs 28.0 mo, HR 0.81 - NOT significant
OS gain in endocrine-sensitive subgroup (HR 0.72); delayed chemotherapy
trials.takeaway: Palbociclib + fulvestrant doubles PFS after ET progression, but the 6.9-month OS difference was not statistically significant.

trials.name: SOFT
trials.descriptor: ovarian suppression added to tamoxifen or exemestane, premenopausal
trials.population: Premenopausal HR+ early breast cancer (remaining premenopausal after chemo, if given)
trials.arms: Tamoxifen alone vs tamoxifen + ovarian suppression vs exemestane + ovarian suppression (× 5 years)
trials.results: Primary (5-yr): DFS 86.6% vs 84.7% (HR 0.83, NS overall); in women who had chemotherapy 82.5% vs 78.0% (HR 0.78). 8-yr update: DFS 83.2% vs 78.9% (HR 0.76), OS 93.3% vs 91.5%; exemestane + OFS 8-yr DFS 85.9%. Largest benefit in women <35 and those needing chemotherapy. Final 15-yr (Francis Ann Oncol 2026): 15-yr BCFI 78.6% E+OFS vs 75.7% T+OFS vs 72.1% T alone (T+OFS vs T HR 0.82, 0.69-0.98, P=0.03). No-chemo cohort: OFS reduced breast cancer events but DRFI and OS high regardless of arm. Prior chemo, HER2-negative (n=1257): 15-yr OS 81.0% E+OFS vs 77.1% T+OFS vs 76.8% T. Age <35 HER2-negative (n=241): 15-yr OS 82.5% vs 77.9% vs 68.1%. Meaningful OS benefit limited to high-risk premenopausal subgroups.
trials.toxicity: Menopausal symptoms, osteoporosis, depression, hypertension, sexual dysfunction with OFS
trials.reference: Francis PA et al. NEJM 2015;372:436; NEJM 2018;379:122 (8-yr, with TEXT); Francis PA et al. Final outcomes of the SOFT and TEXT phase III trials. Ann Oncol 2026;37:1367-1385 (PMID 42229584)
highlights: Add ovarian suppression for premenopausal women at high enough risk to warrant chemotherapy; tamoxifen alone remains reasonable for low-risk disease.
Exemestane + OFS gives the best DFS but not OS; toxicity and adherence limit its use.
trials.takeaway: Ovarian suppression added to tamoxifen improves DFS in higher-risk premenopausal HR+ breast cancer

trials.name: ExteNET
trials.descriptor: extended adjuvant neratinib x1 y
trials.population: 2840 women with stage 1-3 (amended to 2-3) HER2+ breast cancer who completed trastuzumab-based therapy within 2 y (amended to 1 y)
trials.arms: Neratinib 240 mg daily x1 y vs placebo (1:1, double-blind)
trials.results: Primary (2 y): iDFS 93.9% vs 91.6%, HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.50-0.91), P=0.0091. 5-yr (Lancet Oncol 2017): iDFS 90.2% vs 87.7%, HR 0.73 (0.57-0.92), P=0.0083. HR+ patients starting <=1 y after trastuzumab: 5-yr iDFS absolute gain 5.1%, HR 0.58 (0.41-0.82); 8-yr OS HR 0.79 (0.55-1.13, NS). Final OS (EJC 2023, median 8.1 y, ITT): 8-yr OS 90.1% vs 90.2%, HR 0.95 (0.75-1.21), P=0.69 - NO OS benefit.
trials.toxicity: Without diarrhea prophylaxis: grade 3 diarrhea 40% vs 2% (grade 4 <1%); grade 3 vomiting 3%, nausea 2%; no long-term toxicity signal. Antidiarrheal prophylaxis/dose escalation now standard.
trials.reference: Chan A et al. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:367-377 (PMID 26874901); Martin M et al. Lancet Oncol 2017;18:1688-1700 (5-yr, PMID 29146401); Chan A et al. Clin Breast Cancer 2021;21:80-91 (HR+ <=1 y, PMID 33183970); Holmes FA et al. Eur J Cancer 2023;184:48-59 (final OS, PMID 36898233)
highlights: 8-yr OS 90.1% vs 90.2%, HR 0.95 - no OS benefit
Grade 3 diarrhea 40% without prophylaxis; benefit greatest in HR+ starting <=1 y post-trastuzumab
trials.takeaway: One year of neratinib after trastuzumab modestly improves iDFS (mainly HR+ patients starting within 1 y) without improving overall survival, at the cost of substantial diarrhea.

trials.name: MONALEESA-2
trials.descriptor: ribociclib + letrozole 1L
trials.population: 668 postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2- recurrent or metastatic breast cancer, no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease
trials.arms: Ribociclib 600 mg d1-21 q28d + letrozole 2.5 mg daily vs placebo + letrozole (1:1)
trials.results: PFS HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.43-0.72) at interim; 18-mo PFS 63.0% vs 42.2%. Updated PFS (Ann Oncol 2018): median 25.3 vs 16.0 mo, HR 0.568 (0.457-0.704). Final OS (NEJM 2022, median f/u 6.6 y): median 63.9 vs 51.4 mo, HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.63-0.93), P=0.008 - significant.
trials.toxicity: Myelosuppression (neutropenia most common grade 3-4), hepatotoxicity, QTc prolongation; no new safety signals at final OS.
trials.reference: Hortobagyi GN et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:1738-48 (PFS); Hortobagyi GN et al. N Engl J Med 2022;386:942-50 (final OS, PMID 35263519); Ann Oncol 2018 update (PMID 29718092)
highlights: PFS HR 0.56; updated median PFS 25.3 vs 16.0 mo
Final OS 63.9 vs 51.4 mo, HR 0.76 - significant
First 1L CDK4/6i + AI trial to show >12 mo median OS gain
trials.takeaway: First-line ribociclib + letrozole significantly prolongs both PFS and OS (63.9 vs 51.4 mo) in postmenopausal HR+/HER2- MBC.

trials.name: PALOMA-2
trials.descriptor: palbociclib + letrozole 1L
trials.population: 666 postmenopausal women with ER+/HER2- ABC, no prior treatment for advanced disease
trials.arms: Palbociclib 125 mg d1-21 q28d + letrozole vs placebo + letrozole (2:1; 444 vs 222)
trials.results: PFS 24.8 vs 14.5 mo, HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.46-0.72), P<0.001. Final OS (JCO 2024, f/u 90.1 mo): median 53.9 vs 51.2 mo, HR 0.96 (0.78-1.18), one-sided P=0.34 - NOT significant; with recovered survival data 53.8 vs 49.8 mo, HR 0.92 (0.76-1.12), still not significant (imbalanced missing survival data limits interpretation).
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 neutropenia 66.4% vs 1.4%, leukopenia 24.8%; febrile neutropenia rare.
trials.reference: Finn RS et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:1925-36 (PFS); Slamon DJ et al. J Clin Oncol 2024 (final OS, PMID 38252901)
highlights: PFS 24.8 vs 14.5 mo, HR 0.58
OS 53.9 vs 51.2 mo, HR 0.96 - NOT significant
Contrast with MONALEESA-2 (ribociclib), which showed OS benefit
trials.takeaway: Palbociclib + letrozole nearly doubles PFS in 1L HR+/HER2- MBC but did not significantly improve overall survival.

trials.name: APHINITY
trials.descriptor: adjuvant pertuzumab + trastuzumab
trials.population: 4805 patients with operable HER2+ early breast cancer, node-positive or high-risk node-negative (63% node-positive, 36% HR-negative)
trials.arms: Pertuzumab vs placebo x1 y, added to standard adjuvant chemotherapy + trastuzumab x1 y (1:1, double-blind)
trials.results: Primary (median 45 mo): IDFS events 7.1% vs 8.7%, HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.66-1.00), P=0.045; 3-yr IDFS 94.1% vs 93.2%. Node-positive 3-yr IDFS 92.0% vs 90.2% (HR 0.77); node-negative 97.5% vs 98.4% (HR 1.13, no benefit). 6-yr update (JCO 2021): IDFS HR 0.76 (0.64-0.91), 6-yr IDFS 91% vs 88%; node-positive HR 0.72. Third interim OS (Loibl JCO 2024, median 8.4 y): 8-yr OS 92.7% vs 92.0%, HR 0.83 (0.68-1.02), P=0.078 - NOT significant. Node-positive 8-yr IDFS 86.1% vs 81.2% (HR 0.72, 0.60-0.87); node-negative placebo arm 8-yr IDFS 93.3%, OS 96.4%.
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 diarrhea 9.8% vs 3.7% (almost exclusively during chemotherapy); heart failure/cardiac death/cardiac dysfunction infrequent, primary cardiac events <1% in both arms.
trials.reference: von Minckwitz G et al. N Engl J Med 2017;377:122-131 (PMID 28581356); Piccart M et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1448-1457 (6-yr, PMID 33539215); Loibl S et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:3643-3651 (8.4-yr OS, PMID 39259927)
highlights: IDFS HR 0.81 (0.66-1.00); absolute gain ~1% at 3 y overall
Benefit confined to node-positive: 8-yr IDFS 86.1% vs 81.2% (HR 0.72)
8-yr OS 92.7% vs 92.0%, HR 0.83 - not significant
trials.takeaway: Adding pertuzumab to adjuvant trastuzumab + chemo gives a modest IDFS gain concentrated in node-positive disease, with no significant OS benefit at 8.4 years.

trials.name: CREATE-X
trials.descriptor: adjuvant capecitabine after residual disease, HER2-negative
trials.population: HER2-negative breast cancer with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant anthracycline/taxane chemotherapy (Japan/Korea)
trials.arms: Capecitabine 1250 mg/m² BID d1–14 q3wk × 6–8 cycles vs no further chemotherapy (both with standard endocrine/RT)
trials.toxicity: Hand-foot syndrome (73%), neutropenia, diarrhea
trials.reference: Masuda N et al. NEJM 2017;376:2147
highlights: Residual TNBC after neoadjuvant chemo → adjuvant capecitabine × 6–8 cycles; the benefit in HR+ disease was small.
Asian population and 1250 mg/m² dosing; US practice often uses 1000 mg/m² BID for tolerability.
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant capecitabine improves DFS and OS for residual disease after neoadjuvant chemo, mostly in TNBC

trials.name: MONARCH 2
trials.setting: HR+/HER2- metastatic after progression on ET, any menopausal status
trials.descriptor: abemaciclib + fulvestrant after ET
trials.population: 669 women with HR+/HER2- ABC progressing on (neo)adjuvant ET, within 12 mo of adjuvant ET, or on 1L ET for metastatic disease; no prior chemotherapy for ABC
trials.arms: Abemaciclib 150 mg BID continuous + fulvestrant 500 mg vs placebo + fulvestrant (2:1; 446 vs 223)
trials.results: PFS 16.4 vs 9.3 mo, HR 0.553 (95% CI 0.449-0.681), P<0.001. OS (JAMA Oncol 2020, prespecified interim): 46.7 vs 37.3 mo, HR 0.757 (0.606-0.945), P=0.01 - significant. Time to chemotherapy 50.2 vs 22.1 mo.
trials.toxicity: Diarrhea (most common, mostly grade 1-2, early), neutropenia, fatigue; dose started 200 mg then amended to 150 mg BID.
trials.reference: Sledge GW et al. J Clin Oncol 2017;35:2875-84 (PMID 28580882); Sledge GW et al. JAMA Oncol 2020;6:116-24 (OS, PMID 31563959)
highlights: PFS 16.4 vs 9.3 mo, HR 0.55
OS 46.7 vs 37.3 mo, HR 0.757 - significant
Diarrhea is the signature toxicity of abemaciclib
trials.takeaway: Abemaciclib + fulvestrant after ET progression improves PFS and OS (9.4-month median OS gain) regardless of menopausal status.

trials.name: MONARCH 3
trials.descriptor: abemaciclib + NSAI 1L
trials.population: 493 postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2- ABC, no prior systemic therapy in the advanced setting
trials.arms: Abemaciclib 150 mg BID continuous + anastrozole or letrozole vs placebo + NSAI (2:1; 328 vs 165)
trials.results: Interim PFS HR 0.54 (0.41-0.72); final PFS (NPJ Breast Cancer 2019): 28.18 vs 14.76 mo, HR 0.540 (0.418-0.698). Final OS (Ann Oncol 2024, f/u 8.1 y): 66.8 vs 53.7 mo, HR 0.804 (0.637-1.015), P=0.0664 - NOT statistically significant; visceral subgroup 63.7 vs 48.8 mo, HR 0.758, NS.
trials.toxicity: Grade 3+ neutropenia 23.9%, diarrhea 9.5%, leukopenia 8.6%.
trials.reference: Goetz MP et al. J Clin Oncol 2017;35:3638-46 (PMID 28968163); Johnston S et al. NPJ Breast Cancer 2019;5:5 (PMID 30675515); Goetz MP et al. Ann Oncol 2024;35:718-27 (final OS, PMID 38729566)
highlights: Final PFS 28.2 vs 14.8 mo, HR 0.54
Final OS 66.8 vs 53.7 mo, HR 0.804 - NOT significant (P=0.066)
13-month numeric OS gain despite missing significance
trials.takeaway: Abemaciclib + NSAI 1L nearly doubles PFS; the 13-month OS difference did not reach statistical significance.

trials.name: OlympiAD
trials.descriptor: olaparib vs chemo, gbrca her2- mbc
trials.population: Germline BRCA1/2 mutation, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer (HR+ or TNBC), <=2 prior chemo lines for metastatic disease; randomized 2:1
trials.arms: Olaparib tablets 300 mg BID vs physician's choice single-agent chemo (capecitabine, eribulin, or vinorelbine)
trials.results: PFS 7.0 vs 4.2 mo, HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.43-0.80), P<0.001. ORR 59.9% vs 28.8%. Final OS (64% maturity): 19.3 vs 17.1 mo, HR 0.90 (95% CI 0.66-1.23), P=0.513, NOT significant; exploratory 1L subgroup (no prior chemo for mBC) OS HR 0.51 (0.29-0.90). FDA regular approval Jan 12 2018.
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 36.6% vs 50.5%; discontinuation for toxicity 4.9% vs 7.7%; anemia, nausea, fatigue; no cumulative toxicity with extended exposure
trials.reference: Robson M et al. N Engl J Med 2017;377:523-33; Robson ME et al. Ann Oncol 2019;30:558-66 (final OS)
highlights: First PARP inhibitor approval in breast cancer: PFS 7.0 vs 4.2 mo, HR 0.58
Final OS not significant (HR 0.90); possible benefit when used 1L (exploratory HR 0.51)
Less grade >=3 toxicity than chemo (36.6% vs 50.5%)
trials.takeaway: Olaparib improves PFS and tolerability over chemotherapy in gBRCA HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer but does not significantly improve overall survival.

trials.name: EMBRACA
trials.descriptor: talazoparib vs chemo, gbrca her2- abc
trials.population: Germline BRCA1/2 mutation, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, <=3 prior cytotoxic regimens for advanced disease; randomized 2:1
trials.arms: Talazoparib 1 mg PO daily vs physician's choice single-agent chemo (capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, or vinorelbine)
trials.results: PFS 8.6 vs 5.6 mo, HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.71), P<0.001. ORR 62.6% vs 27.2%. Final OS: 19.3 vs 19.5 mo, HR 0.848 (95% CI 0.670-1.073), P=0.17, NOT significant (heavy subsequent PARPi/platinum use in control arm). PROs favored talazoparib. FDA approval Oct 16 2018.
trials.toxicity: Hematologic grade 3-4 AEs 55% vs 38% (mainly anemia); nonhematologic grade 3 AEs 32% vs 38%
trials.reference: Litton JK et al. N Engl J Med 2018;379:753-63; Litton JK et al. Ann Oncol 2020;31:1526-35 (final OS)
highlights: Final OS not significant (19.3 vs 19.5 mo, HR 0.85)
Anemia is the dominant toxicity; QoL favored talazoparib
trials.takeaway: Talazoparib improves PFS, response, and quality of life versus chemotherapy in gBRCA HER2-negative advanced breast cancer without an overall survival benefit.

trials.name: MONALEESA-3
trials.descriptor: ribociclib + fulvestrant 1L/2L
trials.population: 726 postmenopausal women (and men) with HR+/HER2- ABC, treatment-naive or up to 1 prior line of ET for advanced disease
trials.arms: Ribociclib 600 mg d1-21 q28d + fulvestrant 500 mg vs placebo + fulvestrant (2:1; 484 vs 242)
trials.results: PFS 20.5 vs 12.8 mo, HR 0.593 (95% CI 0.480-0.732), P<0.001. OS (NEJM 2020 final protocol OS): 42-mo OS 57.8% vs 45.9%, HR 0.72 (0.57-0.92), P=0.00455 - significant. Extended OS (Ann Oncol 2021, f/u 56.3 mo): median 53.7 vs 41.5 mo, HR 0.73 (0.59-0.90); 1L subgroup HR 0.64; 2L 39.7 vs 33.7 mo, HR 0.78 (0.59-1.04). Exploratory 1L update (Breast Cancer Res 2023, f/u 70.8 mo): 1L median OS 67.6 vs 51.8 mo, HR 0.67 (0.50-0.90).
trials.toxicity: Grade 3 neutropenia ~46%; hepatotoxicity, QTc prolongation.
trials.reference: Slamon DJ et al. J Clin Oncol 2018;36:2465-72 (PFS); Slamon DJ et al. N Engl J Med 2020;382:514-24 (OS, PMID 31826360); Slamon DJ et al. Ann Oncol 2021 (PMID 34102253); Neven P et al. Breast Cancer Res 2023 (PMID 37653397)
highlights: PFS 20.5 vs 12.8 mo, HR 0.59
OS 53.7 vs 41.5 mo, HR 0.73 - significant
1L subgroup median OS 67.6 vs 51.8 mo (exploratory)
trials.takeaway: Ribociclib + fulvestrant improves PFS and OS in 1L and 2L HR+/HER2- ABC, with the largest benefit in the first-line subgroup.

trials.name: MONALEESA-7
trials.descriptor: ribociclib + ET + goserelin premenopausal
trials.population: 672 pre/perimenopausal women aged 18-59 with HR+/HER2- ABC; no prior ET for advanced disease, up to 1 prior line of chemotherapy allowed
trials.arms: Ribociclib 600 mg d1-21 q28d vs placebo, each + goserelin + NSAI or tamoxifen (1:1; 335 vs 337)
trials.results: PFS 23.8 vs 13.0 mo, HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.44-0.69), P<0.0001. OS (NEJM 2019 interim): 42-mo OS 70.2% vs 46.0%, HR 0.71 (0.54-0.95), P=0.00973 - significant; NSAI subgroup HR 0.70. Extended OS (Clin Cancer Res 2022, f/u 53.5 mo, exploratory): median 58.7 vs 48.0 mo, HR 0.76 (0.61-0.96).
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 neutropenia 61% vs 4%, leukopenia 14%; QTc prolongation higher with tamoxifen (ribociclib not indicated with tamoxifen).
trials.reference: Tripathy D et al. Lancet Oncol 2018;19:904-15 (PFS); Im SA et al. N Engl J Med 2019;381:307-16 (OS, PMID 31166679); Lu YS et al. Clin Cancer Res 2022 (updated OS, PMID 34965945)
highlights: Only dedicated premenopausal CDK4/6i phase 3
PFS 23.8 vs 13.0 mo, HR 0.55
OS HR 0.71 (42-mo OS 70% vs 46%); updated median 58.7 vs 48.0 mo
trials.takeaway: In premenopausal HR+/HER2- ABC, ribociclib + ovarian suppression + ET improves PFS and OS; pair with an AI, not tamoxifen (QT).

trials.name: TAILORx
trials.descriptor: Oncotype DX RS 11–25: endocrine therapy alone vs chemo-endocrine
trials.population: HR+/HER2−, node-negative breast cancer (1.1–5 cm or 0.6–1 cm high grade); RS 11–25 randomized; RS ≤10 endocrine only, RS ≥26 chemo-endocrine
trials.arms: Endocrine therapy alone vs chemotherapy + endocrine therapy (RS 11–25)
trials.results: 9-yr iDFS 83.3% vs 84.3% (HR 1.08) — endocrine alone non-inferior. Women ≤50 with RS 16–25 had a 6–7 point iDFS benefit from chemo; RS ≤10 9-yr distant recurrence 3%
trials.reference: Sparano JA et al. NEJM 2018;379:111; NEJM 2015;373:2005 (RS ≤10)
highlights: Chemotherapy can be omitted for RS ≤25 in node-negative disease if age >50; in women ≤50, RS 16–25 still favors chemotherapy (possibly via ovarian suppression).
RS ≥26 → chemotherapy; RS ≤10 → endocrine therapy alone regardless of age.
trials.takeaway: Endocrine therapy alone is non-inferior for RS 11–25 node-negative HR+ disease, except women ≤50 with RS 16–25

trials.name: KATHERINE
trials.descriptor: T-DM1 vs trastuzumab for residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy
trials.population: HER2+ early breast cancer with residual invasive disease in breast or axilla after neoadjuvant taxane + trastuzumab
trials.arms: Trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1) 3.6 mg/kg q3wk × 14 vs trastuzumab × 14
trials.toxicity: Thrombocytopenia, elevated transaminases, peripheral neuropathy; more discontinuation with T-DM1 (18% vs 2%)
trials.reference: von Minckwitz G et al. NEJM 2019;380:617; Geyer CE et al. NEJM 2025 (OS)
highlights: Residual disease after neoadjuvant HER2 therapy → switch to T-DM1 × 14 rather than completing trastuzumab.
The main argument for neoadjuvant therapy in HER2+ disease: response guides escalation.
trials.takeaway: T-DM1 halves recurrence risk for HER2+ residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy

trials.name: SOLAR-1
trials.descriptor: alpelisib + fulvestrant in pik3ca-mutated disease
trials.population: Men and postmenopausal women with HR+/HER2- ABC progressing on or after AI; PIK3CA-mutant cohort (tissue) n=341 of 572. Very few (about 6%) had prior CDK4/6i
trials.arms: Alpelisib 300 mg PO daily + fulvestrant 500 mg vs placebo + fulvestrant
trials.results: PIK3CA-mut: median PFS 11.0 (95% CI 7.5-14.5) vs 5.7 mo (3.7-7.4), HR 0.65 (0.50-0.85), P<0.001. PIK3CA-WT cohort: HR 0.85 (0.58-1.25) - no meaningful benefit. Final OS (PIK3CA-mut): 39.3 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.86 (0.64-1.15), P=0.15 - NOT significant (did not cross boundary).
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 hyperglycemia 36.6% vs 0.7%; grade 3-4 rash 9.9% vs 0.3%; grade 3 diarrhea 6.7% vs 0.3%; discontinuation for AEs 25.0% vs 4.2%.
trials.reference: Andre F et al. N Engl J Med 2019;380(20):1929-1940; final OS Andre F et al. Ann Oncol 2021;32(2):208-217 (PMID 33246021)
highlights: First PI3K-alpha inhibitor: PFS 11.0 vs 5.7 mo, HR 0.65 in PIK3CA-mutated disease
OS 39.3 vs 31.4 mo, HR 0.86 - not statistically significant
Grade 3-4 hyperglycemia 36.6%; label: check FPG + HbA1c first, safety not established in type 1 or uncontrolled type 2 DM; FDA approved 24 May 2019
trials.takeaway: Alpelisib + fulvestrant improves PFS in PIK3CA-mutated HR+ disease but with frequent severe hyperglycemia, no significant OS gain, and little data after CDK4/6i.

trials.name: HER2CLIMB
trials.descriptor: tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine, previously treated HER2+ metastatic
trials.population: HER2+ metastatic breast cancer after trastuzumab, pertuzumab and T-DM1; active or stable brain metastases allowed (~48% had brain mets)
trials.arms: Tucatinib 300 mg BID + trastuzumab + capecitabine vs placebo + trastuzumab + capecitabine
trials.results: 1-yr PFS 33.1% vs 12.3%, median 7.8 vs 5.6 mo (HR 0.54); OS 21.9 vs 17.4 mo (HR 0.66; updated 24.7 vs 19.2, HR 0.73); brain metastases: 1-yr PFS 24.9% vs 0%, median 7.6 vs 5.4 mo (HR 0.48); CNS-PFS 9.9 vs 4.2 mo (HR 0.32, Lin JCO 2020)
trials.toxicity: Diarrhea, hand-foot syndrome, transaminase elevation
trials.reference: Murthy RK et al. NEJM 2020;382:597; Lin NU et al. JCO 2020 (CNS); Curigliano G et al. Ann Oncol 2022 (OS)
highlights: The only HER2 regimen with an OS benefit in patients with active brain metastases — tucatinib is the go-to for HER2+ CNS disease.
Tucatinib is HER2-selective (spares EGFR) → less diarrhea/rash than neratinib or lapatinib.
trials.takeaway: Tucatinib + trastuzumab + capecitabine improves PFS and OS in pretreated HER2+ disease, including active brain metastases

trials.name: KEYNOTE-355
trials.descriptor: pembrolizumab + chemo, 1l pd-l1+ mtnbc
trials.population: Previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic TNBC (de novo or >=6 mo after curative treatment); PD-L1 by 22C3 CPS; randomized 2:1
trials.arms: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + chemo (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine-carboplatin) vs placebo + chemo
trials.primary_endpoint: PFS and OS (dual primary) in CPS>=10, CPS>=1, and ITT (hierarchical)
trials.results: PFS CPS>=10: 9.7 vs 5.6 mo, HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.49-0.86), primary objective met (Lancet 2020). PFS CPS>=1: 7.6 vs 5.6 mo, HR 0.74, not significant. Final OS (median f/u 44.1 mo): CPS>=10 23.0 vs 16.1 mo, HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.55-0.95), P=0.0185, significant; CPS>=1 17.6 vs 16.0 mo, HR 0.86 (0.72-1.04), NOT significant; ITT 17.2 vs 15.5 mo, HR 0.89 (not tested). FDA: accelerated approval Nov 13 2020 (CPS>=10); converted to regular approval Jul 26 2021.
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs 68.1% vs 66.9%; treatment-related death 0.4% vs 0%; immune-mediated AEs (thyroid, pneumonitis, colitis, hepatitis)
trials.reference: Cortes J et al. Lancet 2020;396:1817-28 (PFS); Cortes J et al. N Engl J Med 2022;387:217-26 (final OS)
highlights: PD-L1 CPS>=10 (22C3) selects benefit: OS 23.0 vs 16.1 mo, HR 0.73
No significant OS benefit at CPS>=1 (HR 0.86); benefit increases with PD-L1 enrichment
Partner chemo options: nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine-carboplatin
trials.takeaway: For 1L metastatic TNBC with PD-L1 CPS>=10, pembrolizumab + chemotherapy improves PFS and OS; CPS 1-9 patients do not derive significant benefit.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-522
trials.descriptor: neoadjuvant pembrolizumab + chemo → adjuvant pembrolizumab, early TNBC
trials.population: Previously untreated stage II–III triple-negative breast cancer (T1c N1–2 or T2–4 N0–2), regardless of PD-L1
trials.arms: Pembrolizumab + carboplatin/paclitaxel → pembrolizumab + AC/EC, then adjuvant pembrolizumab × 9 cycles, vs placebo + the same chemotherapy
trials.primary_endpoint: Pathologic complete response (ypT0/Tis ypN0) and event-free survival
trials.toxicity: Immune-mediated AEs (thyroid dysfunction, adrenal insufficiency, pneumonitis); grade ≥3 AEs ~78% both arms
trials.reference: Schmid P et al. NEJM 2020;382:810 (pCR); NEJM 2022;386:556 (EFS); NEJM 2024;391:1981 (OS)
highlights: The standard for stage ≥II TNBC: pembrolizumab with neoadjuvant chemo, continued adjuvantly regardless of pCR.
Benefit independent of PD-L1 status — do not test CPS to select early-stage patients (unlike metastatic TNBC).
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab + chemo neoadjuvant then adjuvant improves pCR, EFS and OS in stage II–III TNBC

trials.name: monarchE
trials.descriptor: adjuvant abemaciclib × 2 years, node-positive high-risk HR+/HER2−
trials.population: HR+/HER2− early breast cancer, node-positive high risk: ≥4 positive nodes, or 1–3 nodes plus grade 3, tumor ≥5 cm, or Ki-67 ≥20%
trials.arms: Abemaciclib 150 mg BID × 2 years + endocrine therapy vs endocrine therapy alone
trials.results: 2-yr iDFS 92.2% vs 88.7% (HR 0.75) at primary analysis; 5-yr iDFS 83.6% vs 76.0%. Primary OS analysis (Johnston Ann Oncol 2025, median 76.2 mo, ITT 5637): OS HR 0.842 (95% CI 0.722-0.981), P=0.027 - statistically significant; 7-yr OS 86.8% vs 85.0% (absolute +1.8%). Fewer patients living with metastatic disease (6.4% vs 9.4%). 7-yr IDFS 77.4% vs 70.9% (HR 0.734, 0.657-0.820; +6.5%); 7-yr DRFS 80.0% vs 74.9% (HR 0.746, 0.662-0.840; +5.1%). No delayed toxicity signal.
trials.toxicity: Diarrhea (84%, mostly grade 1–2), neutropenia, fatigue, VTE (2.5%), ILD (rare)
trials.reference: Johnston SRD et al. JCO 2020;38:3987; Lancet Oncol 2023;24:77 (4-yr); Rastogi P et al. JCO 2024 (5-yr); Johnston S et al. Overall survival with abemaciclib in early breast cancer. Ann Oncol 2026;37:155-165 (epub Oct 2025; PMID 41110697)
highlights: The first CDK4/6 inhibitor to succeed in the adjuvant setting (PALLAS and PENELOPE-B with palbociclib were negative).
Two-year course; the absolute benefit keeps widening after treatment ends (carry-over effect).
Now the first adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitor with a statistically significant OS benefit (HR 0.84; 7-yr OS 86.8% vs 85.0%).
trials.takeaway: 2 years of adjuvant abemaciclib improves iDFS and OS in node-positive high-risk HR+/HER2- breast cancer

trials.name: ASCENT
trials.descriptor: sacituzumab govitecan vs chemo, pretreated mtnbc
