trials.population: Relapsed or refractory metastatic TNBC after >=2 prior chemotherapy regimens (one could be early-stage if relapse within 12 mo); all taxane-exposed; primary analysis in 468 patients without brain metastases (529 total)
trials.arms: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV d1, d8 q21d vs single-agent physician's choice (eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine, or gemcitabine)
trials.primary_endpoint: PFS by BICR in patients without brain metastases
trials.results: PFS 5.6 vs 1.7 mo, HR 0.41 (95% CI 0.32-0.52), P<0.001. OS 12.1 vs 6.7 mo, HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.38-0.59), P<0.001. ORR 35% vs 5%. FDA: accelerated approval Apr 22 2020; regular approval Apr 7 2021 (>=2 prior systemic therapies, >=1 for metastatic disease).
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 treatment-related: neutropenia 51% vs 33%, leukopenia 10% vs 5%, diarrhea 10% vs <1%, anemia 8% vs 5%, febrile neutropenia 6% vs 2%; no treatment-related deaths with SG. Boxed warning neutropenia + diarrhea; reduced UGT1A1 activity (*28 homozygous) increases neutropenia risk
trials.reference: Bardia A et al. N Engl J Med 2021;384:1529-41
highlights: First TROP2 ADC (SN-38 payload): PFS 5.6 vs 1.7 mo, OS 12.1 vs 6.7 mo
Neutropenia and diarrhea are the key toxicities (boxed warning); UGT1A1*28 homozygotes at higher risk
Dosing 10 mg/kg d1, d8 q21d
trials.takeaway: In pretreated metastatic TNBC, sacituzumab govitecan roughly doubles OS versus single-agent chemotherapy and is standard 2L+ therapy.

trials.name: ATEMPT
trials.descriptor: adjuvant T-DM1 vs paclitaxel-trastuzumab
trials.population: 497 treated patients with stage I centrally confirmed HER2+ breast cancer
trials.arms: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg q3w x17 cycles vs paclitaxel 80 mg/m2 + trastuzumab weekly x12 then trastuzumab to 1 y (TH) (3:1)
trials.primary_endpoint: Co-primary: clinically relevant toxicity (CRT) T-DM1 vs TH; 3-yr iDFS with T-DM1
trials.results: Primary: CRT 46% T-DM1 vs 47% TH (P=0.83) - toxicity NOT lower; 3-yr iDFS with T-DM1 97.8% (95% CI 96.3-99.3). 5-yr update (JCO 2024, median 5.8 y): T-DM1 5-yr iDFS 97.0% (95.2-98.7), RFI 98.3%, OS 97.8%, BCSS 99.4%; TH arm 5-yr iDFS 91.1% (not powered for comparison). HER2DX high risk predicted recurrence.
trials.toxicity: CRT similar (46% vs 47%); T-DM1 caused less neuropathy and alopecia and better work productivity by PROs; thrombocytopenia and transaminase elevation with T-DM1.
trials.reference: Tolaney SM et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:2375-2385 (PMID 34077270); Tarantino P et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:3652-3665 (5-yr, PMID 38935923)
highlights: 3-yr iDFS 97.8%, 5-yr iDFS 97.0% with T-DM1
Clinically relevant toxicity not reduced: 46% vs 47%
Less neuropathy/alopecia with T-DM1 by PROs
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant T-DM1 yields excellent outcomes in stage I HER2+ disease but did not reduce clinically relevant toxicity vs paclitaxel-trastuzumab, so TH (APT) remains standard.

trials.name: OlympiA
trials.descriptor: adjuvant olaparib × 1 year, germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative
trials.population: Germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant, HER2-negative, high-risk early breast cancer (TNBC with residual disease or ≥pT2/pN1; HR+ with residual disease and CPS+EG ≥3 or ≥4 nodes) after (neo)adjuvant chemo
trials.arms: Olaparib 300 mg BID × 1 year vs placebo
trials.results: 3-yr iDFS 85.9% vs 77.1% (HR 0.58); 4-yr OS 89.8% vs 86.4% (HR 0.68). 6-yr update (Garber Ann Oncol 2026, median follow-up 6.1 yr): OS 87.5% vs 83.2% (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.56-0.93); IDFS HR 0.65; DDFS HR 0.65; MDS/AML 0.4% vs 0.7% (no excess)
trials.toxicity: Anemia, nausea, fatigue; no excess MDS/AML at 3.5 yr
trials.reference: Tutt ANJ et al. NEJM 2021;384:2394; Geyer CE et al. Ann Oncol 2022 (OS); Garber JE et al. Ann Oncol 2026 (6-yr, PMID 42636977)
highlights: Germline BRCA testing now has an adjuvant treatment consequence — test all TNBC and high-risk HER2− patients eligible by NCCN/ASCO criteria.
One year of olaparib after chemotherapy; sequencing with pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-522) or endocrine therapy is extrapolated.
trials.takeaway: 1 year of adjuvant olaparib improves iDFS and OS in high-risk gBRCA HER2-negative breast cancer

trials.name: RxPONDER
trials.descriptor: Oncotype DX RS ≤25 with 1–3 positive nodes: chemo benefit by menopausal status
trials.population: HR+/HER2− breast cancer with 1–3 positive axillary nodes and Recurrence Score ≤25
trials.arms: Endocrine therapy alone vs chemotherapy + endocrine therapy
trials.results: Postmenopausal: 5-yr iDFS 91.9% vs 91.3% — no chemotherapy benefit. Premenopausal: 5-yr iDFS 93.9% vs 89.0% (HR 0.60), OS 98.6% vs 97.3%
trials.reference: Kalinsky K et al. NEJM 2021;385:2336
highlights: Postmenopausal women with 1–3 nodes and RS ≤25 can skip chemotherapy; premenopausal women still benefit (unclear whether from cytotoxicity or chemo-induced ovarian suppression).
Extends genomic-assay-driven de-escalation into node-positive disease.
trials.takeaway: With 1–3 nodes and RS ≤25, chemo adds nothing postmenopausally but still benefits premenopausal women

trials.name: DESTINY-Breast03
trials.descriptor: t-dxd vs t-dm1 after trastuzumab + taxane
trials.population: HER2+ unresectable/metastatic BC previously treated with trastuzumab + a taxane; ECOG 0-1; measurable disease
trials.arms: T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg q3w vs T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg q3w (open-label, 1:1)
trials.results: Primary (NEJM 2022): 12-mo PFS 75.8% vs 34.1%, HR 0.28 (95% CI 0.22-0.37), P<0.001; ORR 79.7% vs 34.2%. Updated (Lancet 2023, median f/u ~28 mo): median PFS 28.8 vs 6.8 mo, HR 0.33 (0.26-0.43); median OS not reached in either arm, HR 0.64 (0.47-0.87), p=0.0037 (28% vs 37% OS events).
trials.toxicity: Adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis 10.5% vs 1.9% (primary); 15% vs 3% at update, no grade 4-5 events. Grade >=3 TEAEs 56% vs 52% (update).
trials.reference: Cortes J et al. NEJM 2022;386:1143; Hurvitz SA et al. Lancet 2023;401:105 (OS)
highlights: PFS HR 0.28 at primary; median PFS 28.8 vs 6.8 mo at update
OS benefit HR 0.64 (median not reached either arm)
ILD 15% vs 3% at update, no grade 4-5
trials.takeaway: T-DXd replaced T-DM1 as standard second-line therapy for HER2+ mBC, with a large PFS gain and an OS benefit.

trials.name: DESTINY-Breast04
trials.descriptor: t-dxd vs chemo in her2-low mbc
trials.population: HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH-) unresectable/metastatic BC after 1-2 prior lines of chemo in the metastatic setting; HR+ must be endocrine refractory; 494 HR+ and 63 HR-
trials.arms: T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg q3w vs physician's choice chemo (2:1)
trials.primary_endpoint: PFS by BICR in HR+ cohort
trials.results: HR+ cohort: median PFS 10.1 vs 5.4 mo, HR 0.51, P<0.001; median OS 23.9 vs 17.5 mo, HR 0.64, P=0.003. All patients: median PFS 9.9 vs 5.1 mo, HR 0.50, P<0.001; median OS 23.4 vs 16.8 mo, HR 0.64, P=0.001.
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 52.6% vs 67.4%. Adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis 12.1% with T-DXd; 0.8% grade 5.
trials.reference: Modi S et al. NEJM 2022;387:9
highlights: Created the HER2-low category as a treatable target
HR+ cohort OS 23.9 vs 17.5 mo (HR 0.64)
ILD 12.1%, 0.8% fatal; FDA approval Aug 5, 2022
trials.takeaway: T-DXd improves PFS and OS over chemotherapy in previously treated HER2-low mBC, establishing HER2-low as an actionable category.

trials.name: EMERALD
trials.descriptor: oral serd elacestrant vs standard endocrine therapy after cdk4/6i
trials.population: ER+/HER2- advanced breast cancer after 1-2 lines of endocrine therapy, mandatory prior CDK4/6i, <=1 chemotherapy line; ESR1 mutation (ctDNA, Guardant360) in 47.8%
trials.arms: Elacestrant 345 mg PO daily with food (400 mg elacestrant dihydrochloride) vs investigator's choice SOC endocrine monotherapy (fulvestrant or AI)
trials.primary_endpoint: PFS by blinded independent central review in all patients and in ESR1-mutated patients
trials.results: All patients: PFS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.55-0.88), P=.002. ESR1-mutated (n=228): median PFS 3.8 vs 1.9 mo, HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.39-0.77), P=.0005. ESR1 not detected (exploratory, FDA): HR 0.86 (0.63-1.19), NS - ITT benefit driven by ESR1m subgroup.
trials.toxicity: Treatment-related grade 3/4 AEs 7.2% vs 3.1%; nausea 35.0% vs 18.8% (grade 3/4 2.5% vs 0.9%); discontinuation for TRAEs 3.4% vs 0.9%. Also musculoskeletal pain, dyslipidemia.
trials.reference: Bidard FC et al. J Clin Oncol 2022;40(28):3246-3256
highlights: First oral SERD to beat SOC endocrine therapy in a phase 3 trial
Benefit concentrated in ESR1-mutated disease: PFS 3.8 vs 1.9 mo, HR 0.55
FDA approved 27 Jan 2023 for ER+/HER2- ESR1-mutated ABC after >=1 line of endocrine therapy (Guardant360 CDx)
trials.takeaway: Elacestrant is a standard oral option for ESR1-mutated ER+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer after CDK4/6i, with modest absolute PFS gain and little benefit in ESR1 wild-type disease.

trials.name: TROPiCS-02
trials.setting: HR+/HER2- metastatic, heavily pretreated (after ET, CDK4/6i, taxane, 2-4 chemo lines)
trials.descriptor: sacituzumab govitecan vs physician's choice chemotherapy
trials.population: Endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2- locally recurrent/metastatic BC after ET, taxane and CDK4/6i in any setting + 2-4 prior chemo regimens for metastatic disease; 99% prior CDK4/6i, median 3 prior chemo lines, 95% visceral mets
trials.arms: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trop-2 ADC, SN-38 payload) vs physician's choice (eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine or gemcitabine)
trials.primary_endpoint: PFS by blinded independent central review
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 treatment-related neutropenia 51% vs 38%, diarrhea 9% vs 1%. One treatment-related death (neutropenic colitis/septic shock).
trials.reference: Rugo HS et al. J Clin Oncol 2022;40(29):3365-3376; final OS Rugo HS et al. Lancet 2023;402(10411):1423-1433 (PMID 37633306)
highlights: PFS 5.5 vs 4.0 mo, HR 0.66 in heavily pretreated HR+ disease
OS 14.4 vs 11.2 mo, HR 0.79 - significant, regardless of Trop-2 level
FDA approved 3 Feb 2023 for HR+/HER2- after endocrine therapy + >=2 additional systemic therapies in the metastatic setting
trials.takeaway: Sacituzumab govitecan improves both PFS and OS over single-agent chemotherapy in heavily pretreated HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer, at the cost of neutropenia and diarrhea.

trials.name: CAPItello-291
trials.descriptor: akt inhibitor capivasertib + fulvestrant
trials.population: Pre/peri/postmenopausal women and men with HR+/HER2- ABC relapsed/progressed on or after AI, +/- prior CDK4/6i (69.1% had prior CDK4/6i for ABC); 40.8% AKT pathway-altered (PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN)
trials.arms: Capivasertib 400 mg PO BID, 4 days on/3 days off + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant; double-blind
trials.primary_endpoint: Dual: investigator-assessed PFS in overall population and AKT pathway-altered population
trials.results: Overall: median PFS 7.2 vs 3.6 mo, HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.51-0.71), P<0.001. AKT pathway-altered: 7.3 vs 3.1 mo, HR 0.50 (0.38-0.65), P<0.001. Final OS (ESMO Breast 2026, not yet in PubMed): altered 28.5 vs 30.4 mo, HR 0.83 (0.63-1.10), P=.201 - NOT significant; overall 29.4 vs 28.6 mo, HR 1.00 (0.83-1.19).
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 rash 12.1% vs 0.3%, diarrhea 9.3% vs 0.3%; discontinuation for AEs 13.0% vs 2.3%. Label: hyperglycemia 18% (grade 3-4 2.8%, DKA 0.3%); diarrhea 72% (grade 3-4 9%); cutaneous reactions 58%.
trials.reference: Turner NC et al. N Engl J Med 2023;388(22):2058-2070
highlights: PFS benefit overall (HR 0.60) and in PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered (7.3 vs 3.1 mo, HR 0.50); ~70% post-CDK4/6i
FDA approved 16 Nov 2023 ONLY for PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered disease (FoundationOne CDx)
Final OS not significant (altered HR 0.83; overall HR 1.00)
trials.takeaway: Capivasertib + fulvestrant is a post-CDK4/6i option for PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered HR+ disease, with less hyperglycemia than alpelisib but more rash and diarrhea, and no proven OS benefit.

trials.name: MAINTAIN
trials.descriptor: switch to ribociclib + alternative endocrine therapy after CDK4/6 progression
trials.population: HR+/HER2− metastatic breast cancer progressing on a CDK4/6 inhibitor + endocrine therapy (86% prior palbociclib)
trials.arms: Ribociclib + switched endocrine therapy (fulvestrant or exemestane) vs placebo + switched endocrine therapy
trials.reference: Kalinsky K et al. JCO 2023;41:4004
highlights: First randomized evidence that continuing CDK4/6 blockade (with a switch of agent and endocrine partner) beyond progression has value.
Modest absolute benefit; genomic-driven options (PIK3CA, ESR1, AKT/PTEN) take priority when a target exists.
trials.takeaway: Ribociclib + switched endocrine therapy after CDK4/6i progression modestly improves PFS

trials.name: PRIME II
trials.descriptor: omission of whole-breast RT age >=65
trials.population: 1326 women >=65 y with HR+, node-negative, T1-T2 (<=3 cm) breast cancer after BCS with clear margins, on adjuvant endocrine therapy
trials.arms: Whole-breast irradiation (40-50 Gy) vs no irradiation, both with endocrine therapy
trials.results: Median 9.1 y: 10-yr local recurrence 9.5% (6.8-12.3) no RT vs 0.9% (0.1-1.7) RT, HR 10.4 (4.1-26.1), P<0.001. 10-yr distant recurrence as first event 1.6% vs 3.0% (not higher without RT). 10-yr OS 80.8% vs 80.7% - no difference; regional recurrence and BCSS similar.
trials.toxicity: Not a focus of report; omission avoids RT toxicity.
trials.reference: Kunkler IH et al. N Engl J Med 2023;388:585-594 (PMID 36791159)
highlights: 10-yr local recurrence 9.5% vs 0.9%
10-yr OS 80.8% vs 80.7% - no difference
No increase in distant recurrence without RT
trials.takeaway: In women >=65 with low-risk HR+ N0 tumors <=3 cm on endocrine therapy, omitting RT raises local recurrence (9.5% vs 0.9% at 10 y) without affecting distant recurrence or survival.

trials.name: SOUND
trials.setting: Surgery, small tumor, negative axillary ultrasound
trials.descriptor: omission of sentinel node biopsy with negative axillary ultrasound
trials.population: Breast cancer ≤2 cm with negative preoperative axillary ultrasound, planned breast conservation + RT
trials.arms: Sentinel lymph node biopsy vs no axillary surgery
trials.results: 5-yr DDFS 97.7% vs 98.0% (HR 0.84) — non-inferior; nodal positivity in the SLNB arm was 13.7%, yet outcomes were unaffected
trials.reference: Gentilini OD et al. JAMA Oncol 2023;9:1557
highlights: Axillary staging can be omitted for small, clinically node-negative tumors with a negative ultrasound — especially in older, HR+ patients where nodal status won't change systemic therapy.
Missed nodal disease had no measurable impact because adjuvant decisions were driven by tumor biology.
trials.takeaway: Omitting SLNB is non-inferior for tumors ≤2 cm with negative axillary ultrasound

trials.name: DESTINY-Breast06
trials.descriptor: t-dxd vs chemo after endocrine therapy, her2-low and ultralow
trials.population: HR+ mBC, HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+/ISH-) or HER2-ultralow (IHC 0 with membrane staining), >=1 line endocrine-based therapy, no prior chemo for mBC; 713 HER2-low, 153 ultralow
trials.arms: T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg q3w vs physician's choice chemo (capecitabine 60%, nab-paclitaxel 24%, paclitaxel 16%) (1:1)
trials.primary_endpoint: PFS by BICR in HER2-low population
trials.results: HER2-low: median PFS 13.2 vs 8.1 mo, HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.52-0.75), P<0.001. ITT incl ultralow (FDA review): median PFS 13.2 vs 8.1 mo, HR 0.64 (0.54-0.76). Ultralow exploratory subgroup (FDA review, n=153): median PFS 15.1 vs 8.3 mo, HR 0.76 (0.49-1.17), CI crosses 1. OS immature at PFS analysis.
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 52.8% vs 44.4%. Adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis 11.3% (3 grade 5) vs 0.2%.
trials.reference: Bardia A et al. NEJM 2024;391:2110
highlights: Moves T-DXd ahead of chemo in HR+ HER2-low after endocrine therapy
Ultralow subgroup exploratory only (HR 0.76, CI crosses 1)
OS immature; ILD 11.3% with 3 deaths; FDA approval Jan 27, 2025
trials.takeaway: In chemo-naive HR+ HER2-low or ultralow mBC after endocrine therapy, T-DXd prolongs PFS over chemotherapy, but OS is immature and the ultralow benefit is exploratory.

trials.name: DESTINY-Breast12
trials.setting: Metastatic HER2+, with or without brain metastases
trials.descriptor: single-arm t-dxd in her2+ mbc with brain mets
trials.population: HER2+ mBC after >=1 prior anti-HER2 regimen; stable or active brain mets cohort (n=263) and no-brain-mets cohort (n=241)
trials.arms: T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg q3w (single arm, no formal hypothesis testing)
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 51% (BM) and 49% (non-BM). Investigator-reported ILD 16% (grade >=3 3%) with BMs; 13% (grade >=3 1%) without.
trials.reference: Harbeck N et al. Nat Med 2024;30:3717
highlights: Largest prospective T-DXd brain-mets study (n=263 with BMs)
12-mo PFS 61.6%, 12-mo CNS PFS 58.9%
Single arm, no hypothesis testing; ILD 16% in BM cohort
trials.takeaway: T-DXd has durable systemic and intracranial activity in HER2+ mBC with stable or active brain metastases, supporting its use regardless of baseline brain mets.

trials.name: INAVO120
trials.setting: HR+/HER2- metastatic, 1st line, endocrine-resistant (relapse on/within 12 mo of adjuvant ET)
trials.descriptor: inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant in pik3ca-mutated endocrine-resistant disease
trials.population: PIK3CA-mutated HR+/HER2- locally advanced/metastatic BC relapsing during or within 12 mo after completing adjuvant endocrine therapy
trials.arms: Inavolisib 9 mg PO daily + palbociclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + palbociclib + fulvestrant; double-blind
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4: neutropenia 80.2% vs 78.4%, hyperglycemia 5.6% vs 0%, stomatitis/mucositis 5.6% vs 0%, diarrhea 3.7% vs 0%; no grade 3-4 rash. Ocular toxicity (dry eye, blurred vision) more frequent. Inavolisib discontinuation for AEs 6.8% vs 0.6% (final analysis).
trials.reference: Turner NC et al. N Engl J Med 2024;391:1584; final OS Jhaveri KL et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393(2):151-161 (PMID 40454641)
highlights: Triplet doubled PFS: 15.0 vs 7.3 mo, HR 0.43
First PI3K-pathway trial with significant OS gain: 34.0 vs 27.0 mo, HR 0.67
FDA approved 10 Oct 2024 (Itovebi, FoundationOne Liquid CDx); grade 3-4 hyperglycemia only 5.6%
trials.takeaway: For PIK3CA-mutated HR+ disease relapsing on or soon after adjuvant endocrine therapy, inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant is a first-line standard with a proven OS benefit.

trials.name: NATALEE
trials.descriptor: adjuvant ribociclib × 3 years, stage II–III HR+/HER2− incl. node-negative
trials.population: HR+/HER2− early breast cancer: any stage III, stage IIB, or stage IIA with grade 3 or grade 2 with high genomic risk/Ki-67 ≥20% (node-negative allowed)
trials.arms: Ribociclib 400 mg daily 3 wk on/1 off × 3 years + NSAI (± ovarian suppression) vs NSAI alone
trials.results: 3-yr iDFS 90.4% vs 87.1% (HR 0.75); 4-yr iDFS 88.5% vs 83.6% (HR 0.72). 5-yr follow-up (Crown ESMO Open 2025, median iDFS follow-up 55.4 mo): iDFS HR 0.716 (95% CI 0.618-0.829), nominal P<0.0001; absolute iDFS gain grew from 2.7% at 3 y to 4.5% at 5 y; N0 subgroup HR 0.606 (0.372-0.986). OS still maturing: HR 0.800 (0.637-1.003), nominal one-sided P=0.026 - not yet statistically significant.
trials.toxicity: Neutropenia, arthralgia, LFT elevation; QTc prolongation (400 mg dose lowers this vs 600 mg)
trials.reference: Slamon D et al. NEJM 2024;390:1080; Fasching PA et al. Ann Oncol 2025 (4-yr); Crown J et al. ESMO Open 2025;10:105858 (PMID 41320342)
highlights: Broadens adjuvant CDK4/6 eligibility to node-negative stage II disease, at a lower 400 mg dose for 3 years.
Absolute benefit is ~3–5 points; discuss duration, cost and toxicity against monarchE's 2-year regimen when both qualify.
trials.takeaway: 3 years of adjuvant ribociclib improves iDFS in stage II–III HR+/HER2− breast cancer including node-negative

trials.name: postMONARCH
trials.descriptor: abemaciclib + fulvestrant after progression on CDK4/6 inhibitor + AI
trials.population: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer progressing on a CDK4/6 inhibitor + aromatase inhibitor (metastatic or adjuvant)
trials.arms: Abemaciclib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant
trials.results: PFS 6.0 vs 5.3 mo (HR 0.73); ORR 17% vs 7%; consistent across prior CDK4/6i and ESR1/PIK3CA status
trials.reference: Kalinsky K et al. JCO 2025;43:1101 (ASCO 2024 LBA1001)
highlights: Phase 3 confirmation of the MAINTAIN concept with abemaciclib; the absolute gain is small (~0.7 mo median) but the HR is meaningful.
Reasonable option when no actionable alteration is present and the patient tolerates CDK4/6 inhibition.
trials.takeaway: Abemaciclib + fulvestrant modestly improves PFS after CDK4/6 inhibitor progression

trials.name: ASCENT-03
trials.descriptor: sacituzumab govitecan vs chemo, 1l mtnbc not io candidates
trials.population: Previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic TNBC not candidates for PD-(L)1 inhibitors (PD-L1 CPS<10, or CPS>=10 with prior IO use or comorbidity); randomized 1:1
trials.arms: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg d1, d8 q21d vs chemo (paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, or gemcitabine + carboplatin)
trials.results: PFS 9.7 vs 6.9 mo, HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.50-0.77), P<0.001. ORR 48% vs 46%; DOR 12.2 vs 7.2 mo. OS immature. FDA approval Jun 24 2026 (monotherapy, 1L TNBC not candidates for PD-1/PD-L1 therapy).
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 66% vs 62% (SG: neutropenia 43%, diarrhea 9%, leukopenia 7%); discontinuation 4% vs 12%
trials.reference: Cortes J et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:1912-25
highlights: 1L SG improves PFS 9.7 vs 6.9 mo, HR 0.62 in IO-ineligible TNBC
ORR similar (48% vs 46%) but responses more durable (12.2 vs 7.2 mo)
OS immature at primary report; FDA approved Jun 2026
trials.takeaway: In 1L metastatic TNBC not eligible for PD-(L)1 therapy, sacituzumab govitecan improves PFS over chemotherapy; OS data are immature.

trials.name: DESTINY-Breast05
trials.descriptor: t-dxd vs t-dm1 for high-risk residual disease
trials.population: HER2+ early BC with residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant therapy and high risk (node-positive at surgery or inoperable at diagnosis)
trials.arms: T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg vs T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg q3w (open-label, 1:1), max 14 cycles
trials.results: Median f/u ~30 mo: IDFS events 6.2% vs 12.5%, HR 0.47 (95% CI 0.34-0.66), P<0.001; 3-yr IDFS 92.4% vs 83.7%. 3-yr DFS 92.3% vs 83.5%, HR 0.47. OS immature (47 deaths total).
trials.toxicity: T-DXd: nausea 71.3%, constipation 32%, neutropenia 31.6%, vomiting 31%. T-DM1: AST/ALT rise, thrombocytopenia. Adjudicated drug-related ILD 9.6% vs 1.6%; 2 ILD deaths with T-DXd.
trials.reference: Loibl S et al. NEJM 2025;394:845
highlights: Halves IDFS risk vs T-DM1 (HR 0.47) in high-risk residual disease
3-yr IDFS 92.4% vs 83.7%
ILD 9.6% vs 1.6%, 2 deaths; FDA approval May 15, 2026
trials.takeaway: For high-risk residual HER2+ disease after neoadjuvant therapy, T-DXd beats T-DM1 on IDFS, replacing KATHERINE-style T-DM1, with ILD monitoring required.

trials.name: DESTINY-Breast09
trials.descriptor: 1l t-dxd + pertuzumab vs thp
trials.population: HER2+ advanced/metastatic BC, no prior chemo or HER2-directed therapy for metastatic disease (prior (neo)adjuvant HER2 therapy >6 mo before allowed; 1 prior line of ET allowed)
trials.arms: T-DXd + pertuzumab vs T-DXd + placebo vs THP (taxane + trastuzumab + pertuzumab) (1:1:1)
trials.results: Interim (cutoff Feb 26, 2025): median PFS 40.7 vs 26.9 mo, HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.44-0.71), P<0.00001. Confirmed ORR 85.1% vs 78.6% (CR 15.1% vs 8.5%); median DoR 39.2 vs 26.4 mo. OS immature. T-DXd + placebo (monotherapy) arm remains blinded until final PFS analysis.
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 63.5% vs 62.3%. Adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis 12.1% with T-DXd + P (2 grade 5) vs 1.0% with THP.
trials.reference: Tolaney SM et al. NEJM 2025;394:551
highlights: First major change to 1L HER2+ mBC since CLEOPATRA
PFS 40.7 vs 26.9 mo (HR 0.56); OS immature
T-DXd monotherapy arm still blinded; ILD 12.1% incl 2 deaths; FDA approval Dec 15, 2025
trials.takeaway: T-DXd + pertuzumab significantly prolongs PFS over THP as first-line therapy for HER2+ mBC, at the cost of ~12% ILD; OS and the monotherapy comparison are pending.

trials.name: DESTINY-Breast11
trials.descriptor: neoadjuvant t-dxd then thp vs ddac then thp
trials.population: High-risk HER2+ early BC (>=cT3 N0 or cT0-4 N1-3)
trials.arms: T-DXd x4 -> THP x4 vs ddAC x4 -> THP x4 vs T-DXd x8 (1:1:1); T-DXd-alone arm closed early on IDMC recommendation
trials.results: pCR 67.3% (T-DXd-THP) vs 56.3% (ddAC-THP), difference 11.2% (95% CI 4.0-18.3), P=0.003; HR+ 61.4% vs 52.3%, HR- 83.1% vs 67.1%. T-DXd alone x8: pCR 43.0% (enrollment closed early). EFS immature (4.5% maturity), HR 0.56 (0.26-1.17).
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 37.5% vs 55.8% (T-DXd alone 22.6%); serious AEs 10.6% vs 20.2%; LV dysfunction 1.3% vs 6.1%. Adjudicated ILD 4.4% vs 5.1% (T-DXd alone 4.9%).
trials.reference: Harbeck N et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:166 (epub Oct 2025)
highlights: Anthracycline-free T-DXd-THP raises pCR 67.3% vs 56.3%
T-DXd alone arm stopped early (pCR 43.0%)
Less grade >=3 toxicity and cardiotoxicity; EFS immature; FDA approval May 15, 2026
trials.takeaway: Neoadjuvant T-DXd x4 then THP gives a higher pCR with less toxicity than ddAC-THP in high-risk HER2+ early BC, though EFS is still immature.

trials.name: EMBER-3
trials.descriptor: imlunestrant +/- abemaciclib vs standard endocrine therapy
trials.population: ER+/HER2- ABC recurring/progressing on or after AI alone or with CDK4/6i; ESR1m (n=256) by ctDNA
trials.arms: 1:1:1 imlunestrant 400 mg PO daily vs SOC endocrine monotherapy (fulvestrant or exemestane) vs imlunestrant + abemaciclib (150 mg BID)
trials.primary_endpoint: Investigator-assessed PFS: imlunestrant vs SOC in ESR1m and in all patients; imlunestrant-abemaciclib vs imlunestrant in all concurrently randomized
trials.results: ESR1m: median PFS 5.5 vs 3.8 mo, HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.46-0.82), P=.0008 (HR per FDA; abstract reports RMST 7.9 vs 5.4 mo, P<0.001). All patients: 5.6 vs 5.5 mo, HR 0.87 (0.72-1.04), P=0.12 - NOT significant. Imlunestrant-abemaciclib vs imlunestrant (n=426): 9.4 vs 5.5 mo, HR 0.57 (0.44-0.73), P<0.001, regardless of ESR1 status. FDA exploratory ESR1m subgroup for combo: 11.1 vs 5.5 mo, HR 0.53 (0.35-0.80). OS immature.
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 17.1% imlunestrant, 20.7% SOC, 48.6% imlunestrant-abemaciclib (abemaciclib diarrhea, neutropenia).
trials.reference: Jhaveri KL et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392(12):1189-1202
highlights: Imlunestrant beat SOC only in ESR1m (5.5 vs 3.8 mo, HR 0.62); no benefit in overall population
Imlunestrant + abemaciclib 9.4 vs 5.5 mo vs imlunestrant alone, HR 0.57
FDA: imlunestrant monotherapy approved 25 Sep 2025 (ESR1m, after >=1 line ET); + abemaciclib approved 18 Sep 2026 but only for ESR1m
trials.takeaway: Imlunestrant is an oral SERD option for ESR1-mutated disease after endocrine therapy, and an all-oral SERD + abemaciclib combination is now approved for ESR1-mutated patients.

trials.name: EUROPA
trials.setting: Post-BCS single-modality therapy, age >=70 luminal A-like stage I
trials.descriptor: exclusive RT vs exclusive endocrine therapy
trials.population: 731 women >=70 y with stage I luminal A-like breast cancer after BCS (interim analysis n=207 with 24-mo HRQOL)
trials.arms: Radiotherapy alone (whole or partial breast, 5-15 fractions) vs endocrine therapy alone (AI or tamoxifen 5-10 y) (1:1)
trials.primary_endpoint: Co-primary: change in HRQOL (EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status) at 24 mo; 5-yr ipsilateral breast tumor recurrence (IBTR, not yet reported)
trials.results: Preplanned interim (median 23.9 mo): adjusted mean GHS change -3.40 with RT vs -9.79 with ET; difference 6.39 (95% CI 0.14-12.65), P=0.045 favoring RT. IBTR (co-primary) not yet reported - disease control unknown.
trials.toxicity: Treatment-related AEs 67% RT vs 85% ET; grade 3-4 arthralgia 7% with ET vs 0 with RT; SAEs 15% in both; no treatment-related deaths.
trials.reference: Meattini I et al. Lancet Oncol 2025;26:37-50 (interim analysis; epub Dec 2024; PMID 39675376)
highlights: HRQOL better preserved with RT alone: GHS difference 6.39 (P=0.045)
Treatment-related AEs 67% RT vs 85% ET
IBTR co-primary not yet reported - interim only
trials.takeaway: In women >=70 with luminal A-like stage I disease after BCS, RT alone preserved quality of life better than endocrine therapy alone at 2 years, but recurrence data are pending.

trials.name: INSEMA
trials.setting: Axillary staging, cT1-2 cN0 undergoing breast-conserving surgery
trials.descriptor: omission of sentinel node biopsy
trials.population: 5502 randomized patients with clinically node-negative invasive breast cancer, T1-T2 (<=5 cm) planned for BCS (90% cT1); per-protocol 4858
trials.arms: No axillary surgery vs sentinel lymph node biopsy (1:4)
trials.results: Median 73.6 mo: 5-yr iDFS 91.9% (89.9-93.5) omission vs 91.7% (90.8-92.6) SLNB; HR 0.91 (0.73-1.14), noninferior. Axillary recurrence 1.0% vs 0.3%; deaths 1.4% vs 2.4%.
trials.toxicity: Omission: less lymphedema, greater arm mobility, less arm/shoulder pain vs SLNB.
trials.reference: Reimer T et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392:1051-1064 (epub Dec 2024; PMID 39665649)
highlights: 5-yr iDFS 91.9% vs 91.7%, HR 0.91 - noninferior
Axillary recurrence 1.0% vs 0.3%
Mostly T1 (79% pT1), BCS + whole-breast RT population
trials.takeaway: In clinically node-negative T1-2 (mostly T1) patients having BCS, omitting SLNB is noninferior for iDFS with less arm morbidity.

trials.name: SERENA-6
trials.setting: HR+/HER2- metastatic, 1st line (ctDNA-guided switch before radiographic progression)
trials.descriptor: ctdna-guided switch to camizestrant on emergent esr1 mutation during 1l ai + cdk4/6i
trials.population: ER+/HER2- ABC on >=6 mo of 1L AI + CDK4/6i (palbociclib, ribociclib or abemaciclib) with ctDNA ESR1 testing every 2-3 mo; ESR1 mutation detected without radiologic progression. 3256 tested, 315 randomized
trials.arms: Switch to camizestrant 75 mg PO daily + continued CDK4/6i (+ AI placebo) vs continue AI + CDK4/6i (+ camizestrant placebo); double-blind
trials.results: Interim analysis, median f/u 12.6 mo: median PFS 16.0 (95% CI 12.7-18.2) vs 9.2 mo (7.2-9.5), HR 0.44 (0.31-0.60), P<0.0001. Time to deterioration in global QoL 21.0 vs 6.4 mo, HR 0.54 (0.34-0.84). OS immature.
trials.toxicity: Discontinuation for AEs 1.3% vs 1.9%. Label: boxed warning for arrhythmia from QTc prolongation with concomitant QT-prolonging drugs; bradycardia; embryo-fetal toxicity.
trials.reference: Bidard FC et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393(6):569-580
highlights: First phase 3 trial of switching therapy on molecular (ctDNA ESR1) progression before imaging progression
PFS 16.0 vs 9.2 mo, HR 0.44; OS immature, no crossover
ODAC voted 6-3 on 30 Apr 2026 that benefit was not clinically meaningful; FDA nevertheless granted ACCELERATED approval 4 Sep 2026 (Etcamah) with a CDK4/6i, Guardant360 CDx
trials.takeaway: Switching to camizestrant at ctDNA ESR1 emergence doubled PFS, but whether acting on molecular progression improves survival is unproven, so approval is accelerated and contested.

trials.name: TROPION-Breast01
trials.setting: HR+/HER2- metastatic, after ET and 1-2 chemo lines
trials.descriptor: datopotamab deruxtecan vs investigator's choice chemotherapy
trials.population: Inoperable/metastatic HR+/HER2- BC progressed on (or unsuitable for) endocrine therapy with 1-2 prior chemo lines in the metastatic setting
trials.arms: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Trop-2 ADC) 6 mg/kg IV q3w vs investigator's choice (eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine or gemcitabine)
trials.primary_endpoint: Dual: PFS by BICR and OS
trials.results: PFS by BICR HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.76), P<.0001 (median 6.9 vs 4.9 mo per FDA/secondary sources; medians not in abstract). Final OS (Ann Oncol 2025, median f/u 22.8 mo): HR 1.01 (0.83-1.22), P=0.9445 - NOT significant (medians reported as 18.6 vs 18.3 mo in secondary sources). Subsequent ADC use imbalanced: 12.3% vs 24.0%.
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 TRAEs 20.8% vs 44.7%. Most common: nausea 51.1% (grade >=3 1.4%), stomatitis 50% (grade >=3 6.4%); ICC neutropenia 42.5% (grade >=3 30.8%). Class risks: ocular surface toxicity (keratitis/dry eye), ILD/pneumonitis.
trials.reference: Bardia A et al. J Clin Oncol 2025;43(3):285-296; final OS Pistilli B et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37(5):663-674 (PMID 41448362)
highlights: PFS benefit (HR 0.63) with half the grade >=3 toxicity of chemo (20.8% vs 44.7%)
Dual primary OS endpoint FAILED: HR 1.01, possibly confounded by more post-study ADCs in chemo arm
FDA approved 17 Jan 2025 (Datroway) after prior ET + chemo for metastatic disease; stomatitis prophylaxis + eye care key
trials.takeaway: Dato-DXd improves PFS and tolerability over chemotherapy in pretreated HR+/HER2- disease but did not improve overall survival.

trials.name: ASCENT-04/KEYNOTE-D19
trials.descriptor: sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab vs chemo + pembrolizumab, 1l pd-l1+ mtnbc
trials.population: Previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic TNBC with PD-L1 CPS>=10 (22C3); randomized 1:1
trials.arms: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg d1, d8 q21d + pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w vs chemo (paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, or gemcitabine + carboplatin) + pembrolizumab
trials.results: PFS 11.2 vs 7.8 mo, HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51-0.84), P<0.001. ORR 60% vs 53%; DOR 16.5 vs 9.2 mo. OS immature. FDA approval Jun 24 2026 (SG + pembrolizumab, 1L TNBC with PD-L1 CPS>=10).
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 71% vs 70%; discontinuation for AEs 12% vs 31%; fatal AEs 3% each arm
trials.reference: Tolaney SM et al. N Engl J Med 2026;394:354-66
highlights: Replacing chemo with SG on a pembrolizumab backbone: PFS 11.2 vs 7.8 mo, HR 0.65
Fewer discontinuations for AEs (12% vs 31%)
OS immature; FDA approved Jun 2026 for CPS>=10
trials.takeaway: For 1L PD-L1 CPS>=10 metastatic TNBC, sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab improves PFS over chemotherapy + pembrolizumab; OS is immature.

trials.name: PATINA
trials.setting: 1L maintenance HR+/HER2+ metastatic after induction chemo + anti-HER2
trials.descriptor: palbociclib added to anti-HER2 + ET maintenance
trials.population: 518 patients with HR+/HER2+ MBC without progression after 4-8 cycles of chemotherapy + HER2-targeted therapy
trials.arms: Maintenance trastuzumab (+/- pertuzumab) + ET with palbociclib vs without palbociclib (open-label, 1:1; 261 vs 257)
trials.results: At median f/u 53.5 mo: PFS 44.3 vs 29.1 mo, HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.59-0.96), two-sided P=0.02. OS immature/not reported in abstract.
trials.toxicity: Grade 3 AEs 79.7% vs 30.6%, grade 4 10.0% vs 3.6%, predominantly neutropenia.
trials.reference: Metzger O et al. N Engl J Med 2026;394:451-62 (PMID 41604639)
highlights: 15-month median PFS gain: 44.3 vs 29.1 mo
Open-label; OS not yet reported; more neutropenia
trials.takeaway: Adding palbociclib to maintenance anti-HER2 + ET after induction significantly prolongs PFS in HR+/HER2+ MBC.

trials.name: TROPION-Breast02
trials.descriptor: dato-dxd vs chemo, 1l mtnbc not io candidates
trials.population: Previously untreated locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic TNBC for whom immunotherapy was not an option; stratified by region, DFI, PD-L1; randomized 1:1
trials.arms: Datopotamab deruxtecan 6 mg/kg IV q3w vs investigator's choice chemo (mostly nab-paclitaxel or paclitaxel; also eribulin, capecitabine, carboplatin)
trials.primary_endpoint: Dual primary: PFS by BICR and OS
trials.results: PFS 10.8 vs 5.6 mo, HR 0.57 (99% CI 0.44-0.73), P<0.0001. OS 23.7 vs 18.7 mo, HR 0.79 (95.01% CI 0.64-0.98), P=0.029, significant. ORR 64% vs 30% (FDA). FDA approval May 22 2026 for unresectable or metastatic TNBC not candidates for PD-1/PD-L1 therapy.
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs 33% vs 29%; discontinuation 4% vs 7%; no treatment-related deaths. Label warnings: ILD/pneumonitis, ocular toxicity (keratitis), stomatitis/mucositis
trials.reference: Dent R et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:1066-80
highlights: First ADC to improve both PFS and OS in 1L TNBC not eligible for IO: OS 23.7 vs 18.7 mo, HR 0.79
PFS nearly doubled: 10.8 vs 5.6 mo, HR 0.57
Watch for stomatitis, ocular toxicity, and ILD
trials.takeaway: For 1L metastatic TNBC not eligible for PD-(L)1 therapy, Dato-DXd improves both PFS and OS over chemotherapy and is FDA-approved (May 2026).

trials.name: OPTIMOX1
trials.descriptor: stop-and-go oxaliplatin to limit neuropathy
trials.population: Untreated metastatic colorectal cancer
trials.arms: FOLFOX4 until progression vs FOLFOX7 × 6 → sFU/LV maintenance × 12 → FOLFOX7 reintroduction
trials.results: PFS 9.0 vs 8.7 mo and OS 19.3 vs 21.2 mo (NS); response 58.5% vs 59.2%; grade 3 neuropathy 17.9% vs 13.3%; oxaliplatin reintroduced in only 40% but achieved response or stabilization in 69% of them
trials.reference: Tournigand C et al. JCO 2006;24:394
highlights: Oxaliplatin can be stopped after ~3–4 months and reintroduced without losing efficacy — the basis for planned oxaliplatin holidays in metastatic disease.
OPTIMOX2 later showed that stopping all chemotherapy (complete break) is worse than fluoropyrimidine maintenance.
trials.takeaway: Planned oxaliplatin stop-and-go preserves efficacy and limits neuropathy in metastatic CRC

trials.name: TRIBE
trials.descriptor: FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab vs FOLFIRI + bevacizumab
trials.population: Untreated unresectable metastatic colorectal cancer, age ≤75, ECOG ≤2 (≤1 if 71–75)
trials.arms: FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab vs FOLFIRI + bevacizumab (induction × 12, then 5-FU/bev maintenance)
trials.results: PFS 12.1 vs 9.7 mo (HR 0.75); ORR 65% vs 53%; OS 31.0 vs 25.8 mo (HR 0.79, p=0.054; updated 29.8 vs 25.8, HR 0.80). BRAF-mutant: OS 19.0 vs 10.7 mo (n=28)
trials.toxicity: Grade 3–4 neutropenia 50% vs 20%, diarrhea 19% vs 11%, neuropathy 5% vs 0%
trials.reference: Loupakis F et al. NEJM 2014;371:1609; Cremolini C et al. Lancet Oncol 2015 (OS)
highlights: Triplet chemotherapy + bevacizumab improves PFS, ORR and OS for fit patients — favored for right-sided or RAS-mutant disease and when downsizing matters.
Toxicity limits it to fit patients ≤75; the BRAF signal was hypothesis-generating and superseded by BREAKWATER.
trials.takeaway: FOLFOXIRI + bevacizumab improves PFS, response and OS over FOLFIRI + bevacizumab in fit patients

trials.name: IDEA collaboration
trials.descriptor: 3 vs 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy
trials.population: Stage III colon cancer after resection (pooled analysis of 6 randomized trials)
trials.arms: 3 months vs 6 months of FOLFOX or CAPOX (regimen chosen by investigator)
trials.results: 3-yr DFS 74.6% vs 75.5% (HR 1.07) — failed non-inferiority overall. CAPOX: 3 mo non-inferior (HR 0.95); FOLFOX: 6 mo better (HR 1.16). Low-risk (T1–3 N1): 3 mo non-inferior; high-risk (T4 or N2): 6 mo favored
trials.toxicity: Grade ≥2 neuropathy 16.6% (3 mo) vs 47.7% (6 mo)
trials.reference: Grothey A et al. NEJM 2018;378:1177
highlights: 3 months of CAPOX is acceptable for low-risk stage III (T1–3 N1); FOLFOX or high-risk disease (T4 and/or N2) favors 6 months.
Neuropathy is the currency — 6 months triples persistent oxaliplatin neuropathy.
trials.takeaway: 3 months of adjuvant CAPOX is non-inferior for low-risk stage III; FOLFOX and high-risk disease favor 6 months

trials.name: BEACON CRC
trials.descriptor: encorafenib + cetuximab ± binimetinib after prior therapy, BRAF V600E
trials.population: BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic CRC after 1–2 prior regimens
trials.arms: Encorafenib + binimetinib + cetuximab (triplet) vs encorafenib + cetuximab (doublet) vs irinotecan/FOLFIRI + cetuximab (control)
trials.results: Primary: OS triplet 9.0 vs control 5.4 mo (HR 0.52); doublet 8.4 mo (HR 0.60); ORR 26% / 20% / 2%. Updated (JCO 2021): OS 9.3 / 9.3 / 5.9 mo. Doublet became the approved standard (MEK adds toxicity, not survival)
trials.toxicity: Diarrhea, dermatitis acneiform, nausea; more GI/ocular toxicity with binimetinib
trials.reference: Kopetz S et al. NEJM 2019;381:1632; JCO 2021 (updated)
highlights: First targeted regimen to improve OS in BRAF V600E CRC — BRAF inhibition needs EGFR blockade (feedback reactivation), unlike melanoma.
Now the second-line option after BREAKWATER took the combination first line.
trials.takeaway: Encorafenib + cetuximab improves OS vs chemo in previously treated BRAF V600E metastatic CRC

trials.name: KEYNOTE-177
trials.descriptor: first-line pembrolizumab vs chemotherapy, MSI-H metastatic CRC
trials.population: Untreated MSI-H/dMMR metastatic colorectal cancer
trials.arms: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk vs investigator's-choice chemotherapy (FOLFOX/FOLFIRI ± bevacizumab or cetuximab); crossover allowed
trials.results: PFS 16.5 vs 8.2 mo (HR 0.60); ORR 43.8% vs 33.1%; OS HR 0.74 (NS, 60% crossover); 5-yr OS 54.8% vs 44.2%
trials.toxicity: Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs 22% vs 66%
trials.reference: André T et al. NEJM 2020;383:2207; Diaz LA et al. Lancet Oncol 2022 (OS)
highlights: Pembrolizumab is the first-line standard for MSI-H metastatic CRC — doubles PFS with far less toxicity.
Note early crossover of curves: ~30% progress early on pembrolizumab; chemo-first is reasonable if rapid control is needed.
trials.takeaway: First-line pembrolizumab doubles PFS in MSI-H metastatic colorectal cancer

trials.name: ATOMIC (Alliance A021502)
trials.descriptor: atezolizumab added to adjuvant FOLFOX, stage III dMMR
trials.population: Resected stage III dMMR/MSI-H colon cancer
trials.arms: mFOLFOX6 × 12 + atezolizumab (during and 6 months after chemo) vs mFOLFOX6 × 12
trials.reference: Sinicrope FA et al. ASCO 2025 LBA1; NEJM 2025
highlights: First positive adjuvant immunotherapy trial in colon cancer — dMMR stage III now gets FOLFOX + atezolizumab.
Test MMR/MSI on every newly diagnosed colon cancer; it now changes adjuvant therapy, not just metastatic.
trials.takeaway: Adding atezolizumab to adjuvant FOLFOX halves recurrence risk in stage III dMMR colon cancer

trials.name: BREAKWATER
trials.descriptor: encorafenib + cetuximab + mFOLFOX6 first-line, BRAF V600E metastatic CRC
trials.population: Untreated BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer
trials.arms: Encorafenib + cetuximab + mFOLFOX6 vs encorafenib + cetuximab vs standard chemotherapy ± bevacizumab
trials.results: ORR 60.9% vs 40.0% (triplet+chemo vs control); median OS 30.3 vs 15.1 mo (HR 0.49); PFS 12.8 vs 7.1 mo (HR 0.53)
trials.toxicity: Neutropenia, nausea, anemia, dermatologic (cetuximab)
trials.reference: Kopetz S et al. Nat Med 2025 (ORR); Elez E et al. NEJM 2025 (PFS/OS); FDA accelerated approval Dec 2024
highlights: Moved BRAF-targeted therapy from second line (BEACON) to first line, combined with FOLFOX — doubling median OS.
Test BRAF up front; a BRAF V600E patient should not start bevacizumab-based chemo alone.
trials.takeaway: First-line encorafenib + cetuximab + FOLFOX doubles OS in BRAF V600E metastatic CRC

trials.name: KEYNOTE-048
trials.descriptor: first-line recurrent/metastatic HNSCC
trials.population: 1L recurrent/metastatic HNSCC (oral cavity, oropharynx, hypopharynx, larynx), not curable by local therapy; stratified by PD-L1 CPS
trials.arms: (1) pembrolizumab monotherapy; (2) pembrolizumab + platinum (cis/carbo) + 5-FU; (3) EXTREME = cetuximab + platinum + 5-FU
trials.primary_endpoint: OS + PFS (tested across CPS ≥20, CPS ≥1, total population)
trials.results: Pembro+chemo vs EXTREME OS 13.0 vs 10.7 mo (HR 0.77); CPS≥20 14.7 vs 11.0 (HR 0.60), CPS≥1 13.6 vs 10.4 (HR 0.65). Pembro mono OS: CPS≥20 14.9 vs 10.7 (HR 0.61), CPS≥1 12.3 vs 10.3 (HR 0.78); non-inferior in total population
trials.reference: Burtness B et al. Lancet 2019;394:1915; Harrington KJ et al. JCO 2023 (5-yr)
highlights: Established pembrolizumab-based, CPS-driven therapy as 1L SOC for R/M HNSCC, displacing EXTREME.
CPS ≥1 → pembrolizumab (± chemo); high CPS (≥20) → monotherapy reasonable; CPS <1 → pembro + chemo.
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab ± chemo is 1L SOC for R/M HNSCC, chosen by PD-L1 CPS

trials.name: KEYNOTE-689
trials.descriptor: perioperative pembrolizumab, resectable LA HNSCC
trials.population: Newly diagnosed, resectable, locally advanced (stage III/IVA) HNSCC
trials.arms: Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab → surgery → adjuvant pembrolizumab + SOC RT (± cisplatin) → maintenance pembrolizumab, vs SOC alone (surgery + adjuvant RT ± cisplatin)
trials.results: CPS≥10: 3-yr EFS 59.8% vs 45.9% (HR 0.66, p=0.004). CPS≥1: HR 0.70 (p=0.003). Total: HR 0.73 (p=0.008), median EFS 51.8 vs 30.4 mo. ↑ major pathologic response; DMFS 51.8 vs 35.7 mo
trials.reference: Uppaluri R et al. NEJM 2025 (Jun 18); NEJMoa2415434
highlights: First positive perioperative immunotherapy trial in resectable LA HNSCC — establishes neoadjuvant + adjuvant pembrolizumab as a practice-changing new standard.
trials.takeaway: Perioperative pembrolizumab improves EFS in resectable locally advanced HNSCC

trials.name: SWOG 8736
trials.descriptor: CHOP ×3 + involved-field RT vs CHOP ×8 in localized intermediate/high-grade NHL
trials.population: Stage I, IE, or non-bulky II/IIE intermediate- or high-grade NHL (Working Formulation); 401 eligible (200 CHOP+RT, 201 CHOP)
trials.arms: CHOP ×3 → involved-field RT 40-55 Gy vs CHOP ×8 alone
trials.results: 5-yr PFS 77% vs 64% (P=0.03); 5-yr OS 82% vs 72% (P=0.02). Life-threatening toxicity 61/200 vs 80/201 (P=0.06); decreased LVEF in 7 CHOP-alone patients vs 0 (P=0.02). Long-term SWOG follow-up (Stephens, JCO 2016) showed the curves crossing at ~7-9 yr with no lasting advantage
trials.toxicity: Less life-threatening toxicity and no cardiac events with the abbreviated arm
trials.reference: Miller TP et al. NEJM 1998;339:21
highlights: Established abbreviated chemotherapy + radiation as an option for localized aggressive NHL
Pre-rituximab, and the early PFS/OS advantage did not persist — it no longer defines modern practice
trials.takeaway: Three cycles of CHOP with involved-field RT beat eight cycles of CHOP at 5 years in localized aggressive NHL, but the advantage disappeared with longer follow-up.

trials.name: GELA LNH-98.5
trials.descriptor: R-CHOP vs CHOP in previously untreated DLBCL age 60-80
trials.population: Untreated DLBCL, age 60-80, stage II-IV; 399 randomized (202 R-CHOP, 197 CHOP); 60% aaIPI 2-3
trials.arms: CHOP ×8 q21d vs the same plus rituximab 375 mg/m² on day 1 of each cycle
trials.results: At median 2 yr: CR 76% vs 63% (P=0.005); EFS P<0.001 and OS P=0.007; risk ratio 0.58 (95% CI 0.44-0.77) for treatment failure and 0.64 (0.45-0.89) for death. 10-yr update (Coiffier, Blood 2010;116:2040): PFS 36.5% vs 20%, OS 43.5% vs 27.6%, with equal second cancers and non-lymphoma deaths
trials.toxicity: No clinically relevant increase in toxicity with rituximab, and no excess late toxicity at 10 years
trials.reference: Coiffier B et al. NEJM 2002;346:235
highlights: Established R-CHOP as the global standard of care in DLBCL
An absolute ~16% overall survival gain at 10 years that no chemotherapy backbone has improved on since
trials.takeaway: Adding rituximab to CHOP raised complete response, event-free and overall survival in elderly DLBCL, and the benefit held at ten years.

trials.name: CALGB 50202
trials.descriptor: MT-R induction then EA consolidation, omitting whole-brain radiotherapy, in newly diagnosed PCNSL
trials.population: 44 patients with newly diagnosed primary CNS lymphoma, multicenter
trials.arms: Single arm, two steps: methotrexate 8 g/m² + temozolomide + rituximab induction, then etoposide + cytarabine consolidation in responders. No whole-brain radiotherapy
trials.primary_endpoint: Complete response rate to MT-R induction
trials.results: CR to induction 66%. At median follow-up 4.9 yr, 2-yr PFS 0.57 overall; 2-yr time to progression 0.59 overall and 0.77 among those completing consolidation. Patients over 60 did as well as younger ones; treatment delay was the strongest adverse prognostic variable
trials.toxicity: Dose-intensive consolidation proved feasible outside a single center; myelosuppression predominated
trials.reference: Rubenstein JL et al. JCO 2013;31:3061
highlights: First multicenter demonstration that dose-intensive consolidation without whole-brain radiotherapy is feasible in PCNSL
Directly motivated CALGB 51101, which randomized this consolidation against autologous transplant
trials.takeaway: MT-R induction with etoposide-cytarabine consolidation achieved outcomes comparable to radiation-containing regimens while sparing the brain from radiotherapy.

trials.name: IELSG32 / MATRix
trials.descriptor: methotrexate/cytarabine ± rituximab ± thiotepa induction in newly diagnosed PCNSL
trials.population: HIV-negative, age 18-70, newly diagnosed PCNSL with measurable disease, ECOG 0-3; 227 enrolled at 53 centers in 5 countries, 219 assessable
trials.arms: 1:1:1 — methotrexate 3.5 g/m² + cytarabine 2 g/m² BID; the same plus rituximab; or the same plus rituximab and thiotepa 30 mg/m² (MATRix). Four courses q21d, then a second randomization to whole-brain radiotherapy or autologous transplant
trials.primary_endpoint: Complete remission rate after induction (first randomization)
trials.results: At median follow-up 30 mo: CR 49% (95% CI 38-60) with MATRix vs 23% (14-31) with methotrexate-cytarabine (HR 0.46, 0.28-0.74) and 30% (21-42) with the rituximab doublet (HR 0.61, 0.40-0.94). Thirteen toxic deaths (6%). Second randomization (Lancet Haematol 2017;4:e510): 2-yr PFS 80% with radiotherapy vs 69% with transplant, HR 1.50, P=0.17 — no significant difference. At 7 years OS was 21% / 37% / 56% across the three induction arms
trials.toxicity: Grade 4 hematologic toxicity most frequent with MATRix; infective complications similar across arms; 6% toxic mortality
trials.reference: Ferreri AJM et al. Lancet Haematol 2016;3:e217
highlights: Established MATRix as the standard induction backbone for PCNSL in patients up to age 70
A randomized phase 2, not a phase 3, and 6% toxic mortality limits its use in frail or older patients
trials.takeaway: Adding rituximab and thiotepa to methotrexate-cytarabine doubled the complete remission rate in PCNSL and made MATRix the standard induction.

trials.name: FLYER
trials.descriptor: 4 cycles R-CHOP + 2 rituximab vs 6 cycles R-CHOP in young favorable-prognosis aggressive B-NHL
trials.population: Age 18-60, stage I-II, normal LDH, ECOG 0-1, no bulk (<7.5 cm), aaIPI 0; 588 in the ITT analysis
trials.arms: R-CHOP ×6 vs CHOP ×4 + rituximab ×6 (4 R-CHOP then 2 rituximab alone), q21d; no planned RT except testicular
trials.results: 3-yr PFS 96% (95% CI 94-99) with 4 cycles vs 93% with 6 — difference +3%, lower bound 0%, non-inferiority met at median follow-up 66 mo. 3-yr OS 99% vs 98%. Adverse events roughly a third lower: 294 hematologic + 1,036 non-hematologic vs 426 + 1,280. Both on-therapy deaths were in the 6-cycle arm
trials.toxicity: Substantially less hematologic and non-hematologic toxicity with 4 cycles
trials.reference: Poeschel V et al. Lancet 2019;394:2271
highlights: Made 4×R-CHOP + 2 rituximab standard for young aaIPI-0 non-bulky DLBCL
Applies only to that narrow favorable subset — age ≤60, stage I-II, normal LDH, no bulk
trials.takeaway: Four cycles of R-CHOP plus two extra rituximab doses is non-inferior to six cycles in young favorable-risk DLBCL, with less toxicity.

trials.name: GO29365 (pola-BR)
trials.descriptor: polatuzumab vedotin + bendamustine/rituximab vs bendamustine/rituximab in transplant-ineligible R/R DLBCL
trials.population: Transplant-ineligible R/R DLBCL; randomized cohort of 80 (40 per arm)
trials.arms: Polatuzumab 1.8 mg/kg + bendamustine 90 mg/m² + rituximab 375 mg/m² q21d ×6 vs BR ×6
trials.primary_endpoint: Complete response rate at end of treatment by independent review
trials.results: CR at end of treatment 40.0% vs 17.5% (P=0.026). Median PFS 9.5 vs 3.7 mo, HR 0.36 (95% CI 0.21-0.63), P<0.001; median OS 12.4 vs 4.7 mo, HR 0.42 (0.24-0.75), P=0.002, at median follow-up 22.3 mo. A 106-patient extension cohort gave ORR 41.5%, CR 38.7%
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 neutropenia 46.2% vs 33.3%, thrombocytopenia 41% vs 23.1%; peripheral neuropathy 43.6%, grade 1-2 and mostly reversible
trials.reference: Sehn LH et al. JCO 2020;38:155
highlights: Basis for approval of pola-BR in R/R DLBCL after ≥2 prior lines
Only 40 patients per randomized arm — a very small dataset for a registrational survival claim
trials.takeaway: Adding polatuzumab to bendamustine-rituximab more than doubled complete responses and roughly tripled median survival in transplant-ineligible R/R DLBCL.

trials.name: L-MIND
trials.descriptor: single-arm tafasitamab + lenalidomide in transplant-ineligible relapsed/refractory DLBCL
trials.population: R/R DLBCL after 1-3 prior regimens including an anti-CD20, not ASCT candidates, ECOG 0-2; 81 treated at 35 sites
trials.arms: Single arm: tafasitamab 12 mg/kg IV + lenalidomide 25 mg PO d1-21 for up to 12 cycles, then tafasitamab alone q2wk until progression
trials.primary_endpoint: Best objective response rate by central review
trials.results: Primary (median follow-up 13.2 mo): ORR 60% (95% CI 48-71), CR 43%, PR 18% of 80 evaluable. Five-year final analysis (Duell, Haematologica 2024;109:553): ORR 57.5%, CR 41.3%, median PFS 11.6 mo, median OS 33.5 mo; by prior lines, ORR 67.5% after one line vs 47.5% after ≥2
trials.toxicity: Grade ≥3 neutropenia 48%, thrombocytopenia 17%, febrile neutropenia 12%; serious adverse events 51%
trials.reference: Salles G et al. Lancet Oncol 2020;21:978
highlights: Basis for accelerated approval of tafasitamab + lenalidomide in transplant-ineligible R/R DLBCL
Single-arm phase 2 of 80 patients, enriched for a single prior line — real-world third-line results are lower
trials.takeaway: Tafasitamab plus lenalidomide gave roughly 60% responses and 40% complete responses in transplant-ineligible R/R DLBCL, best after only one prior line.

trials.name: NCI 9177 (risk-adapted DA-EPOCH-R)
trials.descriptor: risk-adapted DA-EPOCH-R in untreated adult Burkitt lymphoma
trials.population: 113 adults with untreated Burkitt lymphoma at 22 centers, any HIV status; 87% high-risk, median age 49, 26% with marrow and/or CSF involvement, 25% HIV-positive
trials.arms: Single arm, risk-adapted: low risk → DA-EPOCH-R ×3 with no CNS prophylaxis; high risk → ×6 with intrathecal methotrexate. No cranial radiation
trials.results: At median follow-up 58.7 mo: EFS 84.5%, OS 87.0%. EFS 100% in low-risk and 82.1% in high-risk, with equivalent outcomes across age, HIV status and IPI. Five treatment-related deaths (4%); febrile neutropenia in 16% of cycles
trials.toxicity: Markedly less toxic than CODOX-M/IVAC or hyper-CVAD; 4% treatment-related mortality
trials.reference: Roschewski M et al. JCO 2020;38:2519
highlights: Made risk-adapted DA-EPOCH-R a standard option for adult Burkitt, including older and HIV-positive patients
Low-risk patients were cured with three cycles and no intrathecal prophylaxis; CSF involvement remains the unsolved problem
trials.takeaway: Risk-adapted DA-EPOCH-R cured about 85% of adults with Burkitt lymphoma regardless of age or HIV status, with far less toxicity than dose-intensive regimens.

trials.name: NP30179 (glofitamab)
trials.descriptor: fixed-duration glofitamab monotherapy after ≥2 prior lines
trials.population: R/R DLBCL with ≥2 prior lines; 155 enrolled, 154 treated; median 3 prior therapies, about a third with prior CAR-T, ~84% refractory to their last regimen
trials.arms: Single arm: obinutuzumab 1,000 mg pretreatment C1D1, glofitamab step-up 2.5 mg C1D8 and 10 mg C1D15, then 30 mg on day 1 of cycles 2-12 — fixed 12 cycles
trials.primary_endpoint: Complete response rate by independent review
trials.results: At median follow-up 12.6 mo: CR 39% (95% CI 32-48), ORR 52%; CR 35% among the 52 with prior CAR-T. Median time to CR 42 days; 78% of complete responses ongoing at 12 mo; 12-mo PFS 37%. Three-year update (Blood 2024): CR 40%, median duration of CR 29.8 mo
trials.toxicity: CRS 63% (grade ≥3 4%), grade ≥3 neurologic events 3%, discontinuation for adverse events 9%
trials.reference: Dickinson MJ et al. NEJM 2022;387:2220
highlights: Basis for approval of glofitamab in R/R DLBCL after ≥2 lines; the fixed 12-cycle course gives treatment-free remission
Obinutuzumab pretreatment is mandatory for CRS mitigation, and CRS is more frequent than with epcoritamab
trials.takeaway: Fixed-duration glofitamab gave a 39% complete response rate in heavily pretreated R/R DLBCL, with most remissions durable off therapy.

trials.name: POLARIX
trials.descriptor: pola-R-CHP vs R-CHOP in previously untreated intermediate/high-risk DLBCL
trials.population: Untreated DLBCL, age 18-80, IPI 2-5; 879 randomized (440 pola-R-CHP, 439 R-CHOP)
trials.arms: 6 cycles pola-R-CHP (polatuzumab replaces vincristine) + 2 rituximab vs 6 cycles R-CHOP + 2 rituximab; double-blind
trials.toxicity: Comparable grade ≥3 adverse events; peripheral neuropathy similar to R-CHOP and largely reversible
trials.reference: Tilly H et al. NEJM 2022;386:351
highlights: First regimen in two decades to beat R-CHOP on PFS; approved for IPI ≥2 DLBCL
No overall survival benefit; the gains concentrate in age >60, IPI 3-5 and non-GCB disease
trials.takeaway: Pola-R-CHP improved 2-year PFS over R-CHOP in IPI ≥2 DLBCL without any difference in overall survival.

trials.name: EPCORE NHL-1
trials.descriptor: subcutaneous epcoritamab monotherapy after ≥2 prior lines
trials.population: R/R CD20+ large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL, HGBCL, PMBCL, FL grade 3B) with ≥2 prior lines including anti-CD20; n=157, median 3 prior lines, 61.1% primary refractory, 38.9% prior CAR-T
trials.arms: Single arm: subcutaneous epcoritamab with step-up dosing in cycle 1 then 48 mg — weekly cycles 1-3, q2wk cycles 4-9, q4wk from cycle 10, until progression
trials.primary_endpoint: Overall response rate by independent review
trials.results: At median follow-up 10.7 mo: ORR 63.1% (95% CI 55.0-70.6), CR 38.9%; median duration of response 12.0 mo and not reached among complete responders. Two-year update (Leukemia 2024): ORR 63.1%, CR 40.1%, 24-mo PFS 27.8%, OS 44.6%
trials.toxicity: CRS 49.7% (grade 3 only 2.5%), ICANS 6.4% with one fatal event
trials.reference: Thieblemont C et al. JCO 2023;41:2238
highlights: Basis for approval of epcoritamab in R/R large B-cell lymphoma after ≥2 lines; the first subcutaneous bispecific in DLBCL
Retains activity after CAR-T, and is dosed continuously rather than for a fixed duration
trials.takeaway: Subcutaneous epcoritamab produced 63% responses and 39% complete responses in heavily pretreated large B-cell lymphoma, including after CAR-T.

trials.name: RAPID
trials.descriptor: involved-field radiotherapy vs no further therapy after ABVD ×3 in PET-negative stage IA/IIA cHL
trials.population: 602 recruited with newly diagnosed stage IA or IIA cHL; 571 scanned after 3 cycles, 426 PET-negative, 420 randomized. Median age 34
trials.arms: After ABVD ×3 and PET: involved-field RT vs no further treatment. PET-positive patients received a 4th cycle plus RT off-randomization
trials.primary_endpoint: Non-inferiority of no further treatment for 3-year PFS, excluding a difference of ≥7 percentage points
trials.results: Non-inferiority NOT demonstrated. 3-yr PFS 94.6% with RT vs 90.8% without; difference −3.8 points (95% CI −8.8 to 1.3), crossing the margin. Eight progressions and 8 deaths (1 from HL) with RT vs 20 progressions and 4 deaths (none from HL) without. Median follow-up 60 months
trials.toxicity: No lymphoma deaths in the RT-omission arm — the case for omission rests on avoiding late radiation toxicity
trials.reference: Radford J et al. NEJM 2015;372:1598
highlights: Widely cited as permission to omit radiation in PET-negative early-stage disease, but the trial formally failed its non-inferiority endpoint
Uses 3 cycles before PET, unlike the 2 in HD16 and H10 — the designs are not interchangeable
trials.takeaway: Omitting radiation after three cycles of ABVD in PET-negative early-stage Hodgkin costs about 4% of PFS and missed non-inferiority, with no lymphoma deaths either way.

trials.name: RATHL
trials.descriptor: drop bleomycin after a negative interim PET, escalate to BEACOPP if positive, in advanced cHL
trials.population: 1,214 registered with newly diagnosed advanced classic HL; 1,119 had a protocol interim PET after 2 cycles and 937 (83.7%) were PET-negative and randomized
trials.arms: PET-negative randomized to continue ABVD cycles 3-6 vs omit bleomycin (AVD). PET-positive escalated to BEACOPP-14 or escalated BEACOPP off-randomization
trials.primary_endpoint: 3-year PFS difference, non-inferiority excluding ≥5 percentage points
trials.results: Narrowly missed non-inferiority in the primary report: 3-yr PFS 85.7% with ABVD vs 84.4% with AVD, difference 1.6 points (95% CI −3.2 to 5.3) against a 5-point margin. 3-yr OS 97.2% vs 97.6%. PET-positive patients escalated to BEACOPP had 3-yr PFS 67.5%. At 7.3 years (Luminari, JCO 2024;42:13) the difference of 1.3 points (−3.0 to 4.7) falls inside the margin and non-inferiority is confirmed
trials.toxicity: Respiratory adverse events significantly more severe with continued bleomycin — the entire rationale for the strategy
trials.reference: Johnson P et al. NEJM 2016;374:2419
highlights: Established PET-adapted bleomycin omission as standard practice in advanced Hodgkin
Almost always quoted as a positive non-inferiority trial — it missed by a hair in 2016 and was only formally confirmed on the 2024 long-term analysis
trials.takeaway: After a negative interim PET in advanced Hodgkin, dropping bleomycin preserves efficacy and cuts pulmonary toxicity.

trials.name: EORTC/LYSA/FIL H10
trials.descriptor: PET-adapted therapy in stage I-II cHL — omit INRT if early PET-negative, escalate to escalated BEACOPP if positive
trials.population: 1,950 randomized with previously untreated stage I-II cHL, split into EORTC favorable and unfavorable strata; 1,925 evaluable by early PET after 2 cycles, of whom 18.8% were positive
trials.arms: Standard: ABVD (×3 favorable, ×4 unfavorable) + involved-node RT regardless of PET. Experimental: PET-negative → ABVD alone with no INRT; PET-positive → escalated BEACOPP ×2 + INRT
trials.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival — non-inferiority for the PET-negative comparison, superiority for the PET-positive one
trials.results: PET-positive: 5-yr PFS 90.6% with escalated BEACOPP + INRT vs 77.4%, HR 0.42 (0.23-0.74), P=.002 — superiority met. PET-negative: non-inferiority NOT shown in either stratum (favorable 99.0% vs 87.1%, HR 15.8; unfavorable 92.1% vs 89.6%, HR 1.45). At 10 years (Federico, JCO 2024;42:19) the BEACOPP advantage was no longer significant, HR 0.67 (0.37-1.20), P=.1777
trials.toxicity: Escalation was safe at 10 years with no excess late events or second malignancies
trials.reference: Andre M et al. JCO 2017;35:1786
highlights: The largest PET-adapted early-stage trial, and the third to fail non-inferiority for radiation omission
The benefit of escalating PET-positive patients to BEACOPP eroded with follow-up and is no longer significant at 10 years
trials.takeaway: Escalating PET-positive early-stage Hodgkin to BEACOPP helped at five years but not at ten, and omitting radiation in PET-negative patients again fell short of non-inferiority.

trials.name: ECHELON-1
trials.descriptor: brentuximab vedotin + AVD vs ABVD in untreated stage III/IV classic Hodgkin
trials.population: 1,334 patients with previously untreated stage III or IV classic HL
trials.arms: Up to six cycles of A+AVD vs ABVD, given on days 1 and 15 of 28-day cycles. Interim PET was required but not used to adapt therapy
trials.primary_endpoint: Modified progression-free survival by independent review — progression, death, or non-complete response followed by subsequent anticancer therapy
trials.results: 2-yr modified PFS 82.1% vs 77.2%, difference 4.9 points, HR 0.77 (0.60-0.98), P=0.04. At six years (Ansell, NEJM 2022;387:310) 39 vs 64 deaths, HR 0.59 (0.40-0.88), P=0.009; 6-yr OS 93.9% vs 89.4%; fewer second cancers (23 vs 32)
trials.toxicity: More febrile neutropenia, prompting mandatory primary G-CSF, and more peripheral neuropathy, most of which resolved. Avoids bleomycin lung toxicity
trials.reference: Connors JM et al. NEJM 2018;378:331
highlights: The first frontline advanced-Hodgkin regimen to show an overall survival benefit over ABVD — but only on the six-year update
The primary endpoint was modified PFS, a composite including non-complete response plus subsequent therapy, and the primary result was modest
Now itself displaced as first choice by nivolumab-AVD
trials.takeaway: A+AVD improved modified PFS over ABVD and, at six years, delivered a real survival advantage of 93.9% versus 89.4%.

trials.name: GHSG HD16
trials.descriptor: ABVD ×2 + 20 Gy IFRT vs ABVD ×2 alone in PET-2-negative early favorable classic HL
trials.population: 1,150 patients age 18-75 with newly diagnosed early-stage favorable cHL by GHSG criteria; PET after 2 cycles (PET-2). Per-protocol PET-2-negative cohort 628
trials.arms: Combined modality ABVD ×2 + 20 Gy involved-field RT vs PET-guided ABVD ×2 alone if PET-2 negative (Deauville <3)
trials.primary_endpoint: Dual — non-inferiority of 5-yr PFS for ABVD alone in PET-2-negative patients (per-protocol), and confirmation of PET-2 positivity as a risk factor
trials.results: Non-inferiority NOT shown. 5-yr PFS 93.4% with combined modality vs 86.1% with ABVD alone; difference 7.3% (1.6-13.0), HR 1.78 (1.02-3.12). 5-yr OS 98.1% vs 98.4% — no difference. Within the CMT arm, PET-2 positivity predicted worse PFS, more sharply at a Deauville ≥4 cutoff (93.1% vs 80.9%, P=.0011)
trials.toxicity: Radiation adds late-effect risk (second malignancy, cardiac) — the trade against a 7.3% PFS loss
trials.reference: Fuchs M et al. JCO 2019;37:2835
highlights: Kept ABVD ×2 + 20 Gy as standard for early favorable disease — a negative PET-2 does not license dropping radiation
Overall survival was identical at 98%, so omission remains defensible when late-effect risk is high, as in young women with mediastinal disease
trials.takeaway: In early favorable Hodgkin, omitting radiation after a negative interim PET costs 7.3% of PFS without changing survival.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-204
trials.descriptor: pembrolizumab vs brentuximab vedotin after or ineligible for autologous transplant
trials.population: 304 adults with relapsed/refractory classic HL at 78 centers in 20 countries, either relapsed after autologous transplant or ineligible for it; ECOG 0-1
trials.arms: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3wk vs brentuximab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg IV q3wk
trials.primary_endpoint: Dual primary — PFS by blinded independent review and overall survival; OS was not analyzed at this interim cutoff
trials.results: At median follow-up 25.7 months, median PFS 13.2 months (95% CI 10.9-19.4) with pembrolizumab vs 8.3 months (5.7-8.8) with brentuximab; HR 0.65 (0.48-0.88), P=0.0027
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-5 pneumonitis 4% with pembrolizumab vs 1%; neutropenia 2% vs 7%; one treatment-related death from pneumonia on pembrolizumab
trials.reference: Kuruvilla J et al. Lancet Oncol 2021;22:512
highlights: Made pembrolizumab preferred over brentuximab in relapsed disease after or without transplant
This is an interim analysis in which the co-primary OS endpoint was not analyzed, so no survival benefit has been shown
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab roughly doubled median PFS over brentuximab vedotin in relapsed/refractory Hodgkin, 13.2 versus 8.3 months.

trials.name: GHSG HD21
trials.descriptor: PET-guided BrECADD vs escalated BEACOPP in newly diagnosed advanced-stage cHL
trials.population: 1,500 adults aged ≤60 with newly diagnosed advanced cHL at 233 sites in 9 countries; median age 31
trials.arms: BrECADD vs escalated BEACOPP, 4 or 6 cycles at 21-day intervals with the number of cycles guided by PET after 2 cycles
trials.primary_endpoint: Hierarchical co-primary — first improved tolerability by treatment-related morbidity, then non-inferior PFS with a 6-point margin; superiority tested only if non-inferiority passed
trials.results: Both met, and superiority followed. Treatment-related morbidity 42% vs 59%, relative risk 0.72 (0.65-0.80), P<0.0001. At median 48 months, PFS HR 0.66 (0.45-0.97), P=0.035; 4-yr PFS 94.3% vs 90.9%. 4-yr OS 98.6% vs 98.2% — no difference
trials.toxicity: 17 absolute points less treatment-related morbidity than escalated BEACOPP; brentuximab brings neuropathy, BEACOPP brings gonadal toxicity
trials.reference: Borchmann P et al. Lancet 2024;404:341
highlights: Made PET-guided BrECADD the GHSG standard for advanced disease in fit adults — 4-year PFS of 94.3% with markedly less toxicity
Designed as a tolerability and non-inferiority trial; the PFS superiority is a prespecified follow-on test and survival is identical. Capped at age 60
trials.takeaway: BrECADD is both better tolerated than escalated BEACOPP and at least as effective, with 4-year PFS of 94.3%.

trials.name: SWOG S1826
trials.descriptor: nivolumab-AVD vs brentuximab-AVD in newly diagnosed stage III-IV cHL from age 12
trials.population: 994 randomized, age ≥12 with newly diagnosed stage III-IV classic HL; median age 27, 24% under 18, 10% over 60, 32% with IPS 4-7. The largest Hodgkin study in NCTN history
trials.arms: Six cycles of nivolumab + AVD vs six cycles of brentuximab vedotin + AVD. G-CSF mandatory with BV-AVD, optional with nivolumab-AVD
trials.results: Crossed the efficacy boundary at the second interim analysis (HR 0.48, 99% CI 0.27-0.87, P=0.001). With median 2.1 years of follow-up, 2-yr PFS 92% vs 83%, HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.30-0.65). Only 7 patients received radiotherapy
trials.toxicity: More grade ≥3 neutropenia with nivolumab but fewer febrile complications; far less peripheral neuropathy (28% vs 54%). In patients over 60, non-relapse mortality was 6% vs 16%
trials.reference: Herrera AF et al. NEJM 2024;391:1379
highlights: The new US standard for advanced Hodgkin across adolescents and adults, with almost no radiotherapy
Harmonized pediatric and adult treatment and was especially favorable over 60, where BV-AVD carried 16% non-relapse mortality
Follow-up is short at 2.1 years and no survival benefit has been shown
trials.takeaway: Nivolumab-AVD beat brentuximab-AVD in advanced Hodgkin with 2-year PFS of 92% versus 83% and less neuropathy.

trials.name: PRIMA
trials.descriptor: two years of rituximab maintenance after frontline immunochemotherapy in high-tumor-burden follicular lymphoma
trials.population: 1,217 enrolled with previously untreated high-tumor-burden follicular lymphoma needing systemic therapy; 1,019 responders randomized after non-randomized induction
trials.arms: Rituximab 375 mg/m² q8wk for 2 years vs observation
trials.results: 3-yr PFS 74.9% vs 57.6%, HR 0.55 (0.44-0.68), P<0.0001. No survival difference (HR 0.87). At 9 years (Bachy, JCO 2019;37:2815) median PFS 10.5 vs 4.1 years, HR 0.61, and still no OS benefit with 10-yr OS around 80% in both arms
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 adverse events 24% vs 17%; grade 2-4 infections 39% vs 24%
trials.reference: Salles G et al. Lancet 2011;377:42
highlights: Doubles median PFS but has never produced a survival benefit at any follow-up — worth saying out loud when consenting
Randomization happens among responders after induction, not at diagnosis
The price is infection: grade 2-4 infections rise from 24% to 39%
trials.takeaway: Two years of rituximab maintenance roughly doubles median PFS in high-burden follicular lymphoma without improving survival.

trials.name: StiL NHL1
trials.descriptor: bendamustine-rituximab vs R-CHOP frontline in indolent lymphoma and mantle cell
trials.population: 549 randomized with newly diagnosed stage III-IV indolent lymphoma or mantle cell lymphoma at 81 German centers
trials.arms: Bendamustine 90 mg/m² d1-2 q4wk + rituximab vs R-CHOP q3wk, maximum 6 cycles, no maintenance
trials.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival, non-inferiority with a 10% margin, per-protocol
trials.results: Median PFS 69.5 vs 31.2 months, HR 0.58 (0.44-0.74), P<0.0001 at median 45 months — a superiority result from a non-inferiority design. No overall survival difference
trials.toxicity: Markedly better tolerated: alopecia 0% vs 100%, hematologic toxicity 30% vs 68%, neuropathy 7% vs 29%, infections 37% vs 50%; more erythematous skin reactions with bendamustine
trials.reference: Rummel MJ et al. Lancet 2013;381:1203
highlights: Made bendamustine-rituximab the preferred frontline backbone for indolent lymphoma and older mantle cell
Designed only to show non-inferiority and delivered superiority, on a per-protocol analysis
trials.takeaway: Bendamustine-rituximab beat R-CHOP on PFS with far less toxicity and no alopecia.

trials.name: GALLIUM
trials.descriptor: obinutuzumab-chemotherapy vs rituximab-chemotherapy, each with two years of the same antibody as maintenance
trials.population: 1,202 patients with previously untreated advanced-stage follicular lymphoma
trials.arms: Obinutuzumab or rituximab, each with bendamustine, CHOP or CVP, followed by two years of maintenance with the same antibody
trials.results: At a planned interim analysis with 34.5 months of follow-up, 3-yr PFS 80.0% vs 73.3%, HR 0.66 (0.51-0.85), P=0.001. Response rates were essentially identical (88.5% vs 86.9%) and there was no survival difference
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-5 adverse events 74.6% vs 67.8%; serious events 46.1% vs 39.9%; infusion reactions 59.3% vs 48.9%
trials.reference: Marcus R et al. NEJM 2017;377:1331
highlights: A modest 6.7-point PFS gain at three years, bought with more grade 3-5 toxicity and more infusion reactions
No survival benefit and identical response rates
trials.takeaway: Obinutuzumab modestly improves PFS over rituximab in frontline follicular lymphoma at the cost of more toxicity, without improving survival.

trials.name: RELEVANCE
trials.descriptor: rituximab + lenalidomide vs rituximab-chemotherapy, both followed by rituximab maintenance
trials.population: 1,030 patients with previously untreated grade 1-3a follicular lymphoma requiring therapy by GELF criteria
trials.arms: Lenalidomide 20 mg + rituximab vs investigator's choice of R-CHOP, R-bendamustine or R-CVP, each followed by rituximab maintenance
trials.primary_endpoint: Co-primary — complete response at 120 weeks and progression-free survival. A superiority design
trials.results: Negative for superiority. CR/CRu at 120 weeks 48% vs 53%, P=0.13; interim 3-yr PFS 77% vs 78%. At six years (JCO 2022) PFS 60% vs 59%, HR 1.03, and OS 89% in both arms
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 neutropenia 32% vs 50% and febrile neutropenia 2% vs 7% favoring the chemo-free arm; grade 3-4 cutaneous reactions 7% vs 1% against it
trials.reference: Morschhauser F et al. NEJM 2018;379:934
highlights: A superiority trial that was negative — R-squared is an equivalent chemotherapy-free option, not a better one
Co-primary endpoints were complete response at 120 weeks and PFS, not PFS alone
Frequently conflated with Fowler's single-institution phase 2, which is a different study
trials.takeaway: Rituximab-lenalidomide matches rituximab-chemotherapy in frontline follicular lymphoma without beating it, making it a legitimate chemo-free alternative.

trials.name: SHINE
trials.descriptor: ibrutinib added to bendamustine-rituximab with rituximab maintenance in transplant-ineligible older mantle cell
trials.population: 523 patients aged 65 or older with untreated mantle cell lymphoma; median age 71
trials.arms: Ibrutinib 560 mg daily until progression vs placebo, each with six cycles of bendamustine-rituximab then rituximab maintenance q8wk for 12 doses
trials.results: At median 84.7 months, median PFS 80.6 vs 52.9 months, HR 0.75 (0.59-0.96), P=0.01. Complete response 65.5% vs 57.6%. No overall survival benefit, attributed to excess adverse-event deaths on ibrutinib
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 adverse events 81.5% vs 77.3%; atrial fibrillation 13.9% vs 6.5%
trials.reference: Wang ML et al. NEJM 2022;386:2482
highlights: A 2.3-year PFS gain that does not translate into survival, because toxicity offsets it
Atrial fibrillation doubled — the observation that motivated the second-generation BTKi trial ECHO
trials.takeaway: Adding ibrutinib to bendamustine-rituximab in older mantle cell buys 2.3 years of PFS but no survival benefit.

trials.name: ECOG-ACRIN EA4151
trials.setting: MCL consolidation in MRD-negative first remission
trials.descriptor: autologous transplant plus rituximab maintenance vs maintenance alone in MRD-undetectable first complete remission
trials.population: 650 assigned with mantle cell lymphoma age 18-70 in first remission after rituximab-containing induction; 516 with undetectable MRD at 10^-6 were randomized. Only 7.2% had received a BTK inhibitor
trials.arms: Autologous transplant followed by three years of rituximab maintenance vs three years of rituximab maintenance alone
trials.results: At the third preplanned interim analysis with median follow-up 2.7 years the trial crossed its futility boundary. OS HR 1.11 (0.71-1.74), P=0.66; 3-yr OS 82.1% vs 82.7%. PFS HR 1.05, 3-yr PFS 76.6% vs 77.4%. In the non-randomized MRD-positive arm, patients converting to undetectable MRD after transplant did markedly better. Accrual was stopped in September 2024
trials.toxicity: Not reported beyond cause of death in the abstract; 25.3% of patients assigned to transplant declined it
trials.reference: Fenske TS et al. ASH 2024 abstract LBA-6 — conference report, no peer-reviewed publication
highlights: The primary endpoint is overall survival, and it crossed futility rather than demonstrating equivalence
Conference abstract only, and only 7.2% received a BTK inhibitor during induction, so it does not address modern BTKi-containing regimens
trials.takeaway: Mantle cell patients in MRD-undetectable first remission gain no survival or PFS benefit from consolidative autologous transplant.

trials.name: TRIANGLE
trials.descriptor: three-arm test of adding ibrutinib to induction and maintenance, and of whether autologous transplant is still needed
trials.population: 870 patients with untreated stage II-IV mantle cell lymphoma, age 18-65 and transplant-eligible, at 165 centres; median age 57, 87% stage IV
trials.arms: A: alternating R-CHOP/R-DHAP then autologous transplant. A+I: the same plus ibrutinib during induction and two years of maintenance. I: ibrutinib-containing induction and maintenance with no transplant
trials.primary_endpoint: Failure-free survival — not PFS or OS
trials.results: At 31 months, A+I superior to A: 3-yr FFS 88% vs 72%, HR 0.52, P=0.0008; A was not superior to I. On mature follow-up at 54.9 months, A+I was not superior to I (4-yr FFS 82% vs 81%, HR 0.86), while both ibrutinib arms exceeded transplant alone on survival (4-yr OS 88-90% vs 81%)
trials.toxicity: No excess during induction or transplant, but during maintenance grade 3-5 hematologic toxicity 54% with A+I vs 28% with ibrutinib alone vs 23% with transplant alone; infections 34% vs 26% vs 15%
trials.reference: Dreyling M et al. Lancet 2024;403:2293
highlights: Ended routine autologous transplant for younger mantle cell — adding it to an ibrutinib regimen adds toxicity without benefit
The primary endpoint is failure-free survival, which is not interchangeable with PFS
trials.takeaway: Ibrutinib with R-CHOP/R-DHAP and two years of maintenance, without transplant, is the new standard for younger mantle cell lymphoma.

trials.name: ECHO
trials.descriptor: acalabrutinib added to bendamustine-rituximab in older mantle cell — the second-generation answer to SHINE
trials.population: 598 patients aged 65 or older with untreated mantle cell lymphoma, ECOG ≤2, at 195 sites in 26 countries; median age 71
trials.arms: Acalabrutinib 100 mg twice daily vs placebo until progression, each with six cycles of bendamustine-rituximab then two years of rituximab maintenance; crossover permitted at progression
trials.results: At median 49.8 months, median PFS 66.4 vs 49.6 months, HR 0.73 (0.57-0.94), P=0.0160. Censoring COVID-19 deaths, median PFS was not reached vs 61.6 months, HR 0.64. Complete response 66.6% vs 53.5%. No overall survival difference (HR 0.86)
