trials.takeaway: Enzalutamide more than doubles MFS in nmCRPC

trials.name: SPARTAN
trials.descriptor: apalutamide in non-metastatic CRPC
trials.population: M0 CRPC with PSA doubling time ≤10 months
trials.arms: Apalutamide 240 mg daily vs placebo, both + ADT
trials.results: MFS 40.5 vs 16.2 mo (HR 0.28). Final OS (Smith MR et al. Eur Urol 2021;79:150): 73.9 vs 59.9 mo, HR 0.78 (0.64-0.96), P=0.016
trials.reference: Smith MR et al. NEJM 2018;378:1408; final OS Eur Urol 2021;79:150
highlights: One of the three M0 CRPC trials that made MFS an accepted registrational endpoint.
Overall survival benefit confirmed at final analysis (OS HR 0.69-0.78 across the three nmCRPC trials)
trials.takeaway: Apalutamide more than doubles MFS in nmCRPC

trials.name: ARAMIS
trials.descriptor: darolutamide in non-metastatic CRPC
trials.population: M0 CRPC with PSA doubling time ≤10 months
trials.arms: Darolutamide 600 mg BID vs placebo, both + ADT
trials.reference: Fizazi K et al. NEJM 2019;380:1235; final OS NEJM 2020;383:1040
highlights: Darolutamide's distinct structure gives minimal blood-brain barrier penetration → fewer CNS effects (fatigue, falls, seizures) than enzalutamide or apalutamide.
Overall survival benefit confirmed at final analysis (OS HR 0.69-0.78 across the three nmCRPC trials)
trials.takeaway: Darolutamide doubles MFS in nmCRPC with fewer CNS side effects

trials.name: ARCHES
trials.descriptor: enzalutamide added to ADT in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer
trials.population: 1,150 men with mHSPC, stratified by disease volume and prior docetaxel
trials.arms: Enzalutamide 160 mg daily + ADT vs placebo + ADT
trials.results: rPFS HR 0.39 (95% CI 0.30-0.50), P<0.001 (median NR vs 19.0 mo). Final OS (Armstrong JCO 2022;40:1616): HR 0.66 (0.53-0.81), P<0.001, medians not reached, despite 31% crossover
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 24.3% vs 25.6%; quality of life maintained
trials.reference: Armstrong AJ et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:2974-2986; OS: J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1616
highlights: Benefit held in low-volume disease and after prior docetaxel
Together with ENZAMET, establishes enzalutamide as an mHSPC doublet partner
OS benefit confirmed at final analysis despite crossover
trials.takeaway: Enzalutamide plus ADT improves rPFS and overall survival in mHSPC regardless of volume.

trials.name: CARD
trials.setting: mCRPC after docetaxel and one ARPI
trials.descriptor: cabazitaxel vs a second ARPI
trials.population: 255 men with mCRPC previously treated with docetaxel who progressed within 12 months on abiraterone or enzalutamide
trials.arms: Cabazitaxel 25 mg/m2 q3wk + prednisone + G-CSF vs the alternative ARPI
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 56.3% vs 52.4%
trials.reference: de Wit R et al. N Engl J Med 2019;381:2506-2518
highlights: The trial behind 'never follow one ARPI with another'
Cabazitaxel improved survival as well as rPFS
Mandatory G-CSF prophylaxis at 25 mg/m2
trials.takeaway: After docetaxel and one ARPI, cabazitaxel beats switching to a second ARPI for PFS and OS.

trials.name: ENZAMET
trials.descriptor: enzalutamide added to ADT in M1 CSPC
trials.population: M1 CSPC; concurrent docetaxel permitted at investigator discretion
trials.arms: ADT + enzalutamide vs ADT + a first-generation antiandrogen (standard care)
trials.reference: Davis ID et al. NEJM 2019;381:121
highlights: Notable for showing enzalutamide beats a first-generation antiandrogen, not just placebo.
Its docetaxel-permitted design provided early support for triplet therapy.
trials.takeaway: ADT + enzalutamide beats ADT + first-generation antiandrogen for OS in M1 CSPC

trials.name: ERA 223
trials.descriptor: radium-223 added to abiraterone — harmful combination
trials.population: Asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic chemotherapy-naive mCRPC with bone metastases (≥2 lesions)
trials.arms: Abiraterone/prednisone + radium-223 vs abiraterone/prednisone + placebo
trials.results: SSE-FS 22.3 vs 26.0 mo (HR 1.12, p=0.26); fractures 29% vs 11%; deaths 34.7% vs 28.2% — trial unblinded early for harm
trials.toxicity: Fractures (largely osteoporotic, in patients not on bone-protective agents), no excess marrow toxicity
trials.reference: Smith M et al. Lancet Oncol 2019;20:408
highlights: Do not combine radium-223 with abiraterone — more fractures and deaths. Radium-223 is used sequentially, not concurrently with ARPI ± steroids.
Highlighted the need for bone-protective agents (denosumab/zoledronic acid) whenever radium-223 is given.
trials.takeaway: Radium-223 + abiraterone increased fractures and deaths — never combine them

trials.name: TITAN
trials.descriptor: apalutamide added to ADT in M1 CSPC
trials.population: M1 CSPC, all volumes (high and low)
trials.arms: ADT + apalutamide vs ADT + placebo
trials.reference: Chi KN et al. NEJM 2019;381:13
highlights: Benefit seen regardless of disease volume, extending ARPI intensification to low-volume M1 CSPC.
trials.takeaway: ADT + apalutamide improves OS in M1 CSPC regardless of volume

trials.name: HERO
trials.descriptor: relugolix, oral GnRH antagonist
trials.population: Advanced prostate cancer requiring ADT for ≥1 year
trials.arms: Oral relugolix (360 mg load → 120 mg daily) vs leuprolide injection
trials.results: 96.7% vs 88.8% sustained castration; faster testosterone suppression, faster recovery after stopping; 54% fewer major adverse cardiovascular events
trials.reference: Shore ND et al. NEJM 2020;382:2187
highlights: Established the first oral GnRH antagonist — no testosterone flare, and a favorable cardiovascular profile vs LHRH agonists.
trials.takeaway: Relugolix — oral GnRH antagonist, non-inferior castration with fewer MACE than leuprolide

trials.name: PROfound
trials.descriptor: olaparib in HRR-mutated mCRPC after ARPI progression
trials.population: mCRPC progressing on abiraterone or enzalutamide, with homologous recombination repair alterations (cohort A: BRCA1, BRCA2, ATM)
trials.arms: Olaparib 300 mg BID vs physician's choice of the alternative ARPI
trials.results: rPFS 7.4 vs 3.6 mo (HR 0.34); OS 19.1 vs 14.7 mo despite crossover
trials.reference: de Bono J et al. NEJM 2020;382:2091
highlights: First biomarker-selected targeted therapy in prostate cancer → PARP inhibitor monotherapy in the post-ARPI (relapsed) setting.
Contrast with the first-line PARP + ARPI combinations (TALAPRO-2, MAGNITUDE, PROpel).
trials.takeaway: Olaparib monotherapy for HRR-mutated mCRPC after ARPI — first biomarker-selected therapy in prostate cancer

trials.name: proPSMA
trials.setting: Staging high-risk localized disease before curative therapy
trials.descriptor: PSMA PET-CT vs conventional imaging for staging
trials.population: 302 men with high-risk localized prostate cancer planned for curative-intent surgery or RT
trials.arms: Ga-68 PSMA-11 PET-CT vs CT + bone scan
trials.primary_endpoint: Accuracy for pelvic nodal or distant metastases
trials.results: Accuracy 92% vs 65% (absolute +27%, P<0.0001); sensitivity 85% vs 38%, specificity 98% vs 91%; management change 28% vs 15%; equivocal 7% vs 23%
trials.toxicity: Radiation dose 8.4 vs 19.2 mSv
trials.reference: Hofman MS et al. Lancet 2020;395:1208-1216
highlights: PSMA PET is more accurate, changes management more often, and uses less radiation
No outcome (survival) endpoint - stage migration caveat
Trial risk definitions (CHAARTED volume etc.) were built on conventional imaging
trials.takeaway: PSMA PET-CT is substantially more accurate than CT plus bone scan for staging high-risk prostate cancer.

trials.name: TRITON2
trials.descriptor: rucaparib in BRCA-mutated mCRPC after ARPI and taxane
trials.population: mCRPC with a deleterious BRCA1/2 alteration, progressed on 1–2 ARPIs and 1 taxane
trials.arms: Single-arm: rucaparib 600 mg BID
trials.primary_endpoint: Objective response rate (measurable disease) and PSA response
trials.results: ORR 43.5%; PSA response 54.8%; median rPFS 9.0 mo; responses in both germline and somatic BRCA; low response in ATM/CDK12/CHEK2 cohorts
trials.toxicity: Anemia, fatigue, nausea, transaminase elevation
trials.reference: Abida W et al. JCO 2020;38:3763
highlights: Basis for rucaparib's accelerated approval in BRCA-mutated mCRPC after ARPI and taxane; TRITON3 (2023) later confirmed rPFS benefit vs physician's choice.
Non-BRCA HRR genes (ATM, CDK12, CHEK2) respond poorly to PARP inhibition — BRCA is the actionable target.
trials.takeaway: Rucaparib produces responses in BRCA-mutated mCRPC after ARPI and taxane; ATM/CDK12/CHEK2 respond poorly

trials.name: VISION
trials.descriptor: Lutetium-177–PSMA-617 in PSMA-positive mCRPC
trials.population: PSMA-positive mCRPC (on ⁶⁸Ga-PSMA-11 PET) after ≥1 ARPI and 1–2 taxane regimens
trials.arms: Lu-177-PSMA-617 (7.4 GBq q6wk ×6) + standard of care vs standard of care alone
trials.results: OS 15.3 vs 11.3 mo (HR 0.62); rPFS 8.7 vs 3.4 mo (HR 0.40)
trials.reference: Sartor O et al. NEJM 2021;385:1091
highlights: Established radioligand therapy in prostate cancer — requires a PSMA PET to select patients.
Key toxicities: xerostomia (salivary glands express PSMA), marrow suppression, fatigue.
PSMAfore (2024) later moved Lu-PSMA into the pre-taxane setting.
trials.takeaway: Lu-177-PSMA-617 improves OS and rPFS in PSMA-positive mCRPC after ARPI and taxane

trials.name: ARASENS
trials.descriptor: triplet therapy with darolutamide in M1 CSPC
trials.population: Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer
trials.arms: ADT + docetaxel + darolutamide vs ADT + docetaxel + placebo
trials.results: Median OS not reached vs 48.9 mo (HR 0.68); rPFS 4.4 vs 2.0 yr; no meaningful added toxicity
trials.reference: Smith MR et al. NEJM 2022;386:1132
highlights: The other pillar of triplet therapy; darolutamide's tolerability makes it the preferred ARPI in the high-volume triplet.
trials.takeaway: Adding darolutamide to ADT + docetaxel improves OS in M1 CSPC

trials.name: PEACE-1
trials.descriptor: triplet therapy with abiraterone in de novo M1 CSPC
trials.population: De novo metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer
trials.arms: 2×2 factorial: ADT (± docetaxel) ± abiraterone ± radiotherapy to the primary
trials.results: High-volume disease: OS 5.1 vs 3.5 yr; rPFS 4.1 vs 1.6 yr. Radiotherapy to the primary improved rPFS in low-volume disease
trials.reference: Fizazi K et al. Lancet 2022;399:1695
highlights: Established triplet therapy (ADT + docetaxel + abiraterone) for high-volume M1 CSPC.
Also supports radiation to the primary tumor in low-volume disease.
trials.takeaway: ADT + docetaxel + abiraterone triplet improves OS in high-volume de novo M1 CSPC

trials.name: PROpel
trials.descriptor: olaparib + abiraterone first-line, HRR-unselected mCRPC
trials.population: First-line mCRPC regardless of HRR status (tested retrospectively; ~28% HRR-mutated)
trials.arms: Olaparib 300 mg BID + abiraterone/prednisone vs placebo + abiraterone/prednisone
trials.results: rPFS 24.8 vs 16.6 mo (HR 0.66); HRR-mutated HR 0.50, non-HRR HR 0.76; BRCA-mutated rPFS HR 0.23; OS 42.1 vs 34.7 mo (HR 0.81, NS)
trials.toxicity: Anemia (grade ≥3 15%), fatigue, nausea, VTE/PE (7% vs 2%)
trials.reference: Clarke NW et al. NEJM Evid 2022;1:EVIDoa2200043; Saad F et al. Lancet Oncol 2023 (OS)
highlights: The FDA restricted approval of olaparib + abiraterone to BRCA-mutated mCRPC (May 2023) because the benefit was driven by that subgroup despite the all-comers design.
Together with MAGNITUDE and TALAPRO-2, defines first-line PARP + ARPI combinations — chosen mainly by BRCA/HRR status.
trials.takeaway: Olaparib + abiraterone improves rPFS first-line in mCRPC, with the benefit concentrated in BRCA-mutated disease

trials.name: SPPORT (NRG/RTOG 0534)
trials.descriptor: prostate-bed RT +/- short-term ADT +/- pelvic nodal RT
trials.population: 1,792 men with rising PSA after prostatectomy (1,716 eligible)
trials.arms: Prostate-bed RT alone vs + 4-6 mo ADT vs + ADT + pelvic lymph node RT
trials.results: 5-yr freedom from progression 70.9% vs 81.3% vs 87.4%
trials.toxicity: Acute grade >=2 AEs 18% / 36% / 44%
trials.reference: Pollack A et al. Lancet 2022;399:1886-1901
highlights: Stepwise gain from adding short ADT, then pelvic nodal RT
Supports short-course ADT with salvage RT
Toxicity rises with each added component
trials.takeaway: Short-term ADT and pelvic nodal RT each add progression-free benefit to salvage prostate-bed RT.

trials.name: STAMPEDE (abiraterone, high-risk M0)
trials.descriptor: abiraterone +/- enzalutamide added to ADT in high-risk M0 disease
trials.population: 1,974 men with high-risk node-negative or node-positive non-metastatic prostate cancer (two STAMPEDE comparisons, meta-analyzed)
trials.arms: ADT for 3 yr (+ RT in most) +/- abiraterone 1000 mg + prednisolone 5 mg for 2 yr (one comparison also added enzalutamide 160 mg)
trials.results: MFS HR 0.53 (0.44-0.64), P<0.0001; 6-yr MFS 82% vs 69%. OS HR 0.60 (0.48-0.73). Adding enzalutamide gave no extra benefit (interaction HR 1.02)
trials.reference: Attard G et al. Lancet 2022;399:447-460
highlights: Basis for 2 years of abiraterone with ADT + RT in very-high-risk or node-positive localized disease
Enzalutamide on top of abiraterone added toxicity without benefit
Unusually large OS effect for a localized-disease trial
trials.takeaway: Two years of abiraterone added to ADT improves metastasis-free and overall survival in high-risk non-metastatic prostate cancer.

trials.name: EMBARK
trials.descriptor: enzalutamide + leuprolide vs leuprolide alone vs enzalutamide monotherapy in high-risk biochemical recurrence
trials.population: 1,068 men with high-risk biochemical recurrence after definitive local therapy, M0 and castration-sensitive, PSA doubling time ≤9 months (PSA ≥2 ng/mL above nadir after radiotherapy, or ≥1 ng/mL after prostatectomy ± postoperative RT). Randomized 1:1:1; median follow-up 60.7 months
trials.arms: Enzalutamide 160 mg daily + leuprolide q12wk (n=355) vs placebo + leuprolide (n=358) vs enzalutamide 160 mg monotherapy (n=355). Treatment was suspended at week 37 in patients whose PSA became undetectable
trials.primary_endpoint: Metastasis-free survival by blinded independent central review, combination vs leuprolide alone. Overall survival was an alpha-controlled key secondary endpoint
trials.results: 5-yr MFS 87.3% (combination) vs 71.4% (leuprolide alone) vs 80.0% (monotherapy). Combination vs leuprolide HR 0.42 (95% CI 0.30-0.61), P<0.001; monotherapy vs leuprolide HR 0.63 (0.46-0.87), P=0.005. Final OS analysis (Shore ND et al. NEJM 2025;394:563, PMID 41124201): 8-yr OS 78.9% vs 69.5%, HR for death 0.60 (0.44-0.80), P<0.001 for the combination — but monotherapy 73.1%, HR 0.83 (0.63-1.10), P=0.19, NOT significant
trials.toxicity: No new safety signals and no substantial between-group difference in quality of life. Secondary endpoints favored the combination: 5-yr freedom from castration resistance 96.6% vs 67.8%, from distant metastasis 91.0% vs 81.5%
trials.reference: Freedland SJ et al. NEJM 2023;389:1453
highlights: Brought treatment intensification into the biochemical-recurrence space, previously managed with ADT alone or observation, and now carries a proven survival benefit
The 2025 final analysis separates the two experimental arms: the combination improves overall survival, but enzalutamide monotherapy does not — despite having beaten leuprolide on MFS in 2023
Monotherapy remains a defensible choice for a patient prioritizing avoidance of castration side effects, but it should no longer be presented as survival-equivalent to the combination
trials.takeaway: Enzalutamide plus leuprolide improves both metastasis-free and overall survival in high-risk biochemical recurrence; enzalutamide alone improves MFS but not survival.

trials.name: MAGNITUDE
trials.descriptor: niraparib + abiraterone first-line, HRR-mutated mCRPC
trials.population: First-line mCRPC with HRR gene alterations (BRCA1/2 cohort prespecified); an HRR-negative cohort was closed for futility
trials.arms: Niraparib 200 mg + abiraterone/prednisone vs placebo + abiraterone/prednisone
trials.results: BRCA1/2: rPFS 16.6 vs 10.9 mo (HR 0.53, updated 19.5 vs 10.9); all HRR+: rPFS 16.5 vs 13.7 mo (HR 0.73); no benefit in HRR-negative disease; OS (BRCA) HR 0.79
trials.toxicity: Anemia (grade ≥3 ~28%), hypertension, thrombocytopenia
trials.reference: Chi KN et al. JCO 2023;41:3339
highlights: Niraparib + abiraterone (Akeega) is approved for BRCA-mutated 1L mCRPC - the benefit is essentially confined to BRCA1/2, not the broader HRR set.

Contrast with PROpel (all-comers enrollment, BRCA-only label) and TALAPRO-2 (all-comers enrollment, HRR-only label after FDA declined an all-comers expansion in 2025); biomarker testing is required before any first-line PARP combination.
The same combination moved into castration-sensitive disease with AMPLITUDE (FDA Dec 2025, BRCA2 only).
trials.takeaway: Niraparib + abiraterone improves rPFS in BRCA-mutated first-line mCRPC, with no benefit in HRR-negative disease

trials.name: TALAPRO-2
trials.descriptor: talazoparib + enzalutamide, first-line mCRPC
trials.population: 805 men in the all-comers cohort (first-line mCRPC, ARPI-naive for CRPC) plus a separate HRR-deficient cohort of 399
trials.arms: Talazoparib 0.5 mg + enzalutamide vs placebo + enzalutamide
trials.results: All-comers: rPFS HR 0.63 at primary analysis (updated 33.1 vs 19.5 mo, HR 0.67). Final OS 45.8 vs 37.0 mo, HR 0.80 (0.66-0.96), P=0.016; HRR-deficient subgroup HR 0.55, HRR-non-deficient/unknown HR 0.88 (0.71-1.08), NS. HRR-deficient cohort (n=399): OS 45.1 vs 31.1 mo, HR 0.62 (0.48-0.81); BRCA OS HR 0.50; non-BRCA HR 0.73 (0.52-1.02)
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 anemia 49% (all-comers) / 43% (HRR cohort); neutropenia 19-20%
trials.reference: Agarwal N et al. Lancet 2023;402:291; final OS Agarwal N et al. Lancet 2025;406:447 and Fizazi K et al. Lancet 2025;406:461
highlights: Final OS positive in both cohorts, but the survival effect is concentrated in HRR-deficient, especially BRCA, disease
US label remains HRR gene-mutated mCRPC only: ODAC voted 8-0 against the non-HRR population (May 2025) and FDA declined to expand
Contrast with PROfound - PARP monotherapy belongs in the post-ARPI setting; anemia is the dominant toxicity
trials.takeaway: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide improves overall survival in first-line mCRPC, with the benefit concentrated in HRR-deficient disease; the US label is HRR-mutated only.

trials.name: TRITON3
trials.descriptor: rucaparib vs physician's choice after ARPI in BRCA/ATM mCRPC
trials.population: 405 men with mCRPC and BRCA1/2 (n=302) or ATM (n=103) alteration, progression after one second-generation ARPI, no prior chemo for CRPC
trials.arms: Rucaparib 600 mg BID vs physician's choice (docetaxel, or the alternative ARPI), 2:1
trials.primary_endpoint: Imaging-based PFS by independent review (BRCA, then ITT)
trials.toxicity: Fatigue, nausea most frequent; anemia
trials.reference: Fizazi K et al. N Engl J Med 2023;388:719-732
highlights: Confirmatory trial for the 2020 TRITON2 accelerated approval; converted to regular approval Dec 17, 2025 (BRCA only)
Rucaparib beat docetaxel-containing control, not just an ARPI switch
ATM alterations derive no meaningful benefit
trials.takeaway: Rucaparib improves imaging-based PFS over physician's choice in BRCA-mutated mCRPC after an ARPI, but not in ATM.

trials.name: ARANOTE
trials.descriptor: darolutamide plus ADT without docetaxel in mHSPC
trials.population: 669 men with mHSPC
trials.arms: Darolutamide 600 mg BID + ADT vs placebo + ADT (2:1)
trials.results: rPFS HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.71), P<0.0001. OS HR 0.81 (0.59-1.12), not significant. Time to mCRPC HR 0.40; time to pain progression HR 0.72
trials.toxicity: Low: fatigue 5.6% vs 8.1%; discontinuation for AEs 6.1% vs 9.0%
trials.reference: Saad F et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:4271-4281
highlights: Extended darolutamide beyond the ARASENS triplet to an ADT doublet (FDA June 3, 2025)
OS was not significantly improved at this analysis - an rPFS-based approval
Darolutamide's tolerability (low CNS penetration) is the reason to choose it
trials.takeaway: Darolutamide plus ADT improves rPFS in mHSPC without docetaxel, but an OS benefit has not been shown.

trials.name: ENZA-p (ANZUP 1901)
trials.descriptor: enzalutamide +/- Lu-177-PSMA-617
trials.population: 162 men with ARPI-naive mCRPC and high-risk features, PSMA PET positive
trials.arms: Enzalutamide 160 mg +/- Lu-PSMA-617 7.5 GBq q6-8wk (2 or 4 doses, adapted by week-12 PSMA PET)
trials.reference: Emmett L et al. Lancet Oncol 2024;25:563-571
highlights: Randomized phase 2 - hypothesis-generating despite the OS signal
Supports combining radioligand with ARPI earlier
Not an approved combination
trials.takeaway: Adding Lu-PSMA to enzalutamide improved PSA-PFS and OS in a randomized phase 2 trial in first-line mCRPC.

trials.name: PRESTO (AFT-19)
trials.descriptor: finite 52-week ADT +/- apalutamide +/- abiraterone
trials.population: 503 men with BCR after radical prostatectomy, PSA doubling time <=9 months
trials.arms: 52 weeks of ADT vs ADT + apalutamide vs ADT + apalutamide + abiraterone/prednisone
trials.results: ADT + apalutamide 24.9 vs 20.3 mo, HR 0.52 (0.35-0.77), P=0.00047; triplet 26.0 vs 20.0 mo, HR 0.48 (0.32-0.71). Testosterone recovery similar
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 hypertension 7.5% / 7.4% / 18%
trials.reference: Aggarwal R et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:1114-1123
highlights: Finite intensified therapy delays PSA progression in high-risk BCR
PSA-based endpoint only - no MFS or OS data, unlike EMBARK
Adding abiraterone to apalutamide added hypertension without clear gain
trials.takeaway: A year of ADT plus apalutamide lengthens PSA-PFS in high-risk BCR, but lacks the survival data EMBARK has.

trials.name: PSMAfore
trials.descriptor: Lu-177-PSMA-617 vs ARPI switch before chemotherapy
trials.population: PSMA-positive mCRPC progressing on one ARPI, taxane-naive, candidates for an ARPI change
trials.arms: Lu-177-PSMA-617 × 6 vs change of ARPI (abiraterone or enzalutamide); crossover allowed
trials.results: rPFS 12.0 vs 5.6 mo (HR 0.41); ORR 50.7% vs 14.9%; OS HR ~1.0 (84% crossover)
trials.toxicity: Xerostomia, anemia, fatigue; fewer grade ≥3 AEs than ARPI switch
trials.reference: Morris MJ et al. Lancet 2024;404:1227
highlights: Moves Lu-PSMA into the pre-chemotherapy setting (FDA March 2025) — an alternative to docetaxel after first ARPI failure.
The control arm (ARPI switch) is a weak comparator; whether Lu-PSMA should precede docetaxel remains a judgment call.
trials.takeaway: Lu-177-PSMA-617 doubles rPFS vs switching ARPI in taxane-naive PSMA-positive mCRPC

trials.name: AMPLITUDE
trials.descriptor: niraparib + abiraterone/prednisone in HRR-altered mHSPC
trials.population: 696 men with mCSPC and HRR gene alterations (56% BRCA1/2); 78% high volume; 16% prior docetaxel
trials.arms: Niraparib 200 mg + abiraterone 1000 mg + prednisone 5 mg + ADT vs placebo + AAP + ADT
trials.primary_endpoint: Radiographic PFS (BRCA subgroup first, then ITT)
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 AEs 75% vs 59%; anemia 29% (25% transfused), hypertension 27%; treatment-emergent deaths 14 vs 7
trials.reference: Attard G et al. Nat Med 2025;31:4109-4118
highlights: First PARP combination to show benefit in castration-sensitive disease
FDA approval (Dec 12, 2025) is restricted to BRCA2-mutated mCSPC - exploratory BRCA2 rPFS HR 0.46
Survival data immature and toxicity substantial - weigh against a docetaxel triplet
trials.takeaway: Niraparib plus abiraterone improves rPFS in HRR-altered mHSPC, driven by BRCA; the US label is BRCA2 only.

trials.name: CAPItello-281
trials.descriptor: capivasertib + abiraterone in PTEN-deficient mHSPC
trials.population: 1,012 men with PTEN-deficient mHSPC by IHC (>=90% tumor cells without PTEN staining); 25.3% of screened tumors were PTEN-deficient
trials.arms: Capivasertib 400 mg BID 4 days on/3 off vs placebo, each + abiraterone + prednisone + ADT
trials.toxicity: Diarrhea 51.9% vs 8.0%, hyperglycemia 38.0% vs 12.9%, rash 35.4% vs 7.0%; AE-associated deaths 7.2% vs 5.2%
trials.reference: Fizazi K et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:53-68
highlights: POSITIVE for its primary endpoint - some secondary summaries (e.g. HemeOncBuddy) incorrectly call it negative
FDA approved June 12, 2026 with the VENTANA PTEN (SP218) companion assay
Modest 7.5-month rPFS gain, no OS signal yet, and real AKT-inhibitor toxicity
trials.takeaway: Capivasertib plus abiraterone modestly improves rPFS in PTEN-deficient mHSPC, without an OS benefit so far.

trials.name: CONTACT-02
trials.setting: mCRPC after one ARPI, measurable soft tissue
trials.descriptor: cabozantinib + atezolizumab vs second ARPI
trials.population: 575 men with mCRPC and measurable extrapelvic soft-tissue disease after one ARPI
trials.arms: Cabozantinib 40 mg daily + atezolizumab 1200 mg q3wk vs switch to abiraterone or enzalutamide
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 AEs 56% vs 26%
trials.reference: Agarwal N et al. Lancet Oncol 2025;26:860-876
highlights: PFS gain against a weak comparator (ARPI switch) without OS benefit
Doubled grade 3-4 toxicity
Immunotherapy remains confined to MSI-H/dMMR prostate cancer
trials.takeaway: Cabozantinib plus atezolizumab improved PFS but not overall survival versus a second ARPI in mCRPC and is not a standard option.

trials.name: PEACE-3 (EORTC 1333)
trials.descriptor: enzalutamide +/- radium-223
trials.population: 446 men with mCRPC and bone metastases; bone-protecting agent mandatory from March 2018
trials.arms: Enzalutamide vs enzalutamide + radium-223 x 6
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 65.6% vs 55.8%; grade >=3 hypertension 34%; fractures 24.3% vs 13.4% (with or without bone agent)
trials.reference: Tombal B et al. Ann Oncol 2025;36:1058-1067; final OS Gillessen S et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:736-742
highlights: Contrast with ERA 223: radium is harmful with abiraterone but beneficial with enzalutamide when bone protection is given
Fractures still roughly doubled - a bone-protecting agent is mandatory
Not a labeled combination
trials.takeaway: Radium-223 added to enzalutamide improves rPFS and OS in first-line mCRPC, provided a bone-protecting agent is used.

trials.name: PATCH
trials.descriptor: transdermal estradiol vs LHRH agonist in locally advanced M0 disease
trials.population: Locally advanced, non-metastatic prostate cancer (T3–T4 or N+, M0); 1,360 men at 75 UK centres, 2007–2022, pooling the PATCH + STAMPEDE-1 cohorts. Median age 72; 60% Gleason 8–10; radiotherapy planned in 68%
trials.arms: Transdermal estradiol (tE2) patches — four 100 µg patches twice weekly, reduced to three once castrate — vs standard LHRH agonist
trials.primary_endpoint: Metastasis-free survival, non-inferiority design (margin 4 percentage points ≈ HR 1.31)
trials.results: Non-inferior: 3-yr MFS 87.1% vs 85.9% (HR 0.96, upper one-sided 95% CI ≈1.11). 5-yr OS 81.1% vs 79.2% (HR 0.90). Sustained castration in year 1: 85% in both arms
trials.toxicity: Grade ≥2 hot flashes 8% vs 37%; fractures at 10 yr 5.1% vs 10.5%; grade ≥2 gynecomastia 37% vs 9% (85% vs 42% any grade); no excess cardiovascular events (HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.80–1.53)
trials.reference: Langley RE et al. NEJM 2026;394:1595-1607
highlights: Rationale: LHRH agonists deplete both testosterone and estradiol — and most classic ADT morbidity (bone loss, fractures, hot flashes, metabolic syndrome) is actually estrogen deficiency. Estradiol suppresses testosterone by HPG-axis negative feedback while keeping estrogen on board.

Why transdermal: oral estrogen (DES) was abandoned for thromboembolism driven by first-pass hepatic metabolism inducing procoagulant protein synthesis. The patch bypasses the liver — the entire reason the strategy was revisited, and why no excess cardiovascular events were seen.
Also: no testosterone flare, self-administered, low cost. Main trade-off is gynecomastia (85% any grade); prophylactic breast irradiation was used in only 8%.
Caveats: M0 disease only — does not extend to metastatic disease or ARPI-intensified pathways; shorter median treatment duration with crossover to LHRH; not licensed for prostate cancer.
trials.takeaway: Transdermal estradiol is non-inferior to LHRH agonist for MFS in locally advanced M0 disease, with fewer hot flashes and fractures

trials.name: PSMAddition
trials.descriptor: Lu-177-PSMA-617 added to ADT + ARPI in mHSPC
trials.population: 1,144 men with PSMA-positive metastatic hormone-sensitive (APMN/S) prostate cancer; 50% de novo, 68% high volume
trials.arms: Lu-PSMA-617 7.4 GBq q6wk up to 6 cycles + ADT + ARPI vs ADT + ARPI; crossover on progression
trials.results: rPFS HR 0.72 (0.58-0.90), P=0.0021, medians not reached (second interim). OS immature
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 51% vs 43%; dry mouth 46% vs 4% (all grade 1-2); cytopenias and GI effects more frequent
trials.reference: Tagawa ST et al. Lancet 2026;408:793-807
highlights: Moves Lu-PSMA into castration-sensitive disease; FDA approved July 31, 2026 with an ARPI
Open-label, rPFS-only with immature OS
Control arm was an ARPI doublet, not a docetaxel triplet
trials.takeaway: Adding Lu-PSMA-617 to ADT plus an ARPI improves rPFS in PSMA-positive mHSPC; survival benefit is not yet shown.

trials.name: EORTC 30904
trials.descriptor: nephron-sparing surgery vs radical nephrectomy for small solitary renal tumors
trials.population: Small (<=5 cm), solitary T1-T2 N0 M0 tumors suspicious for RCC with a normal contralateral kidney
trials.arms: Partial (nephron-sparing) nephrectomy vs radical nephrectomy
trials.results: At 9.3 yr: 10-yr OS 75.7% NSS vs 81.1% RN, HR 1.50 (95% CI 1.03-2.16); non-inferiority not shown
trials.toxicity: Slightly more complications with partial nephrectomy
trials.reference: Van Poppel H et al. Eur Urol 2011;59:543-552
highlights: The only randomized trial of partial vs radical nephrectomy
Underpowered, closed early; the OS difference is not considered practice-changing
Nephron-sparing surgery remains preferred for T1a to preserve renal function
trials.takeaway: The only RCT comparing partial and radical nephrectomy did not show OS non-inferiority, but it was underpowered and partial nephrectomy remains standard for small tumors.

trials.name: CheckMate 025
trials.descriptor: nivolumab vs everolimus after 1-2 prior antiangiogenic regimens
trials.population: Advanced ccRCC previously treated with 1-2 antiangiogenic regimens
trials.arms: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV q2w vs everolimus 10 mg PO daily
trials.results: OS 25.0 vs 19.6 mo, HR 0.73; ORR 25% vs 5%; PFS 4.6 vs 4.4 mo (no difference)
trials.toxicity: Fewer grade 3-4 AEs with nivolumab than everolimus
trials.reference: Motzer RJ et al. N Engl J Med 2015;373:1803-1813
highlights: First PD-1 inhibitor to improve OS in RCC
OS benefit without a PFS difference
Now relevant mainly for IO-naive patients after a TKI
trials.takeaway: Nivolumab improves overall survival over everolimus in previously treated advanced ccRCC.

trials.name: Study 205 (lenvatinib + everolimus)
trials.descriptor: lenvatinib + everolimus vs lenvatinib vs everolimus after one prior VEGF-targeted therapy
trials.population: Metastatic clear-cell RCC after one prior VEGF-targeted therapy
trials.arms: Lenvatinib 18 mg + everolimus 5 mg vs lenvatinib 24 mg vs everolimus 10 mg, randomized 1:1:1
trials.results: Combination vs everolimus: PFS 14.6 vs 5.5 mo, HR 0.40 (95% CI 0.24-0.68), P=0.0005; vs lenvatinib alone 7.4 mo, HR 0.66 (NS)
trials.toxicity: Diarrhea, fatigue, hypertension; two treatment-related deaths
trials.reference: Motzer RJ et al. Lancet Oncol 2015;16:1473-1482
highlights: Randomized phase 2 basis for the approval of lenvatinib + everolimus
Not superior to lenvatinib alone
Remains a post-IO option
trials.takeaway: Lenvatinib plus everolimus prolongs PFS over everolimus alone after prior VEGF therapy.

trials.name: ASSURE (ECOG-ACRIN E2805)
trials.descriptor: adjuvant sunitinib or sorafenib vs placebo for high-risk non-metastatic RCC
trials.population: Resected high-risk non-metastatic RCC (clear-cell and non-clear-cell)
trials.arms: Sunitinib 50 mg 4 of 6 weeks vs sorafenib 400 mg BID vs placebo, 54 weeks
trials.results: Median DFS 5.8 yr sunitinib (HR 1.02, 97.5% CI 0.85-1.23), 6.1 yr sorafenib (HR 0.97, 0.80-1.17), 6.6 yr placebo - no benefit
trials.toxicity: Substantial grade >=3 toxicity (hypertension, hand-foot, fatigue); many dose reductions
trials.reference: Haas NB et al. Lancet 2016;387:2008-2016
highlights: Largest adjuvant TKI trial - completely negative
Contrasts with S-TRAC, which used sunitinib in a higher-risk clear-cell population
Toxicity led to protocol dose reductions
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant sunitinib or sorafenib does not improve disease-free survival after resection of high-risk RCC.

trials.name: METEOR
trials.descriptor: cabozantinib vs everolimus after prior VEGFR TKI
trials.population: Advanced clear-cell RCC progressing after >=1 VEGFR TKI
trials.arms: Cabozantinib 60 mg PO daily vs everolimus 10 mg PO daily
trials.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival (first 375 patients); OS and ORR secondary
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4: hypertension 15%, diarrhea 13%, fatigue 11%, hand-foot; frequent dose reductions
trials.reference: Choueiri TK et al. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:917-927
highlights: Improved PFS, OS and ORR over everolimus
Made cabozantinib the post-TKI workhorse
Active in bone metastases
trials.takeaway: Cabozantinib improves overall survival over everolimus after prior VEGF TKI therapy.

trials.name: S-TRAC
trials.descriptor: adjuvant sunitinib vs placebo after nephrectomy in high-risk locoregional ccRCC
trials.population: Locoregional high-risk clear-cell RCC after nephrectomy (UISS high-risk criteria)
trials.arms: Sunitinib 50 mg PO daily 4-on/2-off × 1 year vs placebo
trials.primary_endpoint: Disease-free survival by blinded independent central review
trials.results: DFS 6.8 vs 5.6 years, HR 0.76 (0.59-0.98), P=0.03. OS immature at primary analysis; updated OS not significant, HR 0.92 (0.66-1.28) (Motzer, Eur Urol 2018)
trials.toxicity: Grade 3 AEs 48.4% vs 15.8%, grade 4 12.1% vs 3.6%; dose reductions 34.3%, discontinuations 28.1% vs 5.6%
trials.reference: Ravaud A et al. NEJM 2016;375:2246
highlights: The only adjuvant TKI trial to show a DFS benefit (ASSURE, PROTECT and ATLAS were negative)
No overall survival benefit and heavy toxicity (28% discontinuation) — displaced by adjuvant pembrolizumab
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant sunitinib prolongs DFS by about a year in high-risk resected ccRCC but at substantial toxicity and with no survival benefit.

trials.name: CABOSUN (Alliance A031203)
trials.descriptor: cabozantinib vs sunitinib in untreated IMDC intermediate/poor-risk metastatic RCC
trials.population: Untreated clear-cell mRCC, ECOG 0-2, IMDC intermediate or poor risk
trials.arms: Cabozantinib 60 mg PO daily (n=79) vs sunitinib 50 mg PO daily 4-on/2-off (n=78)
trials.results: PFS 8.2 vs 5.6 mo; adjusted HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.46-0.95), one-sided P=0.012; ORR 33% vs 12%. OS was secondary and not significantly different
trials.toxicity: All-causality grade 3-4 AEs 67% vs 68%; hypertension 28% vs 22%; hematologic AEs 3% vs 22%
trials.reference: Choueiri TK et al. JCO 2017;35:591
highlights: Basis for single-agent cabozantinib as a 1L option in intermediate/poor-risk disease when IO is not feasible
Randomized PHASE 2 with only 157 patients, a one-sided p-value and no OS benefit — frequently misremembered as a phase 3
trials.takeaway: Cabozantinib beat sunitinib on PFS and response rate in untreated intermediate/poor-risk mRCC, but in a small randomized phase 2 with no survival benefit.

trials.name: PROTECT
trials.descriptor: adjuvant pazopanib vs placebo after nephrectomy for localized or locally advanced clear-cell RCC
trials.population: Resected pT2 high-grade or >=pT3 (including N1) ccRCC
trials.arms: Pazopanib (800 mg, amended to 600 mg starting dose) vs placebo for 1 year
trials.primary_endpoint: Disease-free survival in the 600 mg ITT population
trials.results: Primary analysis (600 mg): DFS HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.70-1.06), P=0.165 - not met. 800 mg cohort secondary DFS HR 0.69 (0.51-0.94)
trials.toxicity: Hepatotoxicity (ALT/AST elevation) drove discontinuations
trials.reference: Motzer RJ et al. J Clin Oncol 2017;35:3916-3923
highlights: Dose was lowered mid-trial for toxicity, and the 600 mg primary analysis was negative
No OS benefit
Reinforces that adjuvant VEGF TKIs do not work
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant pazopanib did not improve disease-free survival in resected clear-cell RCC.

trials.name: ATLAS
trials.descriptor: adjuvant axitinib vs placebo after nephrectomy for high-risk RCC
trials.population: Resected RCC at risk of recurrence (predominantly clear cell), largely Asian population
trials.arms: Axitinib vs placebo for up to 3 years
trials.results: Stopped for futility at a preplanned interim analysis. DFS HR 0.870 (95% CI 0.660-1.147), P=0.32. OS immature
trials.toxicity: Expected VEGF-TKI toxicity
trials.reference: Gross-Goupil M et al. Ann Oncol 2018;29:2371-2378
highlights: Third negative adjuvant VEGF-TKI trial (with ASSURE and PROTECT)
Highest-risk subgroup signal was exploratory only
Stopped for futility
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant axitinib did not improve disease-free survival and the trial was stopped for futility.

trials.name: CARMENA
trials.descriptor: sunitinib alone vs cytoreductive nephrectomy followed by sunitinib
trials.population: Synchronous metastatic clear-cell RCC at presentation, suitable candidates for nephrectomy, ECOG 0-1, MSKCC intermediate or poor risk
trials.arms: Cytoreductive nephrectomy → sunitinib 50 mg daily 4-on/2-off (n=226) vs sunitinib alone (n=224)
trials.results: At 50.9 mo and 326 deaths: sunitinib alone noninferior — stratified HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.71-1.10), median OS 18.4 vs 13.9 mo. No difference in ORR or PFS. Updated analysis (Méjean, Eur Urol 2021): HR 0.97 (0.79-1.19), OS 19.8 vs 15.6 mo; with ≥2 IMDC risk factors OS 31.2 vs 17.6 mo favoring sunitinib alone (HR 0.65, P=0.03), while 1 IMDC risk factor favored nephrectomy (31.4 vs 25.2 mo, HR 1.30, P=0.2)
trials.toxicity: Adverse events as anticipated in both groups; 22.5% in the nephrectomy arm never received sunitinib
trials.reference: Mejean A et al. NEJM 2018;379:417
highlights: Ended cytoreductive nephrectomy as routine standard of care in metastatic RCC requiring systemic therapy
Enrolled only intermediate/poor MSKCC risk and used sunitinib, not modern IO — good-performance patients with one risk factor and a large symptomatic primary may still benefit from surgery
trials.takeaway: Sunitinib alone was noninferior to cytoreductive nephrectomy followed by sunitinib in intermediate/poor-risk metastatic RCC, so upfront nephrectomy is no longer routine.

trials.name: CheckMate 214
trials.descriptor: nivolumab + ipilimumab vs sunitinib in untreated advanced clear-cell RCC
trials.population: Previously untreated advanced/metastatic ccRCC; efficacy co-primary endpoints assessed in IMDC intermediate/poor-risk patients (847 of 1096)
trials.arms: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV q3w × 4 → nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w vs sunitinib 50 mg PO daily 4-on/2-off
trials.primary_endpoint: Co-primary OS, ORR and PFS — in IMDC intermediate/poor-risk patients only
trials.results: Intermediate/poor risk at 25.2 mo: OS median NR vs 26.0 mo, HR 0.63, P<0.001; ORR 42% vs 27%, P<0.001; CR 9% vs 1%. PFS 11.6 vs 8.4 mo, HR 0.82, P=0.03 — did NOT meet the prespecified α of 0.009. At 99.1 mo (Tannir, Ann Oncol 2024): OS HR 0.69 int/poor, 0.72 ITT, 0.82 (0.60-1.13) favorable
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs 46% vs 63%; discontinuation for TRAE 22% vs 12%
trials.reference: Motzer RJ et al. NEJM 2018;378:1277
highlights: Established the IO/IO doublet as a 1L standard for IMDC intermediate/poor-risk disease — highest CR rate and most durable responses
PFS was a co-primary endpoint and formally failed; favorable-risk patients did not benefit (ORR numerically lower than sunitinib)
trials.takeaway: Ipi/nivo beats sunitinib on OS and ORR in intermediate/poor-risk advanced ccRCC with durable complete responses — but not on PFS, and not in favorable risk.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-426
trials.descriptor: pembrolizumab + axitinib vs sunitinib in untreated advanced clear-cell RCC
trials.population: Previously untreated advanced ccRCC; KPS ≥70; all IMDC risk groups
trials.arms: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w + axitinib 5 mg PO BID vs sunitinib 50 mg PO daily, 4 wk of each 6-wk cycle
trials.primary_endpoint: Dual primary — overall survival AND progression-free survival (ITT)
trials.results: At 12.8 mo: 12-mo OS 89.9% vs 78.3%, HR 0.53 (0.38-0.74), P<0.0001; PFS 15.1 vs 11.1 mo, HR 0.69 (0.57-0.84), P<0.001; ORR 59.3% vs 35.7%, P<0.001. Benefit across all IMDC risk groups and regardless of PD-L1. Final analysis at 43 mo (Plimack, Eur Urol 2023): OS HR 0.73 (0.60-0.88), PFS HR 0.68 (0.58-0.80), ORR 60% vs 40%; median DOR 24 vs 15 mo
trials.toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs 75.8% vs 70.6%; overlapping hepatotoxicity complicates attribution between the two drugs
trials.reference: Rini BI et al. NEJM 2019;380:1116
highlights: First IO/TKI combination to beat sunitinib on both OS and PFS - made IO/TKI a 1L standard including favorable-risk disease
OS benefit maintained at the final 43-month analysis (HR 0.73), attenuated from the early HR 0.53
Overlapping hepatotoxicity: hold both drugs and give steroids if ALT does not fall
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab + axitinib improved OS, PFS and response rate over sunitinib in untreated advanced ccRCC across all risk groups.

trials.name: SURTIME
trials.descriptor: immediate vs deferred cytoreductive nephrectomy with sunitinib
trials.population: Synchronous metastatic clear-cell RCC with resectable primary
trials.arms: Immediate nephrectomy then sunitinib vs 3 cycles of sunitinib then nephrectomy
trials.primary_endpoint: 28-week progression-free rate (amended from PFS for poor accrual)
trials.results: 28-week PFR not different. Exploratory ITT OS favored deferred CN: HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.34-0.95), median 32.4 vs 15.0 mo; 98% vs 80% received sunitinib
trials.toxicity: No excess surgical morbidity with deferral
trials.reference: Bex A et al. JAMA Oncol 2019;5:164-170
highlights: Closed after 5.7 years with only 99 of 458 planned patients
Deferral lets systemic therapy identify primary-resistant disease before surgery
Together with CARMENA, ended routine upfront cytoreductive nephrectomy
trials.takeaway: Deferring cytoreductive nephrectomy until after systemic therapy is reasonable and may select patients better; immediate surgery is not required.

trials.name: TIVO-3
trials.descriptor: tivozanib vs sorafenib in heavily pretreated metastatic RCC
trials.population: Metastatic RCC with ≥2 prior systemic regimens (≥1 prior VEGFR TKI); ECOG 0-1; ~26-28% prior checkpoint inhibitor
trials.arms: Tivozanib 1.5 mg PO daily in 4-wk cycles vs sorafenib 400 mg PO BID continuously
trials.results: PFS 5.6 vs 3.9 mo, HR 0.73 (0.56-0.94), P=0.016. No OS data in the primary publication; later analysis (Beckermann, Oncologist 2024) OS HR 0.89 (0.70-1.14), not significant, 3-yr PFS 12.3% vs 2.4%
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 treatment-related hypertension 20% vs 14%; serious treatment-related AEs 11% vs 10%; no treatment-related deaths
trials.reference: Rini BI et al. Lancet Oncol 2020;21:95
highlights: Supported FDA approval of tivozanib after ≥2 prior systemic therapies; better tolerated than sorafenib
Modest 1.7-month PFS gain, no OS benefit, and sorafenib is a weak comparator in the modern post-IO setting
trials.takeaway: Tivozanib modestly improves PFS over sorafenib in third/fourth-line RCC with good tolerability but no survival gain.

trials.name: CheckMate 9ER
trials.descriptor: nivolumab + cabozantinib vs sunitinib in untreated advanced clear-cell RCC
trials.population: Previously untreated advanced clear-cell RCC
trials.arms: Nivolumab 240 mg IV q2w + cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily vs sunitinib 50 mg PO daily, 4 wk of each 6-wk cycle
trials.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review
trials.results: At 18.1 mo: PFS 16.6 vs 8.3 mo, HR 0.51 (0.41-0.64), P<0.001; 12-mo OS 85.7% vs 75.6%, HR 0.60 (98.89% CI 0.40-0.89), P=0.001; ORR 55.7% vs 27.1%, P<0.001. Health-related quality of life favored the combination. Final analysis at 5.6 yr (Motzer, Ann Oncol 2025): PFS 16.4 vs 8.3 mo, HR 0.58 (0.49-0.70); OS 46.5 vs 35.5 mo, HR 0.79 (0.65-0.96); ORR 55.7% vs 27.4%, CR 13.9% vs 4.6%; 60-mo OS 40.9% vs 35.4%
trials.toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs 75.3% vs 70.6%; 19.7% discontinued ≥1 drug for AEs, 5.6% discontinued both
trials.reference: Choueiri TK et al. NEJM 2021;384:829
highlights: IO/TKI option with the best reported quality-of-life data; cabozantinib is dosed at 40 mg here, not the 60 mg monotherapy dose
Primary endpoint was PFS alone; OS was secondary, reported with a 98.89% CI at short follow-up
Final 5.6-year analysis confirmed OS benefit (HR 0.79), attenuated from the early HR 0.60
trials.takeaway: Nivolumab + cabozantinib doubled PFS and improved OS and response rate versus sunitinib in untreated advanced ccRCC.

trials.name: CLEAR
trials.descriptor: lenvatinib + pembrolizumab or + everolimus vs sunitinib in untreated advanced RCC
trials.population: Advanced RCC, no prior systemic therapy; 1:1:1 randomization
trials.arms: Lenvatinib 20 mg PO daily + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w; lenvatinib 18 mg + everolimus 5 mg PO daily; sunitinib 50 mg PO daily 4-on/2-off
trials.results: Lenvatinib+pembrolizumab vs sunitinib: PFS 23.9 vs 9.2 mo, HR 0.39 (0.32-0.49), P<0.001; OS HR 0.66 (0.49-0.88), P=0.005; ORR 71.0% vs 36.1%. Lenvatinib+everolimus vs sunitinib: PFS 14.7 vs 9.2 mo, HR 0.65; OS HR 1.15 (0.88-1.50), P=0.30 — no OS benefit. Final prespecified OS (Motzer, JCO 2024): OS HR 0.79 (0.63-0.99), median 53.7 vs 54.3 mo; PFS 23.9 vs 9.2 mo, HR 0.47; ORR 71.3% vs 36.7%
trials.toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs 82.4% (len+pembro), 83.1% (len+eve), 71.8% (sunitinib); hypertension, diarrhea, lipase elevation
trials.reference: Motzer R et al. NEJM 2021;384:1289
highlights: Longest median PFS reported for any 1L RCC regimen (23.9 mo) — a preferred IO/TKI option across IMDC risk groups
Primary endpoint was PFS only; the lenvatinib+everolimus arm showed no OS benefit and is not a 1L standard
At the final OS analysis the HR still favored lenvatinib + pembrolizumab (0.79) but median OS was identical (53.7 vs 54.3 mo)
trials.takeaway: Lenvatinib + pembrolizumab roughly doubles PFS and improves OS versus sunitinib in untreated advanced RCC, at the cost of high-grade toxicity.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-427 Cohort B
trials.descriptor: pembrolizumab monotherapy as first-line therapy for advanced non-clear-cell RCC
trials.population: Untreated advanced nccRCC: 71.5% papillary, 12.7% chromophobe, 15.8% unclassified
trials.arms: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w, single-arm
trials.results: ORR 26.7%, median DOR 29.0 mo; PD-L1 CPS >=1 35.3% vs CPS <1 12.1%; mPFS 4.2 mo; mOS 28.9 mo
trials.toxicity: Treatment-related AEs 69.7%
trials.reference: McDermott DF et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1029-1039
highlights: Modest activity of IO alone in nccRCC
Durable responses when they occur
Chromophobe responds poorly
trials.takeaway: Single-agent pembrolizumab has modest but durable activity in non-clear-cell RCC.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-564
trials.descriptor: pembrolizumab vs placebo after nephrectomy in high-risk clear-cell RCC
trials.population: ccRCC at increased risk of recurrence after nephrectomy ± metastasectomy (intermediate-high, high risk, or M1 NED); surgery ≤12 wk prior; ECOG 0-1
trials.arms: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w × up to 17 cycles (~1 yr) vs placebo
trials.toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs 32.4% vs 17.7%; treatment-related grade 3-4 18.6% vs 1.2%; no treatment-related deaths
trials.reference: Choueiri TK et al. NEJM 2021;385:683
highlights: First adjuvant therapy in RCC to show an OS benefit (2024 update) — now standard of care for resected high-risk ccRCC
ITT included M1 NED (fully resected oligometastatic) patients; benefit in true M0 disease is smaller, so selection matters
trials.takeaway: One year of adjuvant pembrolizumab improves DFS and, on longer follow-up, overall survival in resected high-risk ccRCC.

trials.name: LITESPARK-004
trials.descriptor: belzutifan in von Hippel-Lindau disease-associated renal cell carcinoma
trials.population: Germline VHL with at least one measurable RCC, no metastases, not requiring immediate surgery
trials.arms: Belzutifan 120 mg PO daily, single-arm
trials.results: At 21.8 mo: RCC ORR 49% (95% CI 36-62). Responses in pancreatic lesions 77% and CNS hemangioblastomas 30%
trials.toxicity: Anemia (on-target) and fatigue most common; hypoxia
trials.reference: Jonasch E et al. N Engl J Med 2021;385:2036-2046
highlights: Led to FDA approval for VHL-associated RCC, hemangioblastomas and pNET (August 2021)
Single-arm trial
Reduces the need for repeated nephron-sparing surgery
trials.takeaway: Belzutifan shrinks VHL-associated kidney, pancreatic and CNS tumors and is the systemic standard in VHL disease.

trials.name: SWOG S1500 (PAPMET)
trials.descriptor: sunitinib vs cabozantinib vs crizotinib vs savolitinib in metastatic papillary RCC
trials.population: Metastatic papillary RCC, ≤1 prior therapy (excluding VEGF- and MET-directed agents); 152 randomized, 147 analyzed
trials.arms: Sunitinib 50 mg 4-on/2-off (n=46) vs cabozantinib 60 mg daily (n=44) vs crizotinib 250 mg BID (n=28) vs savolitinib 600 mg daily (n=29)
trials.results: Cabozantinib vs sunitinib: PFS 9.0 vs 5.6 mo, HR 0.60 (0.37-0.97), one-sided P=0.019; ORR 23% vs 4%, P=0.010. Savolitinib and crizotinib arms closed early for futility. Final OS (Barata, JCO 2024): 21.5 vs 17.3 mo, HR 0.83, P=0.46 — no difference
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 AEs: sunitinib 69%, cabozantinib 74%, crizotinib 37%, savolitinib 39%; one grade 5 thromboembolic event with cabozantinib
trials.reference: Pal SK et al. Lancet 2021;397:695
highlights: Established cabozantinib as the reference regimen for metastatic papillary RCC — a rare disease with almost no randomized data
Randomized phase 2 with ~45 patients per active arm, a one-sided p-value and no OS benefit; unselected MET inhibitors failed
trials.takeaway: Cabozantinib outperformed sunitinib on PFS and response in metastatic papillary RCC while MET inhibitors failed, though without a survival benefit.

trials.name: Cabozantinib + nivolumab in nccRCC (phase 2)
trials.descriptor: cabozantinib + nivolumab in non-clear-cell RCC with genomic correlates
trials.population: Advanced nccRCC: cohort 1 papillary/unclassified/translocation, cohort 2 chromophobe
trials.arms: Cabozantinib 40 mg daily + nivolumab 240 mg q2w (or 480 q4w), single-arm
trials.results: Cohort 1 (n=40): ORR 47.5%, mPFS 12.5 mo, mOS 28 mo. Cohort 2 chromophobe (n=7): no responses
trials.toxicity: Grade 3/4 treatment-related AEs in about a third
trials.reference: Lee CH et al. J Clin Oncol 2022;40:2333-2341
highlights: High activity in papillary and unclassified RCC
No activity in chromophobe
Small single-arm study
trials.takeaway: Cabozantinib plus nivolumab is active in papillary and unclassified RCC but not in chromophobe RCC.

trials.name: IMmotion010
trials.descriptor: adjuvant atezolizumab vs placebo after resection of RCC at increased risk of recurrence
trials.population: RCC with clear-cell or sarcomatoid component at increased risk of recurrence after nephrectomy +/- metastasectomy
trials.arms: Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV q3w for 16 cycles or 1 year vs placebo
trials.results: At 44.7 mo: median DFS 57.2 vs 49.5 mo; HR 0.93 (95% CI 0.75-1.15), P=0.50 - primary endpoint not met
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 AEs low and similar; hypertension and hyperglycemia most common
trials.reference: Pal SK et al. Lancet 2022;400:1103-1116
highlights: Anti-PD-L1 adjuvant therapy failed where anti-PD-1 (pembrolizumab) succeeded
Exploratory: high post-nephrectomy KIM-1 identified patients who may benefit
One of three negative adjuvant IO phase 3 trials
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant atezolizumab does not improve disease-free survival in resected RCC.

trials.name: CheckMate 914 (Part A)
trials.descriptor: adjuvant nivolumab + ipilimumab vs placebo after nephrectomy for high-risk clear-cell RCC
trials.population: Localized ccRCC at high risk of relapse, 4-12 weeks after radical or partial nephrectomy
trials.arms: Nivolumab 240 mg IV q2w x12 doses + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6w x4 doses (24 weeks) vs placebo
trials.primary_endpoint: Disease-free survival by blinded independent central review
trials.results: At 37.0 mo: median DFS not reached vs 50.7 mo; HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.71-1.19), P=0.53 - primary endpoint not met
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-5 AEs 38% vs 10%; 32% discontinued for AEs; 4 treatment-related deaths
trials.reference: Motzer RJ et al. Lancet 2023;401:821-832
highlights: Adding CTLA-4 blockade to adjuvant PD-1 therapy gave no DFS benefit
One third of patients stopped therapy for toxicity
Part of the set of negative adjuvant IO trials that leave KEYNOTE-564 standing alone
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab does not improve disease-free survival after nephrectomy and should not be used.

trials.name: CONTACT-03
trials.setting: advanced RCC after immune checkpoint inhibitor
trials.descriptor: atezolizumab + cabozantinib vs cabozantinib after progression on prior ICI
trials.population: Advanced clear-cell or papillary/unclassified RCC progressing on or after anti-PD-(L)1
trials.arms: Atezolizumab 1200 mg q3w + cabozantinib 60 mg daily vs cabozantinib 60 mg daily
trials.primary_endpoint: PFS by blinded central review and OS (dual primary)
trials.results: PFS 10.6 vs 10.8 mo, HR 1.03 (95% CI 0.83-1.28), P=0.78; OS 25.7 mo vs not evaluable, HR 0.94 (0.70-1.27), P=0.69 - both negative
trials.toxicity: More serious AEs and discontinuations with the combination
trials.reference: Pal SK et al. Lancet 2023;402:185-195
highlights: First randomized test of IO rechallenge in RCC - no benefit
Adds toxicity without efficacy
Established that after IO the next line is a TKI alone
trials.takeaway: Adding atezolizumab to cabozantinib after prior IO gives no PFS or OS benefit - do not rechallenge with IO.

trials.name: COSMIC-313
trials.descriptor: cabozantinib + nivolumab + ipilimumab vs placebo + nivolumab + ipilimumab
trials.population: Untreated advanced ccRCC, IMDC intermediate or poor risk
trials.arms: Cabozantinib 40 mg daily + nivolumab + ipilimumab (x4) vs placebo + nivolumab + ipilimumab
trials.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival by blinded independent review
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 AEs 79% vs 56%
trials.reference: Choueiri TK et al. N Engl J Med 2023;388:1767-1778; final analysis Ann Oncol 2026
highlights: Triplet improved PFS but not overall survival
Substantially more grade 3-4 toxicity
Triplet therapy is not a standard of care
trials.takeaway: Adding cabozantinib to ipilimumab/nivolumab improves PFS but not OS, with much more toxicity - the triplet is not used.

trials.name: KEYNOTE-B61
trials.descriptor: pembrolizumab + lenvatinib in untreated advanced non-clear-cell RCC
trials.population: Untreated stage IV nccRCC (papillary, chromophobe, unclassified, other), KPS >=70
trials.arms: Pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w (up to 18 cycles) + lenvatinib 20 mg daily, single-arm
trials.primary_endpoint: Confirmed ORR by independent central review
trials.results: ORR 49% (95% CI 41-57), CR 6%. Updated at 22.8 mo (Voss, Eur Urol 2025): ORR 51%, CR 8.2%, median DOR 19.5 mo; sarcomatoid ORR 47%
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs 51-58%; hypertension 23%
trials.reference: Albiges L et al. Lancet Oncol 2023;24:881-891
highlights: Largest prospective IO/TKI data set in non-clear-cell RCC
Single-arm - no comparator
Activity across histologic subtypes (ORR 34-67%)
trials.takeaway: Pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib is highly active in untreated non-clear-cell RCC in a single-arm phase 2 trial.

trials.name: LITESPARK-005
trials.descriptor: belzutifan vs everolimus after IO and anti-angiogenic therapy
trials.population: Advanced ccRCC progressing after anti-PD-1/PD-L1 and VEGF-targeted therapy; 1-3 prior lines; KPS ≥70
trials.arms: Belzutifan 120 mg PO daily vs everolimus 10 mg PO daily
trials.primary_endpoint: Dual primary — progression-free survival (BICR) AND overall survival
trials.results: Median PFS 5.6 mo in BOTH arms; 18-mo PFS 24.0% vs 8.3%, P=0.002 (met). Confirmed ORR 21.9% vs 3.5%, P<0.001. At 25.7 mo: OS 21.4 vs 18.1 mo, HR 0.88 (0.73-1.07), P=0.20 — OS co-primary NOT met
trials.toxicity: Grade ≥3 AEs 61.8% vs 62.5%; discontinuation for AEs 5.9% vs 14.7%. Class effects: anemia, hypoxia
trials.reference: Choueiri TK et al. NEJM 2024;391:710
highlights: First HIF-2α inhibitor with a positive phase 3 in RCC — a genuinely new mechanism for post-IO, post-TKI disease
Medians are identical (5.6 vs 5.6 mo): the benefit is entirely in the tail of the curve, and the OS co-primary failed
trials.takeaway: Belzutifan improves 18-month PFS and response rate over everolimus in refractory ccRCC without improving overall survival.

trials.name: PROSPER (ECOG-ACRIN EA8143)
trials.descriptor: perioperative nivolumab (neoadjuvant dose + adjuvant) vs surgery alone for high-risk RCC
trials.population: Clinical stage T2 or greater or N+ RCC of any histology planned for nephrectomy; selected oligometastatic patients
trials.arms: Nivolumab 480 mg once before surgery then 9 adjuvant doses vs nephrectomy followed by surveillance
trials.results: Stopped at interim for futility. RFS HR 0.94 (95% CI 0.74-1.21), one-sided P=0.32
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-5 AEs 48% vs 24%; treatment-related deaths 2% vs 1%
trials.reference: Allaf ME et al. Lancet Oncol 2024;25:1038-1052
highlights: The only large trial to test a neoadjuvant IO dose in RCC - no benefit
Enrolled clear-cell and non-clear-cell histology
Stopped early for futility
trials.takeaway: Perioperative nivolumab did not improve recurrence-free survival over nephrectomy alone.

trials.name: TiNivo-2
trials.setting: advanced RCC after immune checkpoint inhibitor
trials.descriptor: tivozanib + nivolumab vs tivozanib monotherapy after prior ICI
trials.population: Advanced RCC progressing after 1-2 prior lines including an ICI
trials.arms: Tivozanib 0.89 mg daily + nivolumab 480 mg q4w vs tivozanib 1.34 mg daily
trials.results: PFS 5.7 vs 7.4 mo, HR 1.10 (95% CI 0.84-1.43), P=0.49 - negative. With ICI as the immediately prior therapy: 7.4 vs 9.2 mo
trials.toxicity: Similar grade >=3 toxicity
trials.reference: Choueiri TK et al. Lancet 2024;404:1309-1320
highlights: Second negative IO-rechallenge phase 3 after CONTACT-03
Numerically worse PFS with the combination
Tivozanib dose was reduced in the combination arm
trials.takeaway: Adding nivolumab to tivozanib after prior IO does not improve PFS; IO rechallenge is not recommended.

trials.name: CheckMate 914 (Part B)
trials.descriptor: adjuvant nivolumab monotherapy vs placebo after nephrectomy for high-risk clear-cell RCC
trials.population: Localized ccRCC at high risk of recurrence after nephrectomy
trials.arms: Nivolumab 240 mg q2w up to 12 doses vs placebo (vs a nivolumab + ipilimumab arm), randomized 2:1:1
trials.primary_endpoint: Disease-free survival by blinded independent central review (nivolumab vs placebo)
trials.results: At 27.0 mo: DFS HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.62-1.21), P=0.40; 18-month DFS 78.4% vs 75.4% - primary endpoint not met. Investigator-assessed DFS HR 0.80 (0.58-1.12)
trials.toxicity: Grade 3-4 all-cause AEs ~17% with nivolumab
trials.reference: Motzer RJ et al. J Clin Oncol 2025;43:189-200
highlights: Six months of adjuvant anti-PD-1 did not beat placebo, unlike 1 year of pembrolizumab in KEYNOTE-564
Shorter treatment duration and trial population differences are proposed explanations
No regulatory approval for adjuvant nivolumab in RCC
trials.takeaway: Adjuvant nivolumab alone did not improve disease-free survival in high-risk resected RCC.

trials.name: NCI bevacizumab + erlotinib (HLRCC / papillary)
trials.setting: advanced HLRCC-associated and sporadic papillary RCC
trials.descriptor: bevacizumab + erlotinib in hereditary leiomyomatosis RCC and sporadic papillary RCC
trials.population: 43 HLRCC-associated and 40 sporadic advanced papillary RCC
trials.arms: Bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV q2w + erlotinib 150 mg PO daily, single-arm
trials.results: HLRCC: ORR 72%, mPFS 21.1 mo, mOS 44.6 mo. Sporadic papillary: ORR 35%, mPFS 8.9 mo, mOS 18.2 mo
trials.toxicity: Acneiform rash 93%, diarrhea 89%, proteinuria 78%; grade >=3 hypertension 34%, proteinuria 17%
trials.reference: Srinivasan R et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392:2346-2356
highlights: The reference regimen for FH-deficient (HLRCC) RCC
Much greater activity in HLRCC than sporadic papillary RCC
Single-arm, single-institution (NCI)
trials.takeaway: Bevacizumab plus erlotinib produces high, durable response rates in HLRCC-associated RCC.

trials.name: LITESPARK-011
trials.descriptor: belzutifan + lenvatinib vs cabozantinib after prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy
trials.population: Advanced ccRCC progressing after anti-PD-(L)1 (adjuvant or 1L-2L), +/- prior VEGF TKI
trials.arms: Belzutifan 120 mg + lenvatinib 20 mg PO daily vs cabozantinib 60 mg PO daily
trials.primary_endpoint: PFS by blinded central review and OS (dual primary)
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 TEAEs 84% vs 83%; hypertension ~30% in both arms
trials.reference: Motzer RJ et al. Lancet 2026;408:808-820
highlights: Beat the cabozantinib standard on PFS after IO
OS not significantly improved at the second interim analysis
FDA sNDA under review, PDUFA date 4 October 2026 - not yet approved
trials.takeaway: Belzutifan plus lenvatinib prolongs PFS over cabozantinib after prior IO, without a significant OS gain so far.

trials.name: LITESPARK-022
trials.descriptor: adjuvant pembrolizumab + belzutifan vs pembrolizumab + placebo for clear-cell RCC at increased risk of recurrence
trials.population: ccRCC at intermediate-high or high risk of recurrence after nephrectomy, or after nephrectomy + resection of metastases (NED)
trials.arms: Pembrolizumab 400 mg q6w (<=9 doses) + belzutifan 120 mg PO daily vs pembrolizumab + placebo, up to 1 year
trials.toxicity: Grade >=3 AEs 52.1% vs 30.2%; belzutifan anemia and hypoxia
trials.reference: Choueiri TK et al. N Engl J Med 2026;395:32-43
highlights: FDA approved belzutifan + pembrolizumab as adjuvant therapy on 12 June 2026
DFS gain comes with a near doubling of grade >=3 toxicity; OS not yet shown
First positive adjuvant combination in RCC - built on KEYNOTE-564
trials.takeaway: Adding belzutifan to adjuvant pembrolizumab improves disease-free survival in higher-risk resected ccRCC, at the cost of more toxicity and with OS still immature.

trials.name: PRODIGE 23
trials.descriptor: induction mFOLFIRINOX before chemoradiation
trials.population: cT3–4 rectal cancer, any N, M0 (locally advanced)
trials.arms: mFOLFIRINOX × 6 → chemoRT → TME → adjuvant mFOLFOX6 × 6 vs chemoRT → TME → adjuvant mFOLFOX6 × 12
trials.results: 3-yr DFS 75.7% vs 68.5% (HR 0.69); pCR 27.8% vs 12.1%; 7-yr OS 81.9% vs 76.1% (HR 0.69, 2023 update); metastasis-free survival improved
trials.toxicity: Grade 3–4 neutropenia and diarrhea during induction; neuropathy
trials.reference: Conroy T et al. Lancet Oncol 2021;22:702; ASCO 2023 (7-yr)
highlights: Induction-first TNT with a triplet improves DFS, OS and pCR without the RAPIDO local-recurrence signal — the preferred TNT sequence for high-risk tumors.
Adjuvant chemotherapy duration is shortened when induction is given (6 months total perioperative).
trials.takeaway: Induction mFOLFIRINOX → chemoRT → TME improves DFS, OS and pCR in locally advanced rectal cancer

trials.name: RAPIDO
trials.descriptor: short-course RT → CAPOX/FOLFOX → TME (total neoadjuvant therapy)
trials.population: High-risk locally advanced rectal cancer on MRI (cT4, N2, EMVI+, threatened MRF, or lateral nodes)
trials.arms: Short-course RT (5×5 Gy) → CAPOX × 6 or FOLFOX × 9 → TME vs long-course chemoRT → TME → optional adjuvant chemo
trials.results: 3-yr DrTF 23.7% vs 30.4% (HR 0.75); pCR 28% vs 14%; distant metastases 20% vs 27%. 5-yr locoregional failure 10% vs 6% (Dijkstra, Ann Surg 2023) — a local-recurrence signal against TNT-first
trials.reference: Bahadoer RR et al. Lancet Oncol 2021;22:29; Dijkstra EA et al. Ann Surg 2023;278:e766 (5-yr)
highlights: Established TNT: doubles pCR and reduces distant relapse — but the 5-year update showed more local recurrence, so high-risk disease now favors induction chemo → chemoRT (rather than short-course RT first).
Short-course RT (5 fractions) with consolidation chemo is a valid, patient-friendly TNT sequence when RT sensitivity matters more than local control.
trials.takeaway: Short-course RT + consolidation chemo (TNT) doubles pCR and lowers distant relapse, with a possible increase in local recurrence

trials.name: OPRA
trials.descriptor: watch-and-wait after clinical complete response to TNT
trials.population: Stage II–III rectal adenocarcinoma (distal/mid rectum)
trials.arms: Induction chemo → chemoRT (INCT-CRT) vs chemoRT → consolidation chemo (CRT-CNCT); cCR/near-cCR patients offered watch-and-wait, others TME
trials.results: 3-yr DFS 76% vs 76% (both arms; similar to historical TME); TME-free survival 41% (INCT-CRT) vs 53% (CRT-CNCT); local regrowth ~25–30%, salvaged surgically without loss of DFS
trials.reference: Garcia-Aguilar J et al. JCO 2022;40:2546; Verheij FS et al. JCO 2024 (5-yr)
highlights: Organ preservation is safe for patients achieving cCR after TNT: half avoid surgery without compromising DFS. Consolidation chemo after chemoRT gives the higher organ-preservation rate.
Watch-and-wait requires cCR on all three of DRE, MRI and endoscopy, plus rigorous surveillance to catch regrowth.
trials.takeaway: Watch-and-wait after clinical complete response to TNT preserves the rectum in ~50% without compromising DFS

trials.name: PROSPECT (Alliance N1048)
trials.descriptor: neoadjuvant FOLFOX with selective chemoradiation vs routine chemoradiation
trials.population: cT2N+ or cT3N0–1 rectal cancer, candidates for sphincter-sparing surgery, not T4, ≤4 nodes, no threatened margin
trials.arms: FOLFOX × 6 with chemoRT only if <20% tumor regression vs standard 5-FU/capecitabine chemoradiation (both → TME ± adjuvant chemo)
trials.results: 5-yr DFS 80.8% vs 78.6% (HR 0.92) — non-inferior; only 9% in the FOLFOX arm needed chemoradiation; pCR 21.9% vs 24.3%; local recurrence 1.8% vs 1.6%
trials.toxicity: Less long-term bowel/sexual dysfunction without RT; more neuropathy and neutropenia acutely with FOLFOX
trials.reference: Schrag D et al. NEJM 2023;389:322
highlights: Radiation can be omitted in ~90% of intermediate-risk rectal cancers (non-T4, ≤4 nodes, sphincter-sparing candidates) by using FOLFOX and restaging.
Does not apply to low tumors needing APR, T4, or ≥5 nodes — those still get TNT with radiation.
trials.takeaway: Neoadjuvant FOLFOX with selective chemoRT is non-inferior to routine chemoradiation in intermediate-risk rectal cancer

trials.name: Einhorn 3 vs 4 cycles BEP (SECSG)
trials.descriptor: three vs four cycles of cisplatin + etoposide + bleomycin in favorable-prognosis disseminated germ cell tumor
trials.population: 184 patients with favorable-prognosis (Indiana minimal or moderate extent) disseminated GCT; Southeastern Cancer Study Group; minimum 1-year follow-up
trials.arms: 3 courses BEP over 9 weeks (n=88) vs 4 courses over 12 weeks (n=96), identical doses per cycle
trials.primary_endpoint: Disease-free (NED) status and relapse — no formally powered primary endpoint stated
trials.results: Equivalent. NED in 86/88 (98%) with 3 cycles vs 93/96 (97%) with 4. Ten relapses total (5%), 5 per arm. Continuously disease-free 92% in both arms
trials.toxicity: Dropping the fourth course reduced toxicity, cost and inconvenience; not quantified
trials.reference: Einhorn LH et al. JCO 1989;7:387
highlights: Established 3×BEP as the standard for good-risk disseminated GCT
Predates IGCCCG — 'favorable' here means Indiana minimal/moderate extent, not IGCCCG good risk; small, short follow-up, no pre-specified equivalence margin
trials.takeaway: Three cycles of BEP equal four in favorable-prognosis disseminated germ cell tumor, with less toxicity.

trials.name: IGCCCG classification (1997) + update (2021)
trials.descriptor: pooled multinational prognostic analysis defining good / intermediate / poor risk in metastatic germ cell tumor
trials.population: 1997: 5,202 nonseminoma + 660 seminoma treated with cisplatin-based chemotherapy across 10 countries. 2021 update: 9,728 NSGCT and 2,451 seminoma treated 1990-2013 at 30 institutions with independent validation
trials.arms: Not applicable — retrospective pooled prognostic modeling, not a treatment comparison
trials.primary_endpoint: Progression-free and overall survival modeled against baseline prognostic variables
trials.results: 1997: good risk 60% of patients, 5-yr OS 91%; intermediate 26%, 79%; poor 14% (all NSGCT), 48%. Adverse factors — mediastinal primary, degree of AFP/hCG/LDH elevation, non-pulmonary visceral metastases (for seminoma, only non-pulmonary visceral mets). 2021 NSGCT update (Gillessen S, JCO 2021;39:1563, PMID 33822655): 5-yr OS good 96%, intermediate 89%, poor 67%; new adverse factors LDH >2.5× ULN, increasing age, lung metastases. 2021 seminoma update (Beyer J, JCO 2021;39:1553, PMID 33729863): 5-yr OS good 95%, intermediate 88%; LDH >2.5× ULN added
trials.reference: IGCCCG. JCO 1997;15:594
highlights: The universal risk framework for metastatic GCT — drives 3×BEP vs 4×BEP/VIP and stratifies essentially every trial
2021 update kept the three groups valid but showed far better modern outcomes (poor-risk 5-yr OS 48% → 67%) and added LDH >2.5× ULN
Retrospective and pooled, not a trial; the 2021 NSGCT and seminoma analyses are separate papers with different first authors
trials.takeaway: IGCCCG splits metastatic GCT into good, intermediate and poor risk by primary site, markers and visceral metastases; the 2021 update confirms the groups and shows markedly improved modern survival.

trials.name: EORTC 30941 / MRC TE20
trials.descriptor: 2×2 factorial of 3 vs 4 cycles BEP and 5-day vs 3-day administration in good-prognosis germ cell cancer
trials.population: 812 patients with good-prognosis germ cell cancer randomized to 3 vs 4 cycles (1995-1998); 681 also randomized to the 5-day vs 3-day schedule
trials.arms: 3 vs 4 cycles BEP; and etoposide 500 mg/m² per cycle given as 100 mg/m² d1-5 vs 165 mg/m² d1-3, cisplatin 100 mg/m² as 20 mg/m² d1-5 vs 50 mg/m² d1-2
trials.primary_endpoint: 2-year progression-free survival; equivalence design ruling out a 5% decrease
trials.results: Equivalent on both axes. 3 vs 4 cycles: 2-yr PFS 90.4% vs 89.4%, difference −1.0% (80% CL −3.8 to +1.8). 5-day vs 3-day: 88.8% vs 89.7%, difference −0.9% (80% CL −4.1 to +2.2). Both within the 5% margin
trials.toxicity: Hematologic and non-hematologic toxicity similar across arms; quality of life better maintained with 3 cycles; no QoL difference between schedules
trials.reference: de Wit R et al. JCO 2001;19:1629
highlights: Confirmed 3×BEP (etoposide 500 mg/m² per cycle) as sufficient for good-prognosis GCT in the IGCCCG era, and validated the 3-day schedule
Commonly misdescribed as 3×BEP vs 4×EP — it is 3 vs 4 cycles of BEP. The 4×EP data come from a separate single-arm MSKCC series
trials.takeaway: Three cycles of BEP suffice for good-prognosis germ cell cancer, and compressing each cycle to 3 days does not compromise efficacy.

trials.name: Kondagunta 4×EP (MSKCC)
trials.descriptor: four cycles of etoposide + cisplatin without bleomycin in good-risk germ cell tumor
trials.population: 289 patients with good-risk germ cell tumors treated at Memorial Sloan Kettering
trials.arms: Single arm: 4 cycles etoposide + cisplatin (no bleomycin)
trials.results: CR in 98% of patients — the basis for 4×EP as the bleomycin-free equivalent of 3×BEP
trials.toxicity: Avoids bleomycin pulmonary toxicity at the cost of one additional cycle of cisplatin/etoposide
trials.reference: Kondagunta GV et al. JCO 2005;23:9290
highlights: The evidence behind offering 4×EP instead of 3×BEP when bleomycin is undesirable — smokers, impaired lung function, older patients, planned thoracic surgery
Single-arm and never randomized against 3×BEP; the equivalence is inferred, not demonstrated
trials.takeaway: Four cycles of EP produce a 98% complete response rate in good-risk GCT and serve as the standard bleomycin-free alternative to 3×BEP.

trials.name: Kondagunta TIP salvage
trials.descriptor: four cycles of paclitaxel + ifosfamide + cisplatin as conventional-dose second-line therapy in favorable-prognosis relapsed testicular GCT
trials.population: 46 men with progressive metastatic testicular GCT; eligibility required both a testis primary and a prior complete response to first-line chemotherapy
trials.arms: Single arm: 4 cycles TIP
trials.results: CR in 32/46 (70%); 3 of 32 relapsed. 29 patients continuously disease-free at median follow-up 69 months — durable CR 63%; 2-yr PFS 65% (95% CI 51-79%)
trials.toxicity: Not quantified in the primary abstract
trials.reference: Kondagunta GV et al. JCO 2005;23:6549
highlights: Established TIP as a conventional-dose salvage regimen with a high durable CR rate in selected patients
Small single-arm phase 2 with deliberately favorable selection — testis primary AND prior CR — so results do not generalize to unselected or platinum-refractory relapse
trials.takeaway: Four cycles of TIP give a 63% durable complete response rate in relapsed testicular GCT selected for testis primary and prior complete response.

trials.name: MRC TE18 / EORTC 30942
trials.setting: adjuvant RT dose, stage I seminoma
trials.descriptor: 20 Gy in 10 fractions vs 30 Gy in 15 fractions of adjuvant para-aortic radiotherapy in stage I seminoma
trials.population: 625 men with stage I testicular seminoma post-orchiectomy, randomized 1995-1998
trials.arms: 20 Gy in 10 fractions over 2 weeks vs 30 Gy in 15 fractions over 3 weeks
trials.primary_endpoint: Relapse rate; powered to exclude an absolute 2-year difference of 3-4%
trials.results: Equivalent. Median follow-up 61 months: 11 relapses with 20 Gy vs 10 with 30 Gy, HR 1.11 (90% CI 0.54-2.28); absolute 2-yr difference 0.7% with an upper one-sided 90% bound of 2.9%, inside the margin
trials.toxicity: 30 Gy caused more moderate/severe lethargy at 4 weeks (20% vs 5%) and more inability to work (46% vs 28%); differences resolved by 12 weeks
trials.reference: Jones WG et al. JCO 2005;23:1200
highlights: Made 20 Gy the standard adjuvant radiotherapy dose for stage I seminoma
Follow-up was too short at publication to assess any difference in second malignancy
trials.takeaway: 20 Gy in 10 fractions matches 30 Gy for relapse control in stage I seminoma with less acute morbidity.

trials.name: MRC TE19 / EORTC 30982
trials.descriptor: single-dose carboplatin AUC7 vs adjuvant para-aortic radiotherapy after orchiectomy in stage I seminoma
trials.population: 1,477 men at 70 hospitals in 14 countries with stage I seminoma post-orchiectomy, randomized 3:5 (carboplatin:RT) 1996-2001
trials.arms: One injection of carboplatin, dose 7 × (GFR + 25) mg (n=573) vs radiotherapy, para-aortic strip or dog-leg field (n=904)
trials.primary_endpoint: Relapse-free rate; powered to exclude an absolute difference in 2-year relapse-free rate greater than 3%
trials.results: Non-inferior. Median follow-up 4 yr: 2-yr RFS 97.7% vs 96.7%; 3-yr 94.8% vs 95.9%; HR 1.28 (90% CI 0.85-1.93), P=0.32. Mature analysis at 6.5 yr (Oliver, JCO 2011;29:957, PMID 21282539): 5-yr RFR 94.7% vs 96.0% (HR 1.25); contralateral germ-cell tumors 2 vs 15 (HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.05-0.95, P=0.03)
trials.toxicity: Carboplatin caused less lethargy and less time off work than radiotherapy
trials.reference: Oliver RTD et al. Lancet 2005;366:293
highlights: Established single-dose carboplatin AUC7 as an alternative to adjuvant RT in stage I seminoma
The reduction in contralateral germ-cell tumors only reached significance in the 2011 mature analysis, not the 2005 primary report
Surveillance was not an arm here and is now the preferred default for most stage I seminoma
trials.takeaway: One dose of carboplatin AUC7 is non-inferior to adjuvant radiotherapy in stage I seminoma and produces fewer contralateral germ-cell tumors.

trials.name: TI-CE high-dose salvage
trials.descriptor: paclitaxel + ifosfamide followed by high-dose carboplatin + etoposide with autologous stem-cell rescue in relapsed or refractory germ cell tumor
trials.population: 107 patients with advanced GCT progressing after chemotherapy plus unfavorable features (extragonadal primary, incomplete response to first-line, or relapse after ifosfamide-cisplatin salvage). Testis 72, mediastinum 21, other 14; 79 platinum-refractory; 26 with ≥2 prior lines
trials.arms: Single arm: paclitaxel + ifosfamide ×2 then high-dose carboplatin + etoposide ×3 with stem-cell support
trials.primary_endpoint: Complete response rate, with a prognostic-factor analysis for DFS and OS
trials.results: CR in 54/107 (50%), plus 8 (8%) partial responses with negative markers. 5-yr DFS 47%, 5-yr OS 52% at median follow-up 61 months; no relapses after 2 years. 5 of 21 primary mediastinal NSGCT continuously disease-free. Adverse factors for DFS: mediastinal primary, ≥2 prior lines, hCG ≥1,000 U/L, lung metastases
trials.toxicity: Not quantified in the efficacy report; safety and dose-finding published separately (JCO 2007;25:85)
trials.reference: Feldman DR et al. JCO 2010;28:1706
highlights: Showed durable cure is achievable with high-dose chemotherapy even in platinum-refractory disease and mediastinal primaries
Single-institution phase 1/2 series, not randomized — the head-to-head question against conventional-dose TIP is what TIGER is testing
trials.takeaway: TI-CE high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue produces about 50% complete responses and 47% 5-year disease-free survival in poor-prognosis pretreated germ cell tumors.

trials.name: SWENOTECA — one cycle adjuvant BEP
trials.descriptor: one cycle of adjuvant BEP assigned by lymphovascular invasion in clinical stage I nonseminoma
trials.population: 517 Norwegian and Swedish men with CS I nonseminoma given one course of adjuvant BEP within a binational population-based risk-adapted program; LVI-positive patients were recommended 1×BEP, LVI-negative patients chose between 1×BEP and surveillance
trials.arms: No randomization — risk-adapted assignment: 1 cycle BEP vs surveillance
trials.primary_endpoint: Relapse rate — a management-program cohort analysis, not a powered endpoint
trials.results: Median follow-up 7.9 yr: 12 relapses among 517 patients; 5-yr relapse 3.2% LVI-positive and 1.6% LVI-negative; latest relapse at 3.3 yr; all relapses IGCCCG good prognosis; 5-yr cause-specific survival 100%. Earlier report (Tandstad, JCO 2009;27:2122, PMID 19307506) gives the surveillance comparison: relapse 41.7% LVI-positive and 13.2% LVI-negative
trials.toxicity: Described as low; no quantitative grade ≥3 rates reported
trials.reference: Tandstad T et al. Ann Oncol 2014;25:2167
highlights: Made one cycle of BEP — not two — the standard adjuvant option for LVI-positive CS I nonseminoma
Not a randomized trial: a prospective population-based risk-adapted program, so the comparison against surveillance is confounded by patient choice in the LVI-negative group
trials.takeaway: One cycle of adjuvant BEP cuts CS I nonseminoma relapse to about 3% in LVI-positive disease with 100% cause-specific survival, on population-based rather than randomized evidence.

trials.name: TIGER (Alliance A031102)
trials.descriptor: conventional-dose TIP vs high-dose TI-CE with autologous transplant as initial salvage for relapsed or refractory germ cell tumor
trials.population: Planned 420 males ≥14 years with seminoma or nonseminoma of any primary site, progressive after exactly one line of cisplatin-based chemotherapy, no prior high-dose chemotherapy; stratified by region and modified IPFSG risk
trials.arms: Conventional-dose TIP vs TI-CE (paclitaxel + ifosfamide then high-dose carboplatin + etoposide with stem-cell reinfusion)
trials.primary_endpoint: Overall survival, up to 36 months post-treatment
trials.results: No results reported. Active, not recruiting; opened August 2015; planned enrollment 420; completion listed as 2031. Do not quote survival figures for TIGER
trials.toxicity: Treatment-related mortality and CTCAE v4 adverse events are secondary endpoints; no data reported
trials.reference: Alliance A031102 (TIGER), ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02375204 — ongoing, no results published
highlights: The definitive randomized test of conventional-dose TIP against high-dose TI-CE at first salvage — the field's longest-standing unresolved question
International effort (Alliance with NCI, EORTC, ICR/CRUK, UNICANCER, Irish Clinical Oncology Research Group); no efficacy data exist yet
trials.takeaway: TIGER is the ongoing phase 3 comparing conventional-dose TIP with high-dose TI-CE at first salvage, with overall survival as the primary endpoint and no results yet.

trials.name: DECISION
trials.descriptor: sorafenib in RAI-refractory DTC
trials.population: Progressive, RAI-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer
trials.arms: Sorafenib vs placebo; crossover permitted
trials.results: PFS 10.8 vs 5.8 mo (HR 0.59, p<0.0001); ORR 12.2%; no OS benefit (crossover)
trials.toxicity: Hand-foot skin reaction, diarrhea, hypertension, fatigue
trials.reference: Brose MS et al. Lancet 2014;384:319-328
highlights: First TKI proven in RAI-refractory DTC; now generally second-choice to lenvatinib (weaker PFS + response).
trials.takeaway: Sorafenib — first TKI with PFS benefit in RAI-refractory DTC; now second to lenvatinib

trials.name: SELECT
trials.descriptor: lenvatinib in RAI-refractory DTC
trials.population: Progressive, radioiodine (RAI)-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (papillary/follicular, incl. Hürthle/poorly differentiated). Key eligibility: RAI-refractory by ≥1 of (a) no iodine uptake in a target lesion, (b) progression of an iodine-avid lesion within ~12 mo of RAI, (c) cumulative RAI >600 mCi; plus RECIST progression ≤13 months before entry, measurable disease, ≤1 prior VEGFR-targeted therapy, ECOG 0–2
trials.arms: Lenvatinib 24 mg/day vs placebo, randomized 2:1; crossover permitted at progression
trials.results: PFS 18.3 vs 3.6 mo (HR 0.21, p<0.001); ORR 64.8% vs 1.5% (4 complete responses); no significant OS difference (crossover-confounded)
trials.toxicity: Hypertension, diarrhea, fatigue, decreased appetite/weight, proteinuria
trials.reference: Schlumberger M et al. NEJM 2015;372:621-630
highlights: Lenvatinib is a preferred first-line TKI for RAI-refractory DTC (dramatic PFS + response rate).
The RECIST-progression-≤13-mo gate defines who warrants a TKI — asymptomatic, non-progressing disease doesn't qualify → active surveillance instead.
trials.takeaway: Lenvatinib — preferred 1L TKI for progressive RAI-refractory DTC (PFS 18.3 vs 3.6 mo)
